This study, titled "Exploring Influences of Pet-Related Social Media Content on Perceptions of Pet Adoption" by Ciphia May D. Molina, investigates how social media content affects the attitudes and intentions of pet owners and non-owners toward pet adoption in Metro Manila, Philippines.

The research addresses a significant gap in existing literature regarding the role of digital media in shaping animal welfare perceptions within the Philippine context. While traditional media has historically portrayed pets as companions, the rise of social media has introduced new dynamics through "pet influencers" and the "cute economy." The study is motivated by the ongoing animal welfare crisis in the Philippines, where millions of dogs and cats live on the streets and adoption rates from shelters remain low. The researcher seeks to understand if the increasing online presence of pets and the "Adopt, Don’t Shop" movement can effectively influence public behavior and perceptions.

The study is grounded in three theoretical frameworks: Uses and Gratification Theory (UGT), which explores why users seek out specific content to fulfill needs; Focus Theory of Normative Conduct (FTNC), which examines how social norms and approval influence behavior; and Cultivation Theory (CT), which suggests that repeated exposure to media narratives can shape an individual's perception of reality.

Using a descriptive-exploratory research design, the study collected data through an online survey administered to 154 respondents in Metro Manila. The sample included past, current, and prospective pet owners aged 18 to 43 who use Facebook, Instagram, or TikTok. The methodology focused on measuring several key constructs: social media exposure, motivations for pet ownership, perceived barriers to adoption, general perceptions of adoption, and adoption intent.

The findings reveal that social media plays a significant role in cultivating positive perceptions and reinforcing pet adoption as a cultural norm. Respondents frequently engage with pet-related content for emotional and informational gratification. The study found that motivational influence and normative influence are positively correlated with positive perceptions of pet adoption. Specifically, when social media content successfully triggers emotional motivation or signals social approval (through likes and comments), respondents hold more favorable views of adoption.

However, a distinction was found between perception and action. While frequent exposure to pet adoption-related content was linked to stronger adoption intent and higher motivational scores, the overall capacity of social media to drive actual adoption is limited. The results indicate that while social media can shape attitudes and reinforce the idea that adoption is a socially desirable practice, it does not directly alleviate the practical barriers respondents face. These barriers include financial costs, long-term responsibility, space restrictions, time constraints, and concerns regarding the behavior of shelter animals.

The study concludes that social media serves as a reinforcing mechanism rather than a determinative one. It is highly effective at cultivating positive attitudes and normalizing pet adoption through the "cute economy" and social cues, but it cannot overcome the significant practical and logistical hurdles that prevent individuals from following through with adoption.

The implications of this research are significant for various stakeholders. For animal welfare organizations and NGOs, the study suggests that while "cute" and emotional content is effective for engagement and building positive perceptions, campaigns must also address the practical barriers—such as cost and responsibility—to convert positive attitudes into actual adoption. For government agencies and policymakers, the findings highlight the potential of digital media as a tool for social change and animal welfare advocacy, suggesting that social media can be leveraged to promote responsible pet ownership and mitigate the community animal displacement crisis in urban areas. Finally, the study provides a foundation for future multimedia research into how digital content influences social justice and cultural norms in non-Western contexts.

title: Seoul to Soul: Perceived Influence of Korean TV Dramas in the Purchase Intentions of Korean Food
abstract:
Owing to the Hallyu wave's extensive global influence, this study investigates the extent of K-drama's influence on viewers' purchase intentions of Korean food. The study was conducted by surveying 110 college students in the National Capital Region in the Philippines. These students were selected as respondents because of their exposure to K-dramas and the availability of Korean food in the area. The results were analyzed using descriptive statistics and were evaluated using Elmo Lewis' AIDA Model. The success of the study depended on the use of various nominal extents, including consumption, preference, and purchase intention of Korean food.

Based on the evidence from the reviews and data collected, this study demonstrates the consumption of Korean food among viewers is positively influenced by K-dramas on Netflix. It argues that the likelihood of purchasing Korean food products is significantly correlated with how frequently people watch Korean dramas. Hence, this research makes a strong case for the influence of the Hallyu wave and the contribution of K-dramas to the promotion of Korean food consumption.

The research titled "Seoul to Soul: Perceived Influence of Korean TV Dramas in the Purchase Intentions of Korean Food" investigates how K-dramas on Netflix influence the food consumption, preferences, and purchase intentions of Generation Z in the Philippines. This study addresses a gap in existing research regarding the specific impact of K-dramas on the purchase intentions of digitally native consumers. Using a causal-explanatory quantitative approach, the researcher surveyed 110 college students in the National Capital Region of the Philippines, aged 18 to 25, who meet specific viewership and consumption criteria. The theoretical framework is anchored in the Theory of Planned Behavior and the AIDA Model.

The findings demonstrate a positive correlation between K-drama consumption and Korean food consumption. Data indicates that viewing K-dramas on Netflix positively influences the consumption and preference of Korean food among respondents, with a significant association between the frequency of watching dramas and the likelihood of purchasing Korean food products. Respondents reported that K-dramas help them appreciate Korean food and spark interest in the cuisine, often feeling guided by these shows or motivated by curiosity to try dishes seen on screen. The study concludes that the Hallyu wave, facilitated by streaming platforms, effectively moves viewers through the stages of the AIDA model. These findings offer insights for media companies and food industry stakeholders to develop targeted marketing strategies.

The research problem focuses on determining how K-dramas on Netflix affect the purchase intentions of Korean food among Filipino Generation Z, specifically regarding food choices, the speed of triggered purchase intentions, and which shows have the most significant impact. Data was gathered through a descriptive research survey from 110 college students in the National Capital Region of the Philippines, aged 18 to 25, who had eaten at least three types of Korean food and watched at least three K-dramas on Netflix. The theoretical framework was anchored in the Theory of Planned Behavior and the AIDA Model (Awareness, Interest, Desire, Action).

The findings demonstrate a positive correlation between K-drama consumption and Korean food consumption. The purchase intention scale revealed that many respondents feel guided by K-dramas when purchasing Korean food and are motivated by curiosity to try dishes seen on screen.

The study concludes that the Hallyu wave, facilitated by streaming platforms like Netflix, serves as a powerful tool for the promotion of Korean food. The consumption of K-dramas effectively moves viewers through the stages of the AIDA model, leading from awareness to the intention to purchase. The research titled "Seoul to Soul: Perceived Influence of Korean TV Dramas in the Purchase Intentions of Korean Food" by Alexis Diane Vivienne L. Candano investigates how the global phenomenon of the Hallyu wave, specifically through Korean dramas (K-dramas) on Netflix, influences the food consumption, preferences, and purchase intentions of Generation Z in the Philippines.

The study is situated within the context of the massive global rise of South Korean culture. The author notes that K-drama viewership increased by 370% during the COVID-19 pandemic as audiences turned to streaming services like Netflix. This media consumption has become a significant driver for the popularity of Korean cuisine globally. In the Philippines, the number of Korean restaurants grew by 81.2% as early as 2018, indicating a strong cultural integration. While previous research has explored the impact of K-dramas on fashion and general behavior, there is a gap in literature regarding the specific impact on the purchase intentions of Generation Z, a digitally native demographic.

The research problem focuses on determining how K-dramas on Netflix affect the purchase intentions of Korean food among Filipino Generation Z. Specifically, the study seeks to understand the extent to which these dramas influence food choices, how quickly purchase intentions are triggered, and which specific television shows have the most significant impact on these intentions.

To address these questions, the researcher employed a causal-explanatory research design using a quantitative approach. The study utilized a descriptive research survey to gather data from 110 college students residing in the National Capital Region of the Philippines. The respondents were selected based on specific criteria: they had to be between 18 and 25 years old, be current college students, have eaten at least three specific types of Korean food, and have watched at least three specific K-dramas on Netflix. The theoretical framework for the study was anchored in the Theory of Planned Behavior, which posits that behavioral intention is influenced by attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control, and the AIDA Model (Awareness, Interest, Desire, Action), which describes the stages a consumer goes through before making a purchase.

The findings of the study demonstrate a positive correlation between K-drama consumption and Korean food consumption. The data indicates that viewing K-dramas on Netflix positively influences the consumption and preference of Korean food among the respondents. Specifically, the results show a significant association between the frequency of watching Korean dramas and the likelihood of purchasing Korean food products. The survey data regarding food preference and consumption showed high levels of agreement among respondents, particularly regarding how K-dramas help them appreciate Korean food and spark interest in the cuisine. Similarly, the purchase intention scale revealed that many respondents feel guided by K-dramas when purchasing Korean food and are motivated by curiosity to try dishes seen on screen.

The study concludes that the Hallyu wave, facilitated by streaming platforms like Netflix, serves as a powerful tool for the promotion of Korean food. The consumption of K-dramas significantly impacts the food preferences and purchase intentions of Generation Z in the Philippines. The research confirms that the visual and emotional storytelling in K-dramas effectively moves viewers through the stages of the AIDA model, leading from mere awareness of a dish to the actual intention to purchase it.

The implications of this research are both academic and practical. Academically, the study contributes to the understanding of how mass media and digital streaming platforms influence the lifestyle and consumer behavior of Generation Z. It provides a foundation and methodology for future researchers to explore other sectors of the Hallyu wave or different demographic strata. Practically, the findings offer valuable insights for media companies and food industry stakeholders. Media companies can understand the extent to which their content influences consumer behavior, while food providers and marketers can use these insights to develop targeted marketing strategies that leverage the popularity of specific K-dramas and food items to reach the Generation Z market more effectively. The researcher recommends that future studies expand the scope to include different streaming platforms, different geographic areas, and a broader range of age groups.

title: Exploring Digital Artwork as NFT in Multimedia
abstract:
Non-fungible tokens or NFTs as popularly known have disrupted art as we know it. Thanks to blockchain technology, artists have been able to certify the authenticity of their works and take control of how they distribute their artwork. The same can be said with buyers and collectors of NFT art as they can now sell and resell their art for a fair sum of money. In order to break through to this new concept, one must first understand how cryptocurrencies and blockchain work, which are key parts of the NFT economy.

Incorporating my personal experience, this study aimed to determine the viability of NFTs as an art medium. I went through the full process of creating NFT art, from the actual artwork to the listing of digital artworks on OpenSea, one of the most popular NFT marketplaces. The study also observed the risks and benefits associated with selling NFT art and identified the issues and challenges that I have experienced in creating and listing NFT art.

The current model of creating, minting, and selling NFTs is still a work in progress. Hopefully, in the near future, the process would be more streamlined to entice more people to be engaged in the world of NFTs which according to famous NFT artist Gary Vaynerchuk a.k.a. GaryVee is here to stay.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
In the study "Exploring Digital Artwork as NFT in Multimedia," Angelo Joaquin C. Ascan investigates the viability of Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) for digital artists, weighing the potential to bypass traditional art market structures against the volatility of the cryptocurrency ecosystem. Using an autoethnographic research design, the author navigated the NFT lifecycle by creating a collection of pixelated trains and experimenting with the Ethereum and Polygon blockchains.

The findings reveal significant technical and economic hurdles. The author noted that while Polygon offers accessibility through the absence of fees, Ethereum involves high and fluctuating "gas fees" and a complicated minting process. External challenges include extreme cryptocurrency market volatility, which can impact sales value, and intense competition. Security concerns such as hacking, smart contract exploitation, online fraud, and "rug pulls" were also identified. Furthermore, promoting work on social media makes it difficult to prevent image theft.

Despite these risks, the study identifies opportunities for NFTs to level the playing field for diverse artists by allowing them to reach audiences without traditional galleries and build direct communities. The author concludes that the medium is currently in an experimental infancy stage where risks and benefits largely balance each other out. For the medium to become more viable, market stability and simplified minting processes are required. The study recommends that artists master blockchain management, focus on storytelling, and build strong social media presences.

two:
The study "Exploring Digital Artwork as NFT in Multimedia" by Angelo Joaquin C. Ascan investigates the viability of Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) as a medium for digital artists. The research seeks to determine to what extent NFT art serves as a viable medium for digital artists and identifies the specific opportunities and risks associated with this emerging technology.

The context of the research is rooted in the rise of blockchain technology and the subsequent explosion of the NFT market. While the technology allows artists to certify authenticity and control distribution through digital deeds of sale, the author notes that while the market has boomed globally, it remains in its infancy in the Philippines. The study is framed by the tension between the potential for artists to bypass traditional, often elitist, art market structures and the significant technical and economic volatility inherent in the cryptocurrency ecosystem.

The author employs an autoethnographic research design, utilizing personal experience to navigate the complexities of the NFT landscape. The methodology involves a hands-on approach to the entire lifecycle of an NFT: from the initial acquisition of cryptocurrency to the creation of digital art, the technical process of minting, and the subsequent promotion of the work. To supplement this personal journey, the author engaged with NFT-related communities on Discord to gather insights and tips from other enthusiasts.

The findings are detailed through the author's practical application of the NFT process. The process begins with the creation of a crypto wallet, specifically using Binance to purchase Ethereum (ETH) via Peer-to-Peer (P2P) trading, and transferring those funds to a MetaMask wallet. For the artwork, the author utilized Adobe Photoshop to create a collection of 14 pixelated, front-view trains. The minting process was explored on two different blockchains: the Ethereum mainnet, which involves high "gas fees" (transaction costs) and complex initialization, and the Polygon blockchain, which the author found to be more accessible due to the absence of gas fees. Promotion was attempted through Discord and Instagram, though the author noted the difficulty of preventing image theft on social media.

The results also highlight significant external factors, specifically the volatility of the cryptocurrency market. The author experienced an Ethereum crash shortly after listing their work, which significantly impacted the potential value and sales of the NFTs. Ultimately, the author was unable to secure a sale despite low pricing, illustrating the difficulty of entering the market.

The study identifies several critical issues and challenges. Technically, the process of buying cryptocurrency and minting NFTs is described as tedious and complicated for newcomers. Economically, high and fluctuating gas fees on the Ethereum blockchain act as a significant barrier to entry. Furthermore, the author notes intense competition, where even artists with social media followings may struggle to make sales. Security and privacy are also major concerns, including the risk of hacking, smart contract exploitation, online fraud, and "rug pulls," where developers abandon projects after collecting funds.

Despite these challenges, the study identifies significant opportunities. NFTs have the potential to level the playing field for artists, including women and people of color, by allowing them to reach audiences without the need for traditional galleries or curators. The technology can empower artists to build direct communities and potentially generate significant income through high-value sales.

In conclusion, the author finds that while NFTs are a revolutionary and disruptive force in the art world, they are still in an experimental infancy stage. The process of creating and selling NFTs is currently too complicated and expensive for many to navigate easily. The author concludes that for a digital artist, the risks and benefits currently balance each other out; neither side clearly outweighs the other. The viability of NFTs as a medium is heavily dependent on the stability of cryptocurrency markets and the simplification of the minting process.

The study offers several recommendations for aspiring NFT artists. It emphasizes that success requires more than just artistic skill; artists must become proficient in blockchain and cryptocurrency management. The author suggests that artists should focus on storytelling to give their collections unique value and should build a strong social media presence to engage with the community. Finally, the author recommends that artists consider collaborations and potentially building a dedicated team to handle marketing and social media, allowing the artist to focus on their creative practice.

title: Ambahan ni Ambo: A Digital Experience
abstract: Ambahan ni Ambo: A Digital Experience is an initiative to adapt one of Ed Maranan’s stories into a digital platform that focuses on the experiences of each character and how these would translate in real life and give inspiration to its users to follow their example. Two frameworks have been implemented - first is to simplify content by dividing the program into age-appropriate branches that each age-group can easily manage, while the second framework focuses more on the experiences of each of the characters in the story and how readers might see their own real-life experiences with them. This research follows a perspective similar to Design Thinking and revolves around Planning, Creation, and Evaluation.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
Rodeliza Joyce T. Dival’s research, "Ambahan ni Ambo: A Digital Experience," explores the preservation of indigenous Filipino culture through digital adaptation. The study focuses on transforming Ed Maranan’s children's book, *Ambahan ni Ambo*, into a mobile application to ensure the stories of the Mangyan people remain accessible to a youth population that increasingly favors digital formats over print.

The researcher employed a modified three-stage Design Thinking framework consisting of Plan, Create, and Evaluate. Because external user testing was not possible, the process relied on continuous self-assessment. During the creation phase, the Godot game engine and Sims 4 were used to develop visual assets. A key finding in the development process was the shift from an age-based organizational structure to an "Experience by Characters" framework. This revised approach organizes the app around specific character journeys, including experiences with Ambo, Jack and Anne, Pete and Tet, and a "Experience with You" segment that connects the narrative to real-world charitable actions. The final prototype features an interactive storybook, a Tagalog-English glossary, and information on supporting indigenous communities.

The study concludes that interactive storytelling is a vital tool for cultural preservation, allowing creators to align traditional narratives with modern consumption habits. The project demonstrates that mobile applications can serve as empathetic educational tools and provides a template for adapting Filipino folklore into immersive digital environments.

The research titled "Ambahan ni Ambo: A Digital Experience" by Rodeliza Joyce T. Dival addresses the challenge of preserving and sharing indigenous Filipino culture in an increasingly digital world. The study focuses on adapting Ed Maranan’s children's book, *Ambahan ni Ambo*, into a mobile application to ensure the stories and struggles of the Mangyan people remain accessible to modern audiences.

The problem identified by the author is the declining readership of print books among Filipino youth, who now spend significantly more time engaging with e-books and audiobooks than physical print. This shift threatens the visibility of indigenous stories, such as those of the Mangyans in Mindoro. As traditional print media loses its dominance, there is a risk that the cultural heritage, hardships, and strengths of indigenous groups will be overlooked by younger generations. The researcher seeks to bridge this gap by utilizing mobile technology to create an immersive digital experience that goes beyond simple reading.

The context of the study is rooted in the need for digital cultural heritage preservation. The author notes that while technology can lead to cultural uniformity, it also offers tools to enrich cultural variety if used to promote diverse narratives. The specific subject, *Ambahan ni Ambo*, tells the story of a family visiting a fictional town in Mindoro and interacting with Ambo, a Mangyan child skilled in "ambahan." The research is situated within the intersection of digital storytelling, cultural representation, and educational technology for children.

The methodology employed is an adaptation of the Design Thinking framework. Due to constraints preventing external user testing, the researcher implemented a modified three-stage cycle: Plan, Create, and Evaluate. This process was inspired by the researcher's personal experience with bullet journaling. The "Plan" stage involved prioritizing the core message of the book, the "Create" stage utilized the open-source Godot game engine and Sims 4 for visual assets, and the "Evaluate" stage involved continuous self-assessment to ensure the product met the goals of the research question.

The findings of the research are presented through the evolution of the application's framework. Initially, the researcher planned to divide the app by age group (children, students, and adults). However, upon evaluation, this was deemed too ambitious and unfocused. The researcher subsequently pivoted to a "Experience by Characters" framework. This revised approach organizes the digital experience around the specific journeys of the characters: "Experience with Ambo" (introducing Mangyan culture), "Experience with Jack and Anne" (an interactive retelling of a hiking adventure), "Experience with Pete and Tet" (focusing on adult perspectives and social solidarity), and "Experience with You" (connecting the story to real-world charitable actions). The final prototype includes features such as an interactive storybook, a Tagalog-English glossary, and information on how to support indigenous communities.

The researcher concludes that interactive storytelling is the natural evolution of print media. By adapting stories like *Ambahan ni Ambo* into digital formats, creators can keep cultural narratives alive in a way that aligns with modern consumption habits. The project demonstrates that even with limited resources, it is possible to create a meaningful digital experience that embodies the spirit of *bayanihan* (community spirit) and encourages cultural awareness.

title: The Dark Side of the Street: A Documentary Video About Women and Their Experience on Street Harassment
abstract:
Street harassment is defined as physical and verbal unwanted behaviors done by a stranger in the public sphere. At an early age, the filmmaker has experienced various acts of street harassment. When she was in grade school, he saw a drunk man trying to molest a girl in a jeepney. When she was in high school, a man flashed his genitals before her eyes on her way to school. The filmmaker also experiences catcalling almost everyday of her life but did not have the courage to tell anyone about her experiences because of the fear to be blamed.

The Dark Side of the Streets tells the story of random women who have street harassment experiences in Quezon City and Manila, two of the only cities in the country to pass an anti- catcalling bill or the Safe City for Women and Girls ordinance. Six (6) women were randomly interviewed by the Filmmaker and one woman who was picked based on the severity of her experiences.

The project was created to raise awareness among both men and women about the implications of street harassment and to expand its discourse. As of today, there is still no law about street harassment. Street Harassment falls under sexual harassment in our country, which are two different things. Anti-Sexual Harassment Act or R.A No. 7877, declares sexual harassment unlawful in employment, education or training environment only. Street harassment stands apart from this, because street harassment is usually done in public sphere by a stranger. A bill is yet to be signed by the President of the Philippines that would tackle the lack of protection for Women and Girls in the streets, Safe Streets and Public Spaces Act of 2017 (S.B No 1326) authored by Sen. Risa Hontiveros.

The filmmaker also aims those who have watched the video share their experiences. This why the filmmaker collaborated with a social media advocacy page, "Catcalled in the Philippines" that has 66,920 likes. The page has helped the video reached a lot of people. The Dark Side of the Street has reached 15,100 views, 291 shares, 302 likes, and 19 comments as of March 22, 2019. (https://www.facebook.com/catcalledinthePH/videos/290727768261895/)

title: Implementing and Maintaining a Completely Free Solution for Hosting a Small Organization's Content-Management System
abstract:
A website is a very powerful and efficient content management system (CMS) platform for storing, updating, and distributing information over the Network. It is a very ideal system that primarily focuses on automating the process of information dissemination, retrieval, and querying. Through a website, data and information that were previously written on manual files are already being encoded and stored in electronic format. These electronic files, which are patterned after the convention of a content management system, are now made more flexible compared to their manual counterparts. In view of this, a website therefore is very applicable in managing and disseminating information that are often subject to repetitive updates and queries such as those of a cooperative.

Providing a website for the TRC employees' cooperative however entails a sizable amount of investment that may go against the basic principle of frugality or financial conservation on their part. Moreover, it is also possible that not every officer and member of the cooperative are aware of the advantages of a website for their organization; considering the organization's long time practice of disseminating data and information among its members in the traditional manner.

Being mindful of these, it is therefore proposed through this project that a cost-free beta version CMS website be constructed and implemented for the TRC employees' cooperative. This beta version is envisioned to serve as an initial platform for future improvements by the time when the cooperative has already enough awareness and capacity to adapt and implement a full-scale CMS website in its operation.

Providing a cost-free CMS website for the TRC employees' cooperative therefore will not only enhance the management and dissemination of information among its members, but will also enhance the image of the cooperative itself; translating into a sense of pride among its members. These enhancements will later become part of the cooperative's intangible asset that increases members' confidence and patronage towards their organization. Moreover, this cost-free website project will not compromise the cooperative into any financial and miscellaneous obligations.

This manuscript includes all the details in creating and implementing a completely free solution for hosting the TRC employees' cooperative CMS website. This manuscript also contains a brief summary of the cooperative member's feedback regarding the website when it is already published online.

This challenge is often compounded by a lack of awareness among members and officers regarding the benefits of a digital presence.

To address these barriers, the author implemented a cost-free beta version of a CMS website. This project served as a foundational platform to test digital dissemination without financial strain, acting as a stepping stone toward a full-scale system. Beyond functional utility, the digital platform improves the cooperative's organizational image, fostering member pride and increasing confidence and patronage.

By utilizing free hosting, organizations can bypass high initial investment barriers while benefiting from automated information retrieval. This research demonstrates that digital transformation is possible without significant capital outlay if implementation is phased. title: Biomodd Do-It-Yourself Manual
abstract:
Biomodd is a collaborative art project that strives to generate a symbiotic relationship between electronic elements and ecological life. Each version of the project is predicated by the following themes: 1) fusion of technology and ecology, 2) re-use and recycling of
e-waste, 3) sculptural approach in case modding, 4) gaming, 5) collaboration and cocreation and 6) open-sourcing.

In 2009 a manual for building a version of Biomodd was created. However, its contents were mostly tips and warnings that the author has for Biomodd builders. It is more of a commentary than an objective manual. To fill this gap, the creation of a second version of
the Biomodd DIY Manual is needed. The second version of the manual improves upon its predecessor, by integrating multimedia content and including links to online resources. These will provide potential Biomodd makers sufficient information to properly address
challenges that the development team will be encountering, while building a version of Biomodd.

The first part of the manual tackles the themes behind Biomodd, the project's stages of development and solutions to issues and concerns that may arise during the build process. The second part is comprised of tips and suggestions that the author has for future
development teams. All of these were drawn from the author's personal experiences and observations, while working in various versions of the Philippine Biomodd.

This deficiency left makers without a definitive resource to navigate the project's complexities.

Biomodd operates at the intersection of technology and ecology, aiming to create a symbiotic relationship between electronic elements and ecological life. The project explores themes such as e-waste recycling, sculptural case modding, gaming, collaboration, and open-sourcing. Developed within the Bachelor of Arts in Multimedia Studies program at the University of the Philippines Open University, the project uses a methodology of improvement and expansion based on the author's personal experience with various Philippine Biomodd versions. The goal was to transform the previous commentary-style document into a robust, objective tool by integrating multimedia content and online resources.

The resulting manual is organized into two sections: the first outlines foundational themes and development stages to provide practical solutions to technical and conceptual issues, while the second offers tips for future development teams. The project concludes that a structured, multimedia-integrated manual is essential for executing complex, collaborative art projects, providing a template for codifying personal experience into objective resources for community-driven endeavors.

title: Technical Challenges with E-Learning Tolls: A Bachelor of Arts in Multimedia Studies Case Study
abstract:
Technology is a key instrument in distance learning. The University of the Philippines Open University (UPOU) has been utilizing distance learning tools to facilitate the learning process. The first batch of Bachelor of Arts in Multimedia Studies (BAMS) students, as well as the faculty, has been exploring these tools. Distance learning tools were used for effective communication, access to information, and different ways of fulfilling course requirements. However, both the students and faculty may have also experienced technical challenges.

This study aimed to assess the usage of the different distance learning tools (Moodle, Email, Yahoo! Messenger, Skype, Google Groups, WizIQ, Academiacs, and Facebook) by the senior students and faculty of the Bachelor of Arts in Multimedia Studies (BAMS) through Web surveys. From their usage of the distance learning tools, the technological challenges were determined.

The distance learning tools have been grouped according to the type of teaching and learning, and interaction. Type I refers to distance learning tools used for teaching and receiving (student-teacher interaction); Type II refers to facilitating and sharing (student-student interaction), and Type III refers to collaborative teaching and learning (collaborative interaction or student-teacher and student interaction).

The usage and technical challenges were classified into the access to distance learning online tools, functionality of the tools, interaction with the tools or effects of tools in the interaction of students and instructors, and attitude towards the tools.

Leongson’s study, "Technical Challenges with E-Learning Tools: A Bachelor of Arts in Multimedia Studies Case Study," investigates the role and difficulties of technology in distance education at the University of the Philippines Open University (UPOU). The research focuses on the first batch of Bachelor of Arts in Multimedia Studies (BAMS) students, faculty members, and tutors to determine how they utilize various distance learning tools and to identify specific technological challenges.

The study examined several platforms, including Moodle, Email, Yahoo! Messenger, Skype, Google Groups, WizIQ, Academiacs, and Facebook. These were categorized into Type I tools for student-teacher interaction, Type II tools for student-student interaction, and Type III tools for collaborative teaching and learning. The researcher assessed these tools based on access, functionality, interaction, and attitudes.

Findings indicate that senior BAMS students, faculty, and tutors generally experience easy access to tools, hardware, and adequate Internet connections. However, interaction emerged as a significant challenge for both students and faculty. Type III tools received the lowest figures across all measured categories. Specifically, senior BAMS students encountered significant problems interacting through Type III tools, which they reported has affected their academic performance. The study concludes that while infrastructure is sufficient, the primary challenge is the ability to interact effectively through collaborative tools. Addressing the efficacy of these digital environments is necessary to ensure technology supports the learning process.

The research focuses on the first batch of Bachelor of Arts in Multimedia Studies (BAMS) students, faculty members (FICs), and tutors to determine how they utilize various distance learning tools and to identify the specific technological challenges they encounter.

The study examined the usage of several platforms, including Moodle, Email, Yahoo! Messenger, Skype, Google Groups, WizIQ, Academiacs, and Facebook. These tools were categorized into three types: Type I tools for student-teacher interaction; Type II tools for student-student interaction; and Type III tools for collaborative teaching and learning involving both student-teacher and student-student interaction. The researcher assessed these tools based on four categories: access to tools, tool functionality, interaction with the tools, and attitudes toward the tools.

The findings indicate that senior BAMS students, faculty, and tutors generally experience easy access to all distance learning tools, hardware resources, and adequate Internet connections. However, despite this ease of access, interaction emerged as a significant challenging issue for both student and faculty respondents. When analyzing the three types of tools, Type III tools—intended for collaborative teaching and learning—received the lowest figures across all measured categories, including access, functionality, interaction, and attitude.

Specifically, senior BAMS students encountered significant problems when attempting to interact with their class through Type III tools. This difficulty in utilizing collaborative tools for communication has had a tangible impact on students, who reported that the failure to effectively use these tools for class communication has affected their academic performance.

In conclusion, while the fundamental infrastructure for distance learning, such as hardware and internet connectivity, appears sufficient for the BAMS cohort, the qualitative experience of using collaborative tools is problematic. The primary technical challenge is not the ability to access the tools, but the ability to interact effectively through them, particularly when the learning model requires collaborative engagement. The study suggests that for distance learning to be successful, especially in specialized programs like Multimedia Studies, attention must be given to the functionality and interactive efficacy of collaborative tools. Addressing the challenges associated with collaborative digital environments is necessary to ensure that technological tools support rather than hinder the learning process.

Type III tools are categorized as tools for collaborative teaching and learning, involving both collaborative interaction and combined student-teacher and student interaction. The study further classified the usage and technical challenges into four specific categories: access to online distance learning tools, the functionality of the tools, the interaction with the tools (or the effects of the tools on student-instructor interaction), and the attitude towards the tools.

The findings of the study indicate that senior BAMS students, faculty, and tutors generally experience easy access to all distance learning tools, hardware resources, and adequate Internet connections. Despite this ease of access, the study identified that interaction emerged as a significant challenging issue for both student and faculty respondents. When analyzing the three types of distance learning tools, the results showed that Type III tools—those intended for collaborative teaching and learning—received the lowest figures across all measured categories, including access, functionality, interaction, and attitude.

The results specifically highlight that senior BAMS students have encountered significant problems when attempting to interact with their class through Type III tools. This difficulty in utilizing collaborative tools for communication has had a tangible impact on the students, as they reported that the failure to effectively use these tools for class communication has affected their academic performance.

In conclusion, while the fundamental infrastructure for distance learning, such as hardware and internet connectivity, appears to be sufficient for the BAMS cohort, the qualitative experience of using collaborative tools is problematic. The study concludes that the primary technical challenge is not necessarily the ability to access the tools, but rather the ability to interact effectively through them, particularly when the learning model requires collaborative engagement.

The implications of these findings suggest that for distance learning to be successful, especially in specialized programs like Multimedia Studies, attention must be given to the functionality and interactive efficacy of collaborative tools. Because the inability to communicate effectively through Type III tools is linked to diminished academic performance, there is a clear need to address the specific challenges associated with collaborative digital environments to ensure that the technological tools support, rather than hinder, the learning process.

title: A Case Study on the Use of Multimedia in Resource Mobilization and Advocacy Work of Upland NGOs the Cases of the Kalahan Educational Foundation (KEF), Koalisyon Ng Katutubong Samahan Ng Pilipinas (KASAPI) and the Upland Marketing Foundation Incorporated (UMFI)
abstract:
Multimedia is known to facilitate communication with and heighten awareness of the target audiences. It obliterates distance and time as it provides accessibility and interactivity at any time and at any place, although several technical considerations have to be considered as well.

The study aims to contribute to the limited information on NGOs, particularly on the small to medium sized upland NGOs' usage of multimedia. This study looks at the multimedia capacity of these organizations, as well as the multimedia material, tools, and applications being utilized by upland NGOs in their activities particularly in fund sourcing and advocacy initiatives. It also attempts to determine the effectiveness of these multimedia applications according to the purpose by which these were adopted.

The study shows that there is a wide recognition of the immense capacity of multimedia in information dissemination in general and upland NGOs are currently utilizing various multimedia applications and tools in project implementation, resource mobilization and advocacy support. Effectiveness of these applications has also been rated to be very effective where desired output was completely achieved.

title: Installation of a Virtual Language Laboratory Integrated into a Learning Management System Using Open-Source Technolog
abstract:
This project is about the implementation of a virtual language laboratory integrated into the online learning management software using open source technology. A computer is installed with Ubuntu Server 11.10 64-bit as its operating system. To manage the server, Webmin version 1.570 is installed. Moodle version 2.2.2 is then installed as the learning management software. To integrate the language laboratory into the Moodle system, Red5 Media Server version 0.8.0 is then installed into the Ubuntu box. Inside Moodle, MoodLL version 2 plugin is then added which is then activated as one of the activity blocks in the management of courses.

This installation intends to replace the existing language laboratory systems which are using either the traditional setup of cassette tapes and reels; or the newer digital setup using computers in a single room.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
In the 2012 project "Installation of a Virtual Language Laboratory Integrated into a Learning Management System Using Open-Source Technology," Roy B. San Buenaventura addresses the limitations of traditional language learning configurations. The author identifies a need to move away from outdated technologies like cassette tapes and reels, as well as modern digital setups that require computers to be located within a single, physical room. Rooted in the evolution of educational technology and the shift toward online learning, the project seeks to provide a modern alternative to physical laboratory constraints by implementing a virtual language laboratory integrated into a Learning Management System (LMS) for remote or distributed instruction.

The methodology involves the technical installation and integration of several open-source software components. The system is built on an Ubuntu Server 11.10 64-bit operating system with Webmin version 1.570 for server management. The primary learning management software is Moodle version 2.2.2, with Red5 Media Server version 0.8.0 installed to achieve specific language laboratory functionality. The MoodLL version 2 plugin is then added to the Moodle system as an activity block for course management.

The findings demonstrate the successful installation and configuration of this integrated software stack. The author shows that combining these specific tools creates a functional virtual language laboratory that operates as an integrated activity block within Moodle. This transitions the laboratory experience from a localized, hardware-dependent setup to a software-driven, integrated digital environment.

The project concludes that open-source technology provides a viable pathway for implementing virtual language laboratories. By integrating the laboratory directly into an LMS, the limitations of physical space and traditional media are bypassed. This implementation shows that a virtualized approach can replace both outdated cassette-based systems and modern, yet physically constrained, single-room computer setups. The implications suggest that educational institutions can leverage open-source software to create flexible, scalable, and cost-effective language learning environments. By moving the laboratory into an LMS, the technology supports a distributed model of learning where students can access activities through a web-based system rather than being tethered to a specific physical room.

title: A Perception Survey on the Influence of Social Media on the Academic Performance of Public High School Senior Student in Tagum City
abstract:
Filipino students have become more and more active in using social media sites. Two of the most popular among these sites, Facebook and YouTube, are of the interest in this study. Several studies have been conducted to examine the impacts of the active use of social media to the academic performance of the students. However, these studies were not able to produce results from which generalizations as to the negative and positive effects of the use of these social media sites can be derived. In the absence of these generalizations, this study looked into the specific case of some groups of students in Tagum City.

As analyzing the influence is deemed to be a complicated measure, this study aimed to at least cover the preliminaries, that is, user perception. A perception survey was conducted. From which, students conferred that the effects of social media in their studies is mostly positive. It has been deduced as well that though social media pose negative impacts, it is mostly due to the lack of the sense of responsibility of the user, and the lack of accountability from the parents, guardians, and mentors. It is thus recommended, that as in all good things concerning the youth, moderation is the key and parental guidance is advised.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
Mervin Jay Z. Suaybaguio investigated how social media, specifically Facebook and YouTube, influences the academic performance of public high school senior students in Tagum City. Because determining direct influence is complex, the study focused on user perception, employing a perception survey to capture how students view the relationship between their social media activities and educational outcomes. This research addresses a gap in existing literature where previous studies have failed to produce consistent results or clear generalizations.

The findings indicate that students perceive the effects of social media on their studies to be mostly positive. While the study acknowledges potential negative impacts, it suggests these consequences are not inherent to the platforms themselves. Instead, negative outcomes are primarily attributed to a lack of responsibility on the part of the user and a lack of accountability from parents, guardians, and mentors.

The study concludes that the impact of social media depends heavily on user behavior and supervision. While social media can be a beneficial tool, its potential for harm is exacerbated by a lack of user responsibility and insufficient oversight from adults. The researcher recommends moderation as the key to ensuring social media remains a positive influence. Additionally, the study emphasizes that parents, guardians, and mentors must take an active role in holding students accountable for their social media usage to mitigate negative academic impacts.

title: Student's Usage of and Attitudes Toward Multimedia Resource in Selected Private High Schools in Davao City
abstract:
This study aimed to determine the students' usage of and attitudes toward multimedia resources in high school level in Davao City. The illustrative survey method was used to determine the students' usage of and attitudes toward multimedia resources in high school level specifically, the profile of the respondents, the students' attitudes toward multimedia resources in their library, the extent students are using multimedia resources, the extent to which multimedia resources contribute to the students' usage of their library, the factors that influence students' use or non-use of multimedia resources, the students' perception on the relevance of available multimedia resources and the relationship between the student's use of and attitudes toward these resources.

The questionnaire was the main instrument used in gathering data from the 173 students of secondary level in selected private schools in Davao City. Percentage, weighted mean and chi-square were the statistical tools used on this study.

Based on the findings, the respondents sometimes use the multimedia resources in their library. Most of them use multimedia resources less than once a week. They are undecided as to what extent do multimedia resources contribute to their usage of library as well as to the factors that influence their use or non-use of multimedia resources in their library. On the other hand, they agreed to moderate extent on the relevance of available multimedia resources in the library. Results also show that there is no relationship between the students' use of and attitudes toward multimedia resources in the library.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
Ricky Ibay Suicano’s study, "Student's Usage of and Attitudes Toward Multimedia Resource in Selected Private High Schools in Davao City," investigates how high school students in specific private institutions in Davao City interact with multimedia resources in their school libraries. The research aims to profile respondents, evaluate their attitudes toward these resources, examine the extent of their usage, and explore how these resources contribute to overall library usage, the factors influencing their use, and students' perceptions regarding the relevance of available materials.

Using an illustrative survey method, the researcher collected data from 173 secondary level students. Data analysis involved percentage, weighted mean, and the chi-square test to determine if a statistically significant relationship existed between usage and attitudes. Findings reveal that respondents "sometimes" use multimedia resources, with most utilizing them less than once a week. Students remained undecided regarding the extent to which these resources contribute to library usage and the specific factors influencing their decision to use them. However, students expressed a positive view regarding utility, agreeing to a moderate extent that the resources are relevant. The chi-square test showed no relationship between usage and attitudes, suggesting that engagement levels do not dictate opinions of the technology.

The study concludes that while resources are perceived as relevant, they are not used frequently, indicating a gap between availability and academic integration. Because students are undecided about influencing factors, schools should investigate barriers like accessibility or training. Educators and librarians may need to develop structured ways to integrate these resources into assignments to encourage consistent use.

The research aims to profile respondents, evaluate their attitudes toward these resources, and examine the extent of their usage. Additionally, the study explores the degree to which these resources contribute to overall library usage, the factors influencing the decision to use them, and students' perceptions regarding the relevance of available multimedia materials.

The researcher employed an illustrative survey method, collecting data from 173 secondary level students through a questionnaire. To analyze the data, the study utilized percentage, weighted mean, and the chi-square test to determine if a statistically significant relationship existed between the students' usage of multimedia resources and their attitudes toward them.

The findings reveal that respondents "sometimes" use the multimedia resources, with most students utilizing them less than once a week. Regarding the impact of these resources, students remained undecided as to the extent to which they contribute to overall library usage. Similarly, students were undecided regarding the specific factors that influence their decision to use or not use the provided multimedia resources. Despite this uncertainty, students expressed a positive view regarding utility, agreeing to a moderate extent that the available multimedia resources are relevant. Most significantly, the chi-square test showed no relationship between the students' use of multimedia resources and their attitudes toward them, suggesting that a student's level of engagement does not necessarily dictate their opinion of the technology.

The study concludes that while multimedia resources are perceived as relevant, they are not being utilized frequently. This low frequency suggests a gap between resource availability and integration into academic routines. The lack of a relationship between usage and attitude implies that non-use is not directly tied to a negative attitude toward the technology.

The implications suggest that providing resources is insufficient to ensure effective use. Because students are undecided about influencing factors, schools need to investigate barriers to usage, such as accessibility, training, or curriculum alignment. Since students perceive the resources as relevant despite low usage, educators and librarians may need to develop structured ways to integrate these resources into classroom assignments or library instruction to move students toward more consistent use.

Regarding the frequency of use, the respondents reported that they "sometimes" use the multimedia resources available in their libraries. More specifically, the data indicates that most students utilize these resources less than once a week. When asked about the impact of these resources, the students expressed uncertainty, remaining undecided as to the extent to which multimedia resources contribute to their overall usage of the library. Similarly, the students were undecided regarding the specific factors that influence their decision to either use or not use the multimedia resources provided in their libraries.

Despite this uncertainty regarding usage and influencing factors, the students did express a positive view regarding the utility of the materials, agreeing to a moderate extent that the available multimedia resources in the library are relevant. However, the most significant statistical finding pertains to the correlation between usage and attitude. The results show that there is no relationship between the students' use of multimedia resources in the library and their attitudes toward these resources. This suggests that a student's level of engagement with the technology does not necessarily dictate their opinion of it, or vice versa.

Based on these findings, the study concludes that while multimedia resources are perceived as relevant by high school students in Davao City, they are not being utilized frequently. The low frequency of use—often less than once a week—suggests a gap between the availability of these resources and their actual integration into the students' academic routines. Furthermore, the lack of a relationship between usage and attitude implies that even students who do not use the resources frequently may still view them as relevant, or that the reasons for non-use are not directly tied to a negative attitude toward the technology itself.

The implications of this study are significant for school administrators, librarians, and educators in private high schools. The data suggests that simply providing multimedia resources may not be sufficient to ensure their effective use. Because students are undecided about the factors influencing their use and the extent to which these resources aid their library engagement, there is a clear need for schools to investigate the barriers to usage. This could involve assessing whether the resources are easily accessible, whether students have been adequately trained to use them, or whether the content provided is aligned with their specific curriculum needs.

Furthermore, the finding that students perceive the resources as relevant despite low usage suggests that the problem may lie in the "how" and "when" of usage rather than the "what." Educators and librarians might need to develop more structured ways to integrate multimedia resources into classroom assignments or library instruction to move students from "sometimes" using the resources to using them more consistently. Ultimately, the study highlights the necessity for a more targeted approach to multimedia resource management to ensure that these technological investments contribute meaningfully to the students' academic experiences and library engagement.

title: The Development of a Web-based Membership Tracking Information System for a Karate Martial Arts School in the Philippines
abstract:
A karate martial arts school that has many branches in the Philippines faced challenges in managing its growing membership base and keeping track of important information, which resulted in inefficiencies, errors, and decreased member satisfaction. To address these issues, a karate martial arts school in the Philippines needed an effective membership tracking information system to automate membership management, improve communication, streamline data management, and enhance member engagement. 

The methodology used to prove the successful implementation of the proposed information system was to utilize the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Socio- Technical Systems Theory (STS), and the Information Processing Theory (IPT). The Web-Based Membership Tracking Information System (WBMTIS) was developed to provide better accessibility, present up-to-date information on karate practitioners, and create a customized platform tailored to a karate martial arts school aimed at utilizing open-source technologies. Throughout the development process of WBMTIS, frameworks such as Scrum and ADDIE, were used with modifications to these frameworks in order to aid in the successful implementation and acceptance of the system based on information system theories included in the research. The research helped in identifying the unique needs of the karate martial arts school and tailor-fitted the system according to the stakeholders wants and needs. 

The overall result of implementing the WBMTIS affirmed the system’s functional effectiveness and high level of user acceptance due to a yielded mean score of 91.25 based on the usability testing conducted using the System Usability Scale (SUS), therefore classifying the WBMTIS under the usability category of “Excellent”. 

The information system theories used in the study were grounded in TAM, STS, and IPT, which assisted in the system’s design, human-computer interaction, and adoption strategy. These frameworks supported the evaluation of the system’s ease of use, social and organizational integration, and cognitive efficiency in information processing. The study concludes that the system successfully met its objectives and offers a practical model for digital transformation within martial arts organizations. Recommendations for future enhancement include the integration of an online payment gateway, push notifications, calendar synchronization, an internal messaging module such as chat, an advanced analytics dashboard, and an e-learning component to extend instructional reach and system functionality.

The thesis titled "The Development of a Web-based Membership Tracking Information System for a Karate Martial Arts School in the Philippines" by Oliver Lester L. Berris addresses the operational challenges faced by a karate martial arts school with multiple branches in the Philippines. The study focuses on the development and implementation of a Web-Based Membership Tracking Information System (WBMTIS) to modernize organizational management.

**Problem**
The primary problem identified is the lack of a centralized database to manage a growing membership base. The school relied on manual coordination among various chapters, coaches, and officials, which led to inaccurate and incomplete data. This inefficiency caused delays and errors in organizing events and verifying participant eligibility. Furthermore, the absence of a reliable system made it difficult to comply with health protocols and government regulations during COVID-19 restrictions. These issues resulted in decreased member satisfaction, communication gaps, and potential member attrition due to members feeling unsupported in their martial arts journey.

**Context**
The study is situated within the context of the growing popularity of karate in the Philippines and the specific needs of martial arts organizations to manage member progress and event participation. The researcher notes that for large organizations, such as Kyokushin, which has millions of members worldwide, maintaining data integrity and seamless communication is essential. The project was developed as part of a Master of Information Systems program at the University of the Philippines Open University.

**Method**
The researcher employed a combination of software development and instructional design frameworks. The development process utilized the Rapid Application Development (RAD) model and the ADDIE (Analyze, Design, Develop, Implement, and Evaluate) model. To ensure iterative progress and stakeholder alignment, the Scrum framework was integrated into the development cycles. 

The theoretical foundation of the project was built upon three key information system theories: the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to ensure perceived usefulness and ease of use; Socio-Technical Systems Theory (STS) to balance technical requirements with the social and organizational workflows of the dojo; and Information Processing Theory (IPT) to optimize how information is captured, stored, and retrieved. The system was built using AWS Cloud for deployment, PHP and MySQL with the Laravel Framework for the backend, and Flutter for the mobile application. Notably, the system incorporates QR codes for digital identification and blockchain technology to ensure the authenticity and integrity of student records.

**Findings**
The implementation of the WBMTIS yielded highly positive results. Usability testing conducted via the System Usability Scale (SUS) resulted in a mean score of 91.25, which classifies the system's usability as "Excellent." The system successfully provided specialized functionalities for three user roles: Students/Guardians, Teachers, and System Administrators. 

Key features identified in the findings include the ability for teachers to track student ranks and karate journeys, the ability for students to view their progress and register for events via mobile or web, and the ability for administrators to manage user roles and generate reports. The system also successfully implemented offline support through a local database and the repository design pattern, ensuring functionality even without internet connectivity. The use of QR codes and blockchain verification provided a level of security and convenience not found in existing commercial alternatives.

**Conclusions**
The study concludes that the WBMTIS successfully met its objectives of automating membership management, improving communication, and streamlining data management. The system provides a practical and effective model for digital transformation within martial arts organizations. By integrating social, technical, and cognitive theories, the researcher was able to create a system that is not only technically robust but also highly acceptable to its intended users. The research demonstrates that customized, open-source-based solutions can effectively address the specific logistical and administrative needs of niche organizations like martial arts schools.

**Implications**
The implications of this research suggest that digital transformation through tailored information systems can significantly enhance organizational performance and member engagement in sports organizations. The study provides a roadmap for other member-based organizations to move away from manual processes toward automated, secure, and accessible digital platforms. 

For the karate school, the system offers a foundation for better decision-making through data analytics and improved event coordination. For the broader field of information systems, the study highlights the value of combining multiple theoretical frameworks (TAM, STS, and IPT) to ensure the successful adoption of new technologies in specialized environments. The researcher recommends several future enhancements to further increase the system's utility, including the integration of an online payment gateway, push notifications, calendar synchronization, an internal messaging module, an advanced analytics dashboard, and an e-learning component to support remote instruction.

title: Development of Out-of-school Youth Monitoring and Evaluation System (OSYMES) for USAID Opportunity 2.0 Program
abstract:
The USAID-funded Opportunity 2.0 (O2) program supports the Philippine education system in providing second-chance opportunities for 180,000 out-of-school youth (OSY) to pursue employment, entrepreneurship, or further education. A crucial element of the program is the monitoring and evaluation (M&E) system, which ensures effective program implementation and resource utilization. However, the current M&E system, M&E Insight, developed by the Education Development Center (EDC) in the US, has faced challenges in meeting the evolving data and reporting needs of the program. The local M&E team, with limited expertise in the system’s underlying programming language (C#), and the complex process of change management with the US office, struggled to address these issues promptly. As a result, the team resorted to manual data entry and consolidation through Youth Trackers, which presented challenges in data validation, deduplication, and report generation.

To address these challenges, the Out-of-School Youth Management and Evaluation System (OSYMES) was created to improve data collection, reduce reliance on manual processes, and ensure more accurate and timely reporting. Built with PHP, OSYMES offers a more flexible and user-friendly interface, enabling the local M&E team to quickly adapt to evolving program requirements. The system also incorporates automated deduplication and multithreading to enhance processing efficiency, while leveraging cloud-based services through AWS Lambda and S3 to optimize resource management. Additionally, the inclusion of a reporting dashboard provides stakeholders with real-time reports to support decision-making. By addressing the limitations of M&E Insight, OSYMES represents a significant step forward in enhancing data management and improving the overall effectiveness of the O2 program's efforts to support out-of-school youth in the Philippines.

title: Candijay Fishery And Agricultural Household Registration Management And Decision Support System (C-Farms)
abstract: This project aims to develop the Candijay Fishery and Agricultural household Registration and Management System (C-FARMS), a decision support system to assist the Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO) in managing its programs for registered farming and fisheries households in the municipality of Candijay. The system focuses on record-keeping and program beneficiary selection to aid the MAO in fulfilling its mandate to promote agriculture and fisheries development among constituents. The project followed the Rapid Application Development model and resulted in a threetiered web application using ReactJS, NodeJS, GraphQL API, and PostgreSQL. The Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) was used to validate and verify the system, including administering online surveys and conducting end-to-end testing with Cypress. Results showed that users found the system to be acceptable and all test cases passed. The system is ready for deployment to the MAO, but maintenance plans should be implemented to ensure continued effectiveness.

title: Nextway: Open Source Last Mile Delivery System For MSMEs
abstract:
As the industry of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in the Philippines grew over the years and contributed much to the economy, opportunities and challenges to the last mile delivery came along with the demand. No business-to-customer (B2C) transactions are complete without product fulfillment. Last mile delivery is the last leg of moving goods from hubs to customers in the supply chain. Such services existed in the Philippines as third-party logistics (3PL) solutions. While MSMEs may simply tap into these 3PLs, this study has proposed and demonstrated that open-source solutions could integrate into their existing logistics and delivery teams.

The Nextway project has developed cost-effective and reliable solutions to aid small companies, drivers, and customers. Considering the economic aspect of MSMEs, a significant capital expense was found unnecessary for adopting their last mile delivery solution. Various literature has proven that a last mile delivery system is a considerable asset and investment a business in the scale of MSME could acquire. In particular, the pilot implementation of this study for the client has solved the challenges of digitization of data, receiving orders and tracking physical packages into warehouses, designation of delivery personnel, tracking of the loaded packages into the vehicle, and providing meaningful information to drivers. The Nextway backend has utilized the open-source Odoo community edition as a provider of the enterprise resource planning (ERP) aspect of the business.

Aldrin A. Navarro's thesis, "Nextway: Open Source Last Mile Delivery System for MSMEs," addresses the logistical challenges faced by micro, small, and medium enterprises in the Philippines. Using a case study of a food-and-beverage manufacturer in Cebu, the research identifies how manual, paper-based systems lead to inaccurate reporting, lack of fleet transparency, and an inability to align production with customer demand. These inefficiencies often result in stock mismatches and unaccounted profits.

title: Unified Barangay E-Services System with Augmented Analytics
abstract:
The Unified Barangay E-Services System is a platform designed to provide online services to the community of Barangay Batasan Hills. The system was developed with the goal of improving the efficiency and accessibility of government services for the community. The development process involved creating a userfriendly website, integrating various government services, and training staff to support the platform's use. The key feature of the system is the use of augmented analytics to analyze and present data generated by the platform. This technology allows the government to make data-driven decisions about how to improve and expand the services offered through the platform. For example, it can identify which services are most frequently used by residents or identify areas where there may
be a need for additional resources or support. Additionally, it can provide personalized recommendations to residents based on their usage history, improving their experience with the platform. The system received a very good interpretation from a survey of residents using it and reduced the time and effort required to access government services. The system can be a model for other communities looking to improve the delivery of government services to their residents and it is recommended that other communities implement similar
platforms and incorporate augmented analytics to improve the accessibility and efficiency of government services. Furthermore, it is recommended that the Unified Barangay E-Services System continue to be updated and maintained to ensure its effectiveness.

Residents faced time-consuming procedures and unaddressed social media inquiries, while barangay leaders lacked data-driven insights for strategic programming and budgeting.

To resolve these issues, the researcher developed the Unified Barangay E-Services System with Augmented Analytics, a progressive web application built using WordPress and PHP. The system centralizes services through online document processing, an integrated booking system, and communication tools like Gmail and Google Calendar. A chatbot was included to manage frequently asked questions. A key feature is the integration of augmented analytics, which uses a one-time registration process and unique resident IDs to automate data profiling, enabling officials to analyze trends for informed decision-making.

The system was evaluated through user, security, and performance testing based on ISO 25010 standards. Results from 384 respondents yielded an overall weighted mean of 4.26, indicating a "Very Good" rating across all criteria. Portability received the highest mean score (4.29), while compatibility received the lowest (4.23). Performance testing showed a First Contentful Paint of 2.27 seconds and a Time to Interactive of 4.75 seconds. The study concludes the system successfully streamlined operations and provides a model for proactive, data-driven local governance.
