The Unified Barangay E-Services System with Augmented Analytics, authored by Jerico G. Pastoril, addresses the operational challenges faced by Barangay Batasan Hills in Quezon City. With a population of 166,572, the barangay provides a wide array of services, including Barangay Identification Cards, clearances, indigency certifications, and disaster risk management. However, the study identifies that the existing manual processes and outdated digital presence created significant inefficiencies.

The problem identified in the study centers on the limitations of manual operations and a non-functional website that served only as a bulletin board. Residents faced time-consuming processes, inaccurate or inconsistent data, delayed service delivery, and difficulties in data archiving and retrieval. Furthermore, the lack of a centralized information hub meant residents often had to visit the barangay physically because social media inquiries frequently went unanswered. The absence of a booking system and digital data capturing meant that resident details were not validated, and payments were often recorded in manual logbooks or simple Excel files, which lacked security and control. Additionally, barangay leaders lacked a data-driven basis for formulating strategic programs and allocating budgets, often relying on anecdotal evidence rather than substantial data.

To address these issues, the researcher developed a progressive web application designed to centralize and automate barangay services. The method employed for this project was based on the Technology-Organization-Environment (TEO) framework, which considers how technological, organizational, and environmental contexts influence the adoption of innovation. The system was developed using WordPress as a Content Management System (CMS) and PHP as the primary programming language. The technical architecture includes a MySQL database layer for data management and a client layer accessible via web browsers on various operating systems.

The system's features include online service processing for documents like clearances and IDs, an online booking system integrated with StartBooking, and communication tools such as Gmail and Google Calendar for reminders. A chatbot was implemented to handle frequently asked questions and provide a "Live Help" option to connect residents with staff for urgent matters. A critical component of the method is the integration of augmented analytics. This feature uses a one-time registration process and unique resident IDs to automate data profiling, allowing officials to analyze trends, compare service usage, and generate insights to support data-driven decision-making.

The project underwent rigorous assessment through user testing, security testing, and performance testing. Security was evaluated using ImmuniWeb, and performance was measured using SpeedLab, which analyzed metrics such as First Contentful Paint (FCP) and Time to Interactive (TTI). The system's acceptability was evaluated based on ISO 25010 standards, including functional suitability, performance efficiency, compatibility, usability, reliability, security, portability, and maintainability.

The findings indicate that the system was highly successful. Survey results from 384 respondents (including 20 barangay employees and 364 residents) showed a "Very Good" verbal interpretation across all ISO 25010 criteria. The highest mean score was achieved in portability (4.29), while the lowest, though still rated "Very Good," was in compatibility (4.23). The overall weighted mean was 4.26, confirming that the system is a highly acceptable and effective alternative to manual processes. Performance testing showed a First Contentful Paint of 2.27 seconds and a Time to Interactive of 4.75 seconds, indicating efficient loading and responsiveness.

In conclusion, the study concludes that the manual system in Barangay Batasan Hills caused significant delays and data inconsistencies. The implementation of the Unified Barangay E-Services System successfully addressed these problems by providing a streamlined, digital platform. The evaluation confirms that the system meets the necessary quality standards for functional suitability, usability, and reliability, making it a viable tool for community service delivery.

The implications of this research suggest that the system can serve as a model for other local government units seeking to modernize their operations. By incorporating augmented analytics, barangays can move from reactive management to proactive, data-driven governance. The study recommends that the system be continuously updated and maintained to ensure effectiveness. Future work should focus on expanding the range of e-services, integrating the platform with other government databases, adding mobile access and online payment capabilities, and further enhancing security measures and user interface responsiveness.

title: Jeepney Queuing and Tracking System (JEEPQTS)
abstract:
The lives of every individual around the world have started to shift to adapt to a digital environment. This need was further accelerated with the arrival of COVID 19 pandemic and have put a lot of pressure on different entities to rapidly shift their existing systems to a digital scheme. A lot were able to adjust quickly, specially those companies with dedicated Information Technology (IT) team in their organization. However, many other services need upgrading as well. One of these is the Transportation service.

An example of such are the Uber, Grab and Ankas services that were known to be effective in tracking and booking transportation services for Cabs, Cars, Motorcycles, etc. However, not everyone can afford to use these services as these transportation means are very expensive. The known public transportation in the Philippines are Jeepneys and yet, very little service providers resolve issues on Jeepney queuing. Different areas in the Philippines, have trouble in waiting for Jeepneys because they are either stuck on traffic, or parked because there’s no way for drivers to know the demand for their services real time.

Thus, this project aims to provide an effective data gathering application to capture data needed both by jeepney drivers and passengers. It aims to provide real time view of the demand and available supply of jeepney transporation services across different areas at a cheaper cost. Both passengers and drivers do not need to spend money on mobile data, they can just use SMS messaging to upload and view information using the JeepQTS system.

title: Asset Management System for Database Management Systems
abstract:
Databases hold critical data that is valuable for both consumers and businesses. As a business expands, the reliance on a healthy and working database becomes imperative for its business operations. Hence, it is essential to maintain and monitor relational databases as they are the backbone for business longevity and growth.

This project aims to retrofit the concept of an inventory management system to database systems. The scope and result of this project are to (1) host the system in a webserver, (2) capability to connect to any of the popular relational database systems (SQL Server, Postgres, Oracle, or MySQL), (3) monitor a database’s availability and capacity, and (4) aggregate and display historical data into graphs and tables.

The resulting system satisfied the requirements mentioned above. The system is hosted on AWS EC2 Windows 2019. Through the web interface, you can monitor and analyze historical data. With the pyodbc library, it can Extract-Transform-Load data from the target database and then load it to the local database. This method is possible with the help of SQLs native for each target database.

Even though numerous database monitoring tools are on the market, this system is a low-cost alternative. Also, the system is still in its infancy. It suffered from project ailments that hindered the progress of this project, such as underestimating tasks, shortage of time, and delayed testing. In essence, the system still satisfies the benchmarks for testing, and it is subjected to future improvements.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
In the thesis "Asset Management System for Database Management Systems," Rey Lawrence L. Torrecampo addresses the challenges businesses face in monitoring and auditing relational database management systems (RDBMS) as data scales. The author identifies a need for a low-cost, web-based, and centralized alternative to expensive monitoring tools. To meet this need, the author developed "DB-IMS," a system designed to monitor database health, specifically focusing on availability and capacity.

Developed using a Waterfall methodology, DB-IMS utilizes a client-server model where a web interface is hosted on an AWS EC2 Windows 2019 server. The system employs an Extract-Transform-Load (ETL) process using Python scripts and the `pyodbc` library to extract data from MS SQL Server, MySQL, Postgres, and Oracle databases. This data is stored in a local MySQL database. The web interface was built using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and PHP.

The findings demonstrate that DB-IMS successfully meets its primary objectives by connecting to major relational database platforms and displaying historical data through graphs and tables. While the ETL pipeline allows for non-intrusive monitoring, technical challenges were noted regarding `pyodbc` driver requirements and difficulties with legacy database stored procedures. Security testing identified vulnerabilities such as Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and the absence of Anti-CSRF tokens. The author concludes that a low-cost asset management system is viable and suggests future improvements include enhanced security, mobile compatibility, and Machine Learning for predictive analytics.

This process uses Python scripts and the `pyodbc` library to connect to various target databases—including MS SQL Server, MySQL, Postgres, and Oracle—to extract data using native SQL. The web interface was built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with PHP managing server-side scripting and sessions.

The development process included several phases: development, integration testing, staging environment testing, and security testing. The findings demonstrate that DB-IMS successfully met its primary objectives. The implemented ETL pipeline allows for non-intrusive monitoring. However, technical challenges were noted, including the `pyodbc` library's reliance on pre-installed Windows ODBC drivers, difficulties executing stored procedures on legacy database versions, and specific driver sensitivity issues when connecting to Oracle databases.

The project concludes that a functional, low-cost database asset management system is viable. Although the author noted the project was in its "infancy" and faced challenges regarding task complexity and time constraints, the integration of Python, PHP, JavaScript, and SQL successfully automated data extraction and display. The thesis titled "Asset Management System for Database Management Systems" by Rey Lawrence L. Torrecampo addresses the critical need for businesses to monitor and audit their relational database management systems (RDBMS). As organizations expand, the scale of their databases grows, making it increasingly difficult to track availability, capacity, and health. The author identifies a gap in the market for a low-cost, web-based, and centralized alternative to expensive, heavy-duty monitoring tools.

The problem domain centers on the difficulty companies face in tracking and auditing their most critical assets: their databases. The research seeks to repurpose the concept of an inventory management system to serve as a database monitoring tool. Specifically, the project aims to answer how an existing inventory system can be transformed to monitor RDBMS, what best practices are required for this transformation, and which RDBMS properties are most relevant for auditing.

To address these problems, the author developed "DB-IMS," a system designed to monitor database availability and capacity. The project utilized a Waterfall methodology, which was chosen due to the linear nature of the requirements and the relatively small scale of the project. The system architecture follows a client-server model where the user interacts with a web interface hosted on an AWS EC2 Windows 2019 server. The system uses a local MySQL database to store aggregated data, which is populated via an Extract-Transform-Load (ETL) process. This process is facilitated by Python scripts using the `pyodbc` library, which connect to various target databases—including MS SQL Server, MySQL, Postgres, and Oracle—to extract data using native SQL. The web interface was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with PHP serving as the server-side scripting language to manage sessions and interact with the local database.

The methodology included several phases: development, integration testing, staging environment testing, and security testing. The author utilized a variety of technologies, including XAMPP for local web services and GitHub for version control. During the testing phase, the author conducted functional testing, white-box testing, and UI testing. Integration testing was performed in two attempts; the first attempt failed due to numerous bugs, but the second attempt, following bug fixes, was successful. Staging environment testing was conducted on the AWS-hosted server using a variety of database versions to ensure compatibility. Security testing was performed using the ZAP application, which identified several vulnerabilities, such as Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), the absence of Anti-CSRF tokens, and information disclosure.

The findings of the project demonstrate that the DB-IMS system successfully met its primary objectives. The system is capable of hosting on a web server, connecting to major relational database platforms, monitoring availability and capacity, and displaying historical data through graphs and tables. The author successfully implemented an ETL pipeline that allows for non-intrusive monitoring of target databases. However, the project also revealed significant technical challenges. The author noted that the `pyodbc` library's reliance on pre-installed Windows ODBC drivers can be problematic. Furthermore, the implementation faced difficulties with legacy database versions; for example, certain stored procedures designed for newer versions of SQL Server or Postgres failed to execute on older versions. The author also noted that connecting to Oracle databases presented unique challenges regarding driver sensitivity and local database connections.

In conclusion, the project successfully developed a functional, low-cost database asset management system that fulfills the core requirements of monitoring and auditing RDBMS. While the system is described as being in its "infancy" and faced challenges such as underestimating task complexity and time constraints, it satisfied the benchmarks for testing. The author concludes that the integration of multiple technologies—Python, PHP, JavaScript, and SQL—allowed for a harmonious automation of data extraction and display, providing a centralized platform for database administrators to monitor their environments on the go.

The implications of this work suggest that a lightweight, open-source approach to database monitoring is viable for organizations seeking cost-effective solutions. For future development, the author recommends addressing the identified security vulnerabilities, improving the user interface, and expanding functionality to include mobile compatibility. Additionally, the author proposes the future integration of Machine Learning (which was not implemented in this version due to time and data constraints) to enable automated performance tuning and more advanced predictive analytics.

title: CS: Computer Store Point of Sale and Inventory Management System with RFID Technology using Flutter Framework
abstract:
The CS: Computer Store Point of Sale and Inventory Management System is a web application project integrating RFID technology, providing a comprehensive solution for Yannie Computer Store.

It includes a POS and inventory management facility that aims to streamline operations, facilitate transactions, and efficiently manage inventory. The system addresses various issues encountered in the original system, such as tracking client returns, stock transfers between branches, monitoring branch sales and stock levels, listing eligible clients for discounts, and handling bundled items.

The developer utilized the Multi-motive Information Systems Continuance Model and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology to ensure user acceptance and enhance user experience. Testing results confirmed the system's operational effectiveness and technical efficiency, with ratings and scores from interviews and surveys highlighting its practicality and user-friendliness compared to the previous system.

The development followed a personal SCRUM approach within the agile methodology, progressing through stages: database layer, application layer, and client layer. Future plans involve creating a storefront web application, incorporating product photos, implementing a printing report feature, and considering integration of an AI system. These enhancements aim to maintain competitiveness in the market and cater to evolving user needs.

two:
The capstone project titled "CS: Computer Store Point of Sale and Inventory Management System with RFID Technology using Flutter Framework," authored by Willord Jay O. Villanueva, addresses critical operational inefficiencies within Yannie Computer Store. The work details the development of a specialized web application designed to modernize the store's manual and fragmented processes through digitalization and centralized monitoring.

**Problem**
The primary problem domain involves significant management issues regarding inventory and monitoring across multiple branches. The existing system lacks centralization, meaning administrators can only monitor sales and stock levels at the main branch, requiring manual inquiries or physical travel to check other locations. Inventory management is hindered by manual, paper-based processes for transferring stocks between branches, which leads to inaccuracies. Furthermore, the store lacks a structured procedure for tracking customer returns and repairs, often resulting in lost information. The Point of Sale (POS) system is also insufficient, as it cannot handle product bundling—requiring staff to manually update individual component stocks after a bundle sale—and it lacks an efficient way to identify and apply discounts to loyal customers.

**Context**
Yannie Computer Store is a private retail business specializing in computer and laptop parts, accessories, and other technological products. The business operates across multiple branches, necessitating a more robust way to manage distributed inventory and sales data. The project was developed within a three-month timeframe using an agile methodology, specifically a personal SCRUM approach, to ensure the system met the specific needs of the store's administrators, staff, and technicians.

**Method**
The developer employed a structured development process involving analysis, prototyping, and testing. The project was guided by two theoretical frameworks: the Multi-motive Information Systems Continuance Model (MISC) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT). These frameworks were used to ensure the system was designed for high user acceptance, ease of use, and long-term usability. 

The technical implementation utilized the Flutter framework for the client layer to ensure a responsive and visually appealing user interface, and the Laravel PHP framework for the application layer. A RESTful API architecture was implemented to facilitate communication between the client and the server. The system uses a hybrid database approach, employing MySQL for both local storage at the branch level and cloud storage for centralized administrative monitoring. To mitigate connectivity risks, a middleware approach was designed to allow local transactions to continue during internet outages, syncing with the cloud once connection is restored. The system also integrates RFID technology to automate customer discount applications.

**Findings**
The development and testing phases yielded several key findings. The system successfully integrated various modules, including a dashboard for centralized monitoring, an inventory facility for managing stock transfers and procurement, a POS facility capable of handling product bundles, an after-sales facility for tracking returns, and a library facility for managing customer, supplier, and user data. 

Testing results confirmed the system's operational and technical effectiveness. Interviews and surveys indicated that the system is more practical and user-friendly than the previous manual and fragmented methods. Technical testing, including manual performance testing and parallel testing (running the new system alongside the old one), showed that the system's reports were consistent with existing records, proving its reliability. The integration of RFID technology was found to be an effective method for streamlining customer promotions and discounts.

**Conclusions**
The project concludes that the implemented system successfully meets the client's requirements and addresses the core problems of inventory tracking, centralized monitoring, and transaction efficiency. The use of the Flutter and Laravel combination proved effective for building a scalable and responsive application. The developer successfully met all project requirements within the allotted timeframe. The study demonstrates that transitioning from manual, paper-based, and decentralized processes to an integrated, digitalized system significantly improves operational efficiency and data accuracy in a multi-branch retail environment.

**Implications**
The implications of this work suggest that implementing such a system can revolutionize small to medium-sized retail operations by providing real-time visibility into business health. For Yannie Computer Store, the system enables better decision-making through data-driven insights into sales and stock trends. The project also highlights the importance of considering connectivity risks in centralized systems by implementing local-first data strategies. 

Future implications and recommendations for further development include the creation of a dedicated storefront web application to expand market reach, the implementation of an SMS facility to notify customers of new stock, and the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to suggest compatible product bundles. Additionally, adding product photos and enhanced report generation (exporting to PDF or Excel) would further improve the user experience and administrative utility.

title: Website and Information System of Labomed Incorporated
abstract:
The use of various software platforms in the daily operation of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs) like Labomed Incorporated makes companies less efficient due to the cumbersome tasks of switching from one program to another. This project has developed a dedicated Information System (IS) that has the features that the company needs to operate efficiently. An analysis of the company's strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) was conducted to help with the project development.

Based on the user testings and surveys administered, the theory is that SMEs must design and implement their very own IS to attain improved business processes. This study emphasizes that SMEs don't need to be stagnant and rely on just using their accustomed software but rather to be undaunted in taking risks in creating their own IS.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
Labomed Incorporated, a US-based manufacturer of laboratory instruments, faced operational inefficiencies due to a reliance on disconnected software platforms like Microsoft Excel, QuickBooks, and WordPress. These fragmented systems required manual data exchange, causing delays in delivering product information to global clients. To address this, a customized Web Application was developed to serve as a centralized Management Information System (MIS). Large-scale Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems were rejected because they were deemed too costly, complex, and contained unnecessary features for the company's needs.

The development utilized the Model-View-Controller (MVC) pattern and included modules for product management, customer and manufacturer interactions, and a business analytics dashboard featuring predictive and prescriptive analytics. The system underwent manual unit, regression, and security testing. Security testing identified high and medium-priority vulnerabilities, such as missing anti-clickjacking headers, which require future code adjustments.

User testing involving ten respondents yielded a System Usability Scale score of 71.25, categorized as a "Good" grade. While users found the system user-friendly and would recommend it, the score suggests a need for further refinement. The study concludes that for SMEs, a customized, centralized IS is more effective than disconnected software or expensive off-the-shelf ERPs. Such tailored solutions consolidate functions, save time, and reduce training requirements. Future work will focus on developing user permission modules, a customer bidding system, and SEO marketing tools.

Labomed Incorporated, a US-based manufacturing company and distributor of laboratory instruments, faced significant operational challenges despite strong annual sales. The company struggled with daily workflow efficiency, specifically regarding the timely and accurate provision of product information to global clients. This inefficiency stemmed from the company's reliance on multiple, disconnected software platforms, including Microsoft Excel, QuickBooks, and WordPress. The necessity of switching between these disparate systems created cumbersome tasks and wasted valuable time, as information had to be manually exchanged between platforms.

To address these issues, the researcher developed a dedicated, customized Web Application designed to serve as a centralized Management Information System (IS). While large enterprises often utilize complex Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems like SAP or Odoo, these were deemed unsuitable for Labomed due to their high cost, excessive complexity, and the presence of many unnecessary features. Furthermore, the company's diverse stakeholder age range (25–90 years old) necessitated a system that was user-friendly and not overly complicated.

The methodology employed a three-part development process: functional analysis to identify necessary business models, data analysis to create conceptual, logical, and physical designs, and an implementation stage. The project utilized the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework to identify technological, organizational, and environmental determinants for the system's adoption. A SWOT analysis was also conducted to diagnose the company's current performance and identify the need for a centralized system. The technical stack included PHP for server-side logic, MySQL for database management, Bootstrap for responsive web design, and a Linux-based web host. The system architecture followed the Model-View-Controller (MVC) pattern to ensure software sustainability.

The developed system includes several key modules: a product information module for managing details, a customer and manufacturer module for generating quotes, sales, and purchase orders, and a business analytics dashboard featuring predictive and prescriptive analytics to track trends and stock levels. It also features dynamic product publishing via CSV imports, a dedicated order history page, and an admin control panel.

To assess the system, the researcher conducted manual unit testing, regression testing, and security testing using the OWASP Zed Attack Proxy (ZAP). User testing was performed through surveys administered to ten respondents, including the CEO, employees, customers, and manufacturers. The usability was measured using the System Usability Scale (SU). Security testing identified several vulnerabilities, including missing anti-clickjacking headers, which the researcher noted could be resolved by updating third-party libraries and adding specific code to page headers.

The findings from the user testing indicated a System Usability score of 71.25, which corresponds to a "B" letter grade, categorized as "Good." While the system was deemed user-friendly and most respondents indicated they would recommend it, the score suggests that the system is not yet exceptional and requires further refinement. Security testing revealed high and medium-priority alerts that require resolution through updates and code adjustments.

The study concludes that for an SME like Labomed Inc., a customized, centralized Information System is more effective than using multiple separate software programs or expensive, overly complex off-the-shelf ERPs. A custom IS allows the company to consolidate organizational functions into one platform, saving time and reducing the training required for stakeholders. The project demonstrates that SMEs can improve business processes by designing and implementing their own tailored technological solutions rather than remaining stagnant with accustomed, disconnected software.

The implications of this work suggest that SMEs should not be deterred by the complexity of information systems but should instead take the risk of creating customized solutions to achieve workflow efficiency. The researcher notes that while the project provides a foundation, further research is needed to confirm the long-term success of custom IS in improving SME workflows. Future work for this project includes the development of a user permission module to enhance privacy, a customer bidding system, a website marketing system for SEO, and a dedicated company information module for administrators.

title: Philippine Army Reserve Command Attendance System
abstract:
There are issues and problems being experienced on the manual accounting of troops using pen and paper attendance sheets being used in the Philippine Army Reserve Command, This problem was recently faced during the Tall Volcano eruption and currently with the Covid19 crisis wherein the troops has to be deployed to different parts of Batangas and Laguna to help assist in the emergencies. The goal of this system is to address this problem which is the real time accounting or troops who are deployed at different locations
on different schedules by using technology. Each personnel can update their commanders for their exact location and the time of their duties by logging in to the system through their mobile devices. The commanders will then have the capability to view real time data on the whereabouts of all personnel under their command.

The system is currently being reviewed by the Group Commander of the Philippine Army Reserve Command.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
The Philippine Army Reserve Command currently relies on manual, paper-based attendance sheets to track personnel, a process that has proven problematic during emergency situations like the COVID-19 crisis and the Taal Volcano eruption. When troops are deployed across various locations in Batangas and Laguna, the manual system makes it difficult to maintain accurate, up-to-date information regarding personnel locations and duty schedules, hindering real-time oversight by leadership.

To address these limitations, this study proposes the development of the Philippine Army Reserve Command Attendance System. This mobile-based technological solution allows individual personnel to use their own mobile devices to log into the system, updating commanders on their exact location and specific duty times. This approach shifts data entry responsibility to personnel on the ground, ensuring reported information is current and location-specific. Consequently, commanders can access real-time data to monitor the whereabouts of all personnel under their command instantaneously, replacing slow and error-prone manual processes with a digital overview of troop distribution.

The system aims to modernize personnel management by transitioning from outdated manual methods to a responsive digital framework. Currently undergoing review by the Group Commander to ensure military suitability, the system's implementation could significantly enhance operational efficiency. By providing real-time visibility of troop locations, the command can make more informed decisions during disaster response efforts.

title: TIPid: A Financial Management Application Designed for Filipinos
abstract: Based on a survey by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, out of three financial literacy related questions only 8% of Filipinos can correctly answer all while less than half can only answer one question. Since mobile applications have been tools to aid users in various daily tasks, TIPid aims to be a financial management application designed for Filipinos. The application does not only provide money tracking features but also integrate tips and information for the awareness and habit building suited to our fellow countrymen.This aims to help the users retain their budget, observe their current financial situation, and be aware of different financial strategies.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
The capstone project "TIPid: A Financial Management Application Designed for Filipinos" addresses low financial literacy rates in the Philippines, where only 8% of citizens can correctly answer all financial literacy questions. While smartphone usage is high, existing management applications often lack cultural relevance. The primary objective of TIPid was to develop a mobile application tailored to the Filipino context using localized terminology and icons to encourage habit-building.

Developed using the Scrum framework, the application was built with the Ionic Framework and AngularJS, utilizing Google Firebase for data storage and deployment. The system design features three core components: the Kita Tracker (Income), the Ipon Tracker (Savings), and the Bayarin Tracker (Expenses/Bills). A unique feature is a notification system that provides random financial tips in conversational Filipino, crowdsourced from various age groups to ensure relatability.

User testing with 11 users showed a highly positive reception, particularly among millennials using iOS devices. Respondents reported feeling confident using the application, finding the functions well-integrated and easy to learn. title: Computer Laboratory Management Services for Prince Mohammed Bin Fahd University Website
abstract: To get the job done efficiently, we rely on technology that can speed up the process of our daily routine. In our world today where computers/devices are interconnected through the Internet, innovations have been made to make our jobs easier. When it comes to data processing and recording, we no longer use methods or recording through paper forms or logbooks. The computer laboratory is a facility that caters to services in terms of computer usage, request of equipment, and monitoring the resources. Scheduling, monitoring requests, and the availability of resources is not an easy task, and it may take a certain amount of time for the person requesting the services. Hence, this research is focused on innovating the way the users (Students, Lab Instructors) acquire services and the person (Lab technicians) who cater these services. By providing a system in the form of a web application that gives access to the users to schedule a reservation, to use a computer in the laboratory, make a request for installation of software or device and check the availability of the resources. The system is developed using the Laravel web framework following the model–view–controller (MVC) pattern. PHP is used to develop web pages using Bootstrap in the front-end design. And MySQL database for the repository. In the resulting system, the lab technician can monitor the computer lab usage, reservations, request, and the inventory of the computers and devices in the laboratory. The users will just access the website and select the services that are available or provided via cellphone, computer terminal, or any device with a web browser that is connected through the Internet. Therefore, there is now no need to go directly to the laboratory technician's office or email to file a service. Just log in to the system and wait for the notification for the service.

half:
Charmaine B. Cruz’s research, "Computer Laboratory Management Services for Prince Mohammed Bin Fahd University Website," addresses inefficiencies caused by manual laboratory management processes. The current reliance on physical logbooks and Excel spreadsheets leads to data entry errors, tedious reporting, security risks regarding record tampering, and a lack of time-stamps. Furthermore, the manual system requires time-consuming in-person visits and redundant email communications.

To resolve these issues, the researcher developed a centralized web application guided by Task-Technology Fit theory. The system provides distinct interfaces for students, faculty, and technicians, featuring online reservations for slots and equipment, service requests for software and hardware, a resource availability viewer, and automated inventory management. Technicians can monitor lab usage and generate comprehensive reports. The project was developed using the Waterfall model, utilizing the Laravel framework, PHP, Bootstrap, HTML5, CSS, JavaScript, and a MySQL database.

User testing involving 74 respondents—40 students, 21 faculty, and 13 technicians—yielded overwhelmingly positive results. Students reported 96% satisfaction regarding the login interface and task efficiency. Faculty members rated task completion at 91% and information clarity at 90%. Technicians reported 95% satisfaction regarding information organization, clarity, and application consistency. The study concludes that the web-based solution provides a faster, more secure, and more efficient method for managing laboratory resources and requests.

title: FEIS: Faculty Evaluation Information System of Card-MRI Development Institute, Inc.
abstract:
FEIS: Faculty Evaluation Information System, implemented at CARD-MRI Development Institute, Inc. for the Academe Department, is a web-based information system that provides assistance to school supervisors to easily evaluate teachers. The system provides consolidated reports and suggestions that will help the management in providing capacity-building programs appropriate for the teacher’s field of expertise.

The web-based information system is developed using the PHP language and JavaScript for the back-end. BOOTSTRAP, HTML, and CSS for front-end design and MySQL in PHPMyAdmin for database. The proponent of the study uses Agile methodology for the software development life cycle model for the active participation of clients in the project development. A project timeline was also proposed to make sure that the development process is right on track. After the software development, testing phase was initiated. The participants have been given a chance to critique and evaluate the software for the next sprint. The software components are integrated into one complete package to be accepted by the user on every deployment. During the customer survey, the proposed system was evaluated using the System Usability Scale (SUS). The data is interpreted using SUS scoring: A grade of 80.3 or higher is equivalent to an A grade, a C grade is equivalent to a score of 52 to 68, and anything less than 51 points is equivalent to an F grade.

title: Security Deployment Tracking System
abstract:
The United Nations (UN) Mission Security Office has a sub-unit who does the daily radio check to know whether staff member(s) are present/absent at any given time within the mission area. It is the Security Office's responsibility to know the staff member(s) and other personnel’s accommodation location and even movement from one team-site to another team-site in the mission. The daily radio check helps the security process, since radio communication is primarily a means to receive and disseminate information in a timely and effective manner to multiple users in times of emergencies like crises. Furthermore, it is a link between the various entities, sectors, and regional offices of a mission. Personnel traveling out of their designated duty station are to notify relevant radio room in duty station of their absence and to be excluded from daily radio check during dates provided. Similarly, those that are traveling back and arriving in the mission area, are to be included in the daily radio check during the stated period of their stay. But the manual logging and lack of significant data and other information needed is becoming problematic.

The Security Deployment Tracking System (SDTS) aims to assist Security Officials to keep up-to-date information related to staff member(s) and other personnel within the Security System. The out-of-date process of monitoring staff member(s) and other personnel was transformed in having efficient information over the web-based application that allow quick saving of data, updating of data, extracting useful data for reporting purposes and an email notification to those who doesn’t do the daily radio check within the time-range specified to do it. This email notification is filtered to certain criteria to avoid alert and email overload.

The QR code feature reduces logging time, while automated reports and email notifications for missed radio checks enhance security efficiency. By transforming fragmented processes into a streamlined digital workflow, the SDTS provides a "single pane of glass" view of personnel, facilitating rapid response during crises.

The system achieves its objectives of improving productivity, reducing costs associated with physical supplies, and enhancing the security of personnel data through centralized management and automated backups. The transition from physical logbooks to a digital platform provides a more reliable and environmentally friendly model for mission security management.

The implications of this work suggest that moving toward integrated, digital-first security management is essential for modern, highly collaborative organizations. By centralizing data, the UN can achieve a "single pane of glass" view of personnel, which is critical for rapid response during crises. The researcher recommends several areas for future development, including the implementation of e-signatures for security clearances, the ability for users to access specific regional data, and the enhancement of the interface to generate QR codes directly. Additionally, the researcher suggests that future iterations could leverage mobile access and more advanced integrations with networked devices, such as cameras or scanners, to create a more robust, ransomware-resilient data protection strategy.

title: Development of Delivery Robot (DELIBOT) Using Microcontroller and Line Tracker
abstract:
The project was developed to transport items using an Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) delivery robot named “Delibot”. For this project, the robot was used in a restaurant environment to transport food and dishes. The robot was able to move inside the workplace by following the black track that guides the robot to reach different locations from the kitchen to customers’ tables and return to the kitchen. The robot movements were controlled and guided by a microcontroller (ATMega2560) and proximity sensors. Four proximity sensors were installed for detecting the tracks and junction nodes. The robot can be programmed by the user to move and follow directions from origin to its destination. The robot was driven by 4 DC motors that allow it to move straight, turn left or right and rotate from its current position. To make the robot user-friendly, it was equipped with an audio module player that allows speaking like humans to communicate to the user.

The robot was tested using a small-scale prototype and successfully achieved the objective of transporting item and its capability to be reprogrammed according to the robot’s track path

title: Digital Transformation of N&T Engineering Enterprise: Automating Paper-Based Maintenance Checklist
abstract:
This project addresses the need of the business to automate its current manual process. The current process involves manual and paper-based checklists with no checking and verification in place. This project implements an application that handles the automation of paper-based processes using computers. Process improvement in their core business includes faster turn-around time, less paperwork and storage requirement, instantaneous information retrieval, and work output integrity check.

N&T Engineering Enterprise (Pte) Ltd. is one of the few Mechanical and Electrical (M&E) Engineering specialists in Singapore with an established track record and a huge array of large clients in government, government-linked companies, and multinational corporations. They handle projects on Mission-Critical Facilities and Infrastructures (air/land/tunnel traffic infrastructure, immigration and checkpoint facilities, institutions, etc.), Mission-Critical Systems (monitoring and control systems, surveillance, support systems, fiber-optic network system, etc.), and Smart City Systems (IoT for Mission-Critical Facilities and Infrastructure).

Software Development Lifecycle is the framework and Project Management governs the process during the development of the application. Asset, telecommunications, and network security were implemented to protect data in motion, in transit, and at rest.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
Federico Gregorio’s capstone project addresses the operational inefficiencies and security vulnerabilities in N&T Engineering Enterprise’s manual maintenance workflows. The Singapore-based firm relied on paper-based checklists for CCTV inspections, a process prone to fraud due to unverifiable site visits and inefficient for data storage. To resolve these issues, Gregorio developed "Gemba," a secure, automated digital application designed to digitize surveillance camera inspections.

The project followed a structured Software Development Lifecycle, emphasizing early security integration to reduce defect costs. Built on Oracle Application Express, the client-server system was deployed on-premises in Hong Kong, utilizing Dell bare-metal machines and dual-layer firewalls. Security was embedded at every layer: the application layer employed sandboxing and code obfuscation, while server hardening included disabling non-essential services. Data protection was ensured through end-to-end encryption, Role-Based Access Control, and comprehensive endpoint security solutions like SentinelOne and Digital Guardian.

Rigorous testing included third-party code reviews, OWASP dynamic testing, and vulnerability assessments. These efforts reduced potential attack vectors from 80 to 44 and addressed over a thousand identified vulnerabilities through patching and service shutdowns. The findings confirm that Gemba successfully automated the workflow, eliminating paperwork and enabling instant retrieval. Fraud mitigation was achieved via audit logs and mandatory site photographs. User testing yielded positive usability results, with dashboards providing real-time oversight.

The study concludes that security must be integrated from the initial design phase to be effective. It highlights that information security is a continuous process requiring both technical controls and administrative measures, such as user awareness training. Future recommendations include implementing Mobile Device Management for field technicians and conducting annual third-party penetration tests to maintain robust security standards against evolving threats.
one:
Federico Gregorio’s capstone project, "Digital Transformation of N&T Engineering Enterprise: Automating Paper-Based Maintenance Checklist," addresses the operational inefficiencies and security vulnerabilities inherent in the manual maintenance workflows of N&T Engineering Enterprise (Pte) Ltd. This Singapore-based Mechanical and Electrical engineering firm specializes in mission-critical facilities and smart city infrastructure. The study focuses on digitizing their surveillance camera inspection processes to replace a legacy paper-based system with a secure, automated digital application named "Gemba."

The problem domain is defined by the reliance on physical checklists for field technicians inspecting CCTV equipment across Singapore. The existing workflow involves technicians manually recording diagnosis items on paper forms, which are subsequently reviewed by supervisors and approved by managers. This manual process lacks mechanisms to verify whether a technician actually visited the site or performed the inspection, creating a significant risk of fraud and integrity issues. Although no direct evidence of collusion was found, management expressed concern regarding the unverifiable nature of the reports. Furthermore, the paper-based system required substantial manpower for filing, storage, and retrieval, leading to slower turnaround times and potential data loss. The project objectives were to automate the workflow, digitize the forms, and mitigate fraud through technological controls.

The methodology employed a structured Software Development Lifecycle governed by project management principles. The theoretical framework emphasized baking security into the software development process from the conceptualization stage, arguing that addressing security early reduces the relative cost of defects. The solution, "Gemba," was developed using Oracle Application Express as the base framework. The system architecture followed a client-server model, deployed on-premises in a private cloud data center in Kwun Tong, Hong Kong. The infrastructure included bare-metal Dell machines with SAN storage, protected by a two-layer firewall deployment involving Cisco ASA and Fortinet FortiGate appliances.

Security was a central component of the technical approach. The application layer utilized secure coding practices, including sandboxing, encrypted shared preferences, and code obfuscation. The server and database layers were hardened by disabling non-essential services and running on Microsoft Windows Server 2019 with an Oracle database engine. To protect data in motion, in transit, and at rest, the system implemented end-to-end encryption via Virtual Private Networking. Access was controlled through a Domain Controller using Role-Based Access Control, with authentication managed by Cisco Identity Services Engine. The client layer was secured with SentinelOne for AI-driven antimalware protection, Rapid7 for Security Incident and Event Management, and Digital Guardian for Data Leak Prevention.

The project included rigorous testing and assessment plans. User testing involved reasonableness checks, white-box and static source code reviews by third parties, and dynamic testing using OWASP standards. Security testing involved an attack surface analysis, which reduced potential attack vectors from 80 to 44 by hardening the system. A vulnerability assessment using InsightVM identified 1,177 vulnerabilities, including 209 critical ones. These were addressed by installing Microsoft patches, uninstalling Adobe Flash, and shutting down unused services.

The findings indicated that the project successfully met its primary objectives. The process was fully automated, eliminating paperwork and enabling instant information retrieval. Fraud mitigation was achieved through system audit logs that tracked the movement of work orders and required field technicians to submit pictures taken from the site. A System Usability Scale survey with eight pilot users yielded overwhelmingly positive results regarding usability. The dashboard provided real-time alerts and a visual representation of maintenance status, enhancing managerial oversight.

The conclusions emphasize that while software development tools have become more accessible, the true challenge lies in securing sensitive information. The project demonstrated that security must be integrated from the initial design phase to be effective. Recommendations highlight that information security is a continuous process requiring process maturity. The author suggests that administrative controls, such as user awareness training, are as critical as technical controls. Specific recommendations for future development include the implementation of Mobile Device Management to protect confidential information on smartphones used by field technicians. Additionally, the author recommends annual penetration testing by a third party to ensure that any external-facing services are regularly audited for vulnerabilities.

The existing workflow involves technicians manually recording diagnosis items on paper forms, which are subsequently reviewed by supervisors and approved by managers. This manual process lacks mechanisms to verify whether a technician actually visited the site or performed the inspection, creating a significant risk of fraud and integrity issues. Although no direct evidence of collusion was found, the management expressed concern regarding the unverifiable nature of the reports. Furthermore, the paper-based system required substantial manpower for filing, storage, and retrieval, leading to slower turnaround times and potential loss of data. The project objectives were threefold: to automate the workflow, to digitize the forms, and to mitigate the risk of fraud through technological controls.

The methodology employed a structured Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) governed by project management principles. The theoretical framework emphasized the importance of baking security into the software development process from the conceptualization stage, rather than treating it as an afterthought. The author argued that addressing security early reduces the relative cost of defects and prevents the creation of insecure software. The solution, "Gemba," was developed using Oracle Application Express (APEX) as the base framework. The system architecture followed a client-server model, with the application deployed on-premises in a private cloud data center located in Kwun Tong, Hong Kong. The infrastructure included bare-metal Dell machines with SAN storage, protected by a two-layer firewall deployment involving Cisco ASA and Fortinet FortiGate appliances.

Security was a central component of the technical approach. The application layer utilized secure coding practices, including sandboxing, encrypted shared preferences, and code obfuscation. The server and database layers were hardened by disabling non-essential services and running on Microsoft Windows Server 2019 with an Oracle database engine. To protect data in motion, in transit, and at rest, the system implemented end-to-end encryption via Virtual Private Networking (VPN). Access was controlled through a Domain Controller using Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), with authentication managed by Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE). The client layer was secured with SentinelOne for AI-driven antimalware protection, Rapid7 for Security Incident and Event Management (SIEM), and Digital Guardian for Data Leak Prevention (DLP). The system features included reports management, resource management for manpower and machines, workflow logic for automated notifications, and a dashboard providing an at-a-glance view of maintenance status via a geographic map of Singapore.

Abuse cases were modeled to identify potential negative impacts on the system. A vulnerability assessment using InsightVM identified 1,177 vulnerabilities, including 209 critical ones. These were addressed by installing Microsoft patches, uninstalling Adobe Flash, and shutting down unused services such as FTP and SMTP. Additional mitigations for web vulnerabilities included implementing anti-CSRF tokens, configuring cross-domain settings, and ensuring secure page content.

The findings indicated that the project successfully met its primary objectives. The process was fully automated, eliminating paperwork and enabling instant information retrieval. The digitization of forms improved usability and reduced storage requirements. Fraud mitigation was achieved through system audit logs that tracked the movement of work orders and the requirement for field technicians to submit pictures taken from the site. A System Usability Scale survey conducted with eight pilot users yielded overwhelmingly positive results regarding usability and user experience. The dashboard provided real-time alerts and a visual representation of maintenance status, enhancing managerial oversight.

The conclusions drawn by the author emphasize that while software development tools have become more accessible, the true challenge lies in securing sensitive information. The project demonstrated that security must be integrated from the initial design phase to be effective. The author noted that the application development faced challenges due to the pandemic and resource limitations, leaving room for future improvements. However, the core goals of automation, digitization, and fraud mitigation were satisfactorily achieved.

The recommendations highlight that information security is a continuous process requiring process maturity. The author suggests that administrative controls, such as user awareness training, are as critical as technical controls. Specific recommendations for future development include the implementation of Mobile Device Management (MDM) to protect confidential information on smartphones used by field technicians. Additionally, the author recommends annual penetration testing by a third party to ensure that any external-facing services are regularly audited for vulnerabilities. The study serves as a case study for integrating robust security measures into digital transformation initiatives within engineering enterprises.

title: Vehicle Monitoring System with QR Code for the Don Mariano Marcos Memorial State University, North La Union Campus, Bacnotan, La Union
abstract:
This study developed a Vehicle Monitoring System Using QR Code to help monitor the vehicles entering and leaving the campus in order to ensure the health and safety of the employees/workers/students at Don Mariano Marcos Memorial State University (DMMMSU) - North La Union Campus (NLUC).

Specifically, it aimed to (a) determine the socio-demographic profile of the respondents as to age and type of respondent; and (b) assess the level of acceptability of the Vehicle Monitoring System as to functional suitability, performance efficiency, usability, reliability, security and portability.

The study used descriptive and developmental research methods, with survey questionnaires as the primary data collection instruments. Twenty (20) employees and twenty (20) security guards were among the survey's participants.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
Don Mariano Marcos Memorial State University - North La Union Campus faces challenges with manual vehicle monitoring, such as traffic congestion, illegible handwriting, and security risks. The manual process of recording details in logbooks also complicates health protocols requiring social distancing. To address these issues, a Vehicle Monitoring System utilizing QR codes was developed to monitor vehicles entering and leaving the campus to ensure the safety of employees, workers, and students.

The study employed descriptive and developmental research methods, collecting data from twenty employees and twenty security guards. The system functions as a time-stamp database providing real-time monitoring and printable logs. It features a Super Admin role to manage profiles and generate electronic passes. Technical implementation involved HTML 5 QR generator, PHP, and MySQLi on a Windows 10 Pro operating system.

Findings showed the majority of respondents were in the age bracket of 26-30. The system received an overall acceptability rating of 97.50%. Specific ratings included 100% for functional suitability, performance efficiency, usability, reliability, and portability. The security characteristic received an 85% rating, as some respondents desired more extensive access levels. The study concludes the system is a successful tool and recommends official implementation at Gate 1 and Gate 2, alongside staff training, regular maintenance, and the purchase of additional QR readers if expanded to other campuses.

The system architecture includes a Super Admin role capable of managing employee profiles and generating QR codes, which serve as electronic passes (E-Pass) for users. The findings revealed that the majority of the respondents were in the age bracket of 26-30. title: Data Analytics Information System for Railway-Subway Construction Industry
abstract:
Instrumentation data management system which collects real-time instrumentation data, project progress information, Tunnel Borehole Machines (TBM) statistics were mainly used for monitoring. It was already playing a vital role in Singapore construction industry even before the disastrous event way back in 2004. Cited as one of the most tragic events in the history of Subway development when Nicole Highway structure collapsed and claimed lives. The system turned out to be practically inefficient and lacks acumen. Furthermore, different systems were being utilized by different contractors which leads to a decentralized data storage and there were no data retention at all every end of the project.

The on-going predicament of safety in every construction project can be resolved by proposing an intelligent information system by leveraging on historical data and technology. The proposed concept can be achieved by integrating cloud infrastructure, tools specialized on Data Analytics and fundamentals from experienced Subject-Matter experts. The artificial neural network would make the system capable of learning on its own based on the progressive infused records. On the other hand, project owners or stakeholders will challenge the value over its cost impact. The Research & Development alone should have a significant impact to the overall construction budget. Including the operation and maintenance expenditure in keeping the system available, responsive, intuitive and up to date. The proof of concept should be able to quantify its value holistically to the pay masters.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
This research addresses critical inefficiencies in data management within the railway and subway construction industry. Current methods for monitoring real-time instrumentation, project progress, and Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM) statistics are often inefficient and lack necessary acumen. title: First Aid Response (FAR) Mobile Application
abstract: First Aid Response Mobile Application (FAR) is an emergency software that states the location of the incident and works similar to ride-hailing applications such as but not limited to Grab, Uber, Lalamove, and Angkas, which has a similar concept where it helps the first aider to respond quickly in addition to the traditional way of the emergency response system, wherein the user shall call an emergency number and the emergency alert will be received by the dispatcher and the latter shall send the alert notification to all active medical team/personnel within the vicinity area of the former hence will track down who is the nearest to the location of the user/victim among them, once the active first aider received the alert it will automatically dispatch and  accommodate the request of the user. The First Aid Mobile Application will give the user another help and option that could eliminate the time that is consumed by heavy traffic or travel time through the provision of direct notifications to the nearest first aid volunteer.

Developed by Armand Boy Peralta, the First Aid Response (FAR) mobile application is a specialized software designed to augment traditional emergency response systems. The project addresses delays in medical intervention caused by factors like heavy traffic, which can prevent emergency vehicles from reaching victims during critical windows, such as the four to six minutes before brain death occurs. By utilizing a ride-hailing concept, the app connects victims to the nearest trained individuals to bridge the gap between an incident and professional help.

The system supports three user roles: Regular Users, First Aiders, and Admins. Technical implementation includes Firebase, Node.js, and Google Cloud. Key features include OTP verification, certification document uploads for First Aiders, an administrative dashboard, and location tracking to identify available responders within a one-kilometer radius. The app also provides offline-accessible, step-by-step first aid instructions.

Testing via Black Box - Decision Table Testing confirmed the functional reliability of registration, OTP generation, and the First Aider approval process. The ride-hailing mechanism and knowledge base also functioned as expected. A SWOT analysis identified strengths in response time and location accuracy, while noting weaknesses such as the requirement for an Android device (version 11 or higher) and an internet connection. The author concludes that FAR is a vital supplementary tool that empowers trained citizens to act during the "golden minutes" of an emergency.

The First Aid Response (FAR) mobile application is a specialized emergency software designed to augment traditional emergency response systems. Developed by Armand Boy Peralta, the project addresses the critical need for rapid medical intervention during life-threatening emergencies such as cardiac arrest, heart attacks, or strokes.

**Problem and Context**
The core problem addressed by this work is the delay in emergency response times, which can be fatal. In the Philippines, particularly in Metro Manila, heavy traffic often prevents emergency vehicles from reaching victims quickly. The author notes that medical professionals define "clinical death" as the cessation of heartbeat and respiration, and if proper treatment like Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is not administered within four to six minutes, the victim may progress to "brain death," which is irreversible. While the current system of calling 911 or local hotlines is functional, it relies on dispatchers manually locating and sending teams, a process that consumes vital seconds. The author seeks to bridge this gap by providing a digital solution that connects victims directly to the nearest trained individuals.

**Method**
The project utilizes a ride-hailing concept, similar to applications like Grab or Uber, to facilitate rapid response. The system architecture supports three distinct user roles: Regular Users (the general public), First Aiders (trained and certified individuals), and Admins (support staff). 

The technical implementation involves a modern software stack: Firebase for the real-time database and backend services, Adobe Photoshop for UI design, InVision for prototyping, Node.js for the runtime environment, and Google Cloud for storage. The system design includes several key features: a registration process with One-Time Password (OTP) verification for security, a document upload feature for First Aiders to submit certifications, and an administrative dashboard for verifying the credentials of responders. A central feature is the ride-hailing mechanism, which uses location tracking to identify the nearest available First Aider within a one-kilometer radius of an incident. Additionally, the app includes a knowledge-based feature providing step-by-step first aid instructions that can be accessed without an internet connection.

**Findings**
The project underwent assessment through user testing and an Alpha test using the Black Box - Decision Table Testing methodology. The testing results confirmed the functional reliability of the application's core components. Specifically, the registration features for both regular users and First Aiders functioned as expected, correctly handling valid and invalid inputs. The OTP generation and First Aider approval processes were successful, ensuring that only verified users could access responder roles. The ride-hailing feature was tested for response timing, confirming that requests are successfully sent and received within the designated parameters. Furthermore, the knowledge-base feature was verified to be accessible without interrupting ongoing emergency requests. The SWOT analysis identified strengths such as reduced response time and location accuracy, while noting weaknesses like the requirement for an internet connection and the necessity of an Android device (version 11 or higher).

**Conclusions**
The author concludes that the FAR mobile application serves as a vital supplementary tool to existing emergency services. By leveraging the ubiquity of mobile phones, the application provides a way to minimize the time between an accident and the arrival of professional medical help. The study reinforces the theoretical framework that while mobile applications cannot replace practical medical training, they significantly enhance the performance of trained responders by providing rapid communication and instructional guidance. The application successfully integrates location-based technology with a verified user database to create a more efficient emergency ecosystem.

**Implications**
The implications of this work suggest a significant shift in how community-based emergency response can be managed. By empowering trained citizens to act as immediate responders, the reliance on heavy-traffic-delayed ambulances is mitigated during the "golden minutes" of an emergency. 

The author proposes several avenues for future development to maximize the application's impact. Technically, the author recommends expanding compatibility to iOS and Windows platforms. Operationally, the author suggests increasing the response radius and coordinating with government entities such as the Department of Science and Technology (DOST), the Department of Health (DOH), and the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) to provide zero-rated data access, ensuring the app is free to use for all citizens. Finally, to ensure long-term reliability and security, the author recommends implementing a rating system and a reporting function to prevent misuse or fraudulent requests.

title: TESTTIME: An Online Examination System
abstract: The UPOU Office of Student Affairs or OSA Examination Services Program has begun administering exams in either online non proctored or online proctored double set up due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic (UPOU OSA, 2020). The project, entitled TestTime, is an online examination system that will help UPOU provide exams to their students in a streamlined manner without sacrificing exam integrity. The online examination system has the functionality to register users such as students and teachers. If the user is a teacher, the system has the functionality to add/edit/delete examinations as well as to add/edit/delete grades. If the user is a student, the system has the functionality to browse, read, take, and review examination questions and submit examination answers, as well as to submit answers for clarifications and regrading. It also allows a user who is either a teacher or faculty member to use a proctoring system while the student is taking an exam. This includes a webcam or screen capture of the student during the exam that allows the proctor to monitor the student in real time. The project includes a review of online examination systems and existing alternatives. The results were evaluated by gathering the input of students on the usability of the system’s functionality and features. Recommendations on how the system can be improved with further development were also included.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
Andrew Joseph L. Ramos's capstone project, "TestTime: An Online Examination System," addresses challenges faced by the University of the Philippines Open University (UPOU) during the COVID-19 pandemic. The study identifies gaps in existing digital processes, specifically regarding question management, feedback mechanisms, and built-in proctoring to ensure academic integrity. Remote testing presents additional difficulties, including potential malpractice, identification concerns, infrastructural barriers like internet connectivity, and high labor costs for human proctoring.

To address these issues, the author developed TestTime, an online examination system designed to streamline processes while maintaining integrity. The system offers distinct functionalities for different roles: teachers can register, manage examinations, and manage grades, while students can register, browse, take, and review exams, submit answers, and provide feedback. A key feature is the integrated proctoring functionality, which allows faculty to monitor students in real-time via webcam or screen capture.

The project utilized a prototyping approach and open-source web technologies, including Ubuntu, Apache, PHP, MySQL, and JavaScript libraries. Following development, the system underwent user acceptance testing using a System Usability Scale (SUS) and security testing using the OWASP Zed Attack Proxy (ZAP). Findings were highly positive, with the system achieving a mean SUS score of 75.5. Student feedback indicated the integrated proctoring feature was particularly beneficial as it eliminated the need for external applications. Security testing revealed no high-risk vulnerabilities, though some medium-level risks were identified.

The capstone project "TestTime: An Online Examination System" by Andrew Joseph L. Ramos addresses the specific challenges faced by the University of the Philippines Open University (UPOU) in administering assessments during the COVID-19 pandemic. As academic institutions shifted from physical classrooms to digital environments, several critical gaps were identified in the existing UPOU online examination processes. These gaps included a lack of comprehensive features for managing exam questions and answers, the absence of a straightforward mechanism for student and teacher feedback, and a lack of built-in proctoring functionality to ensure academic integrity.

The problem is compounded by the inherent difficulties of the digital method of testing. The author notes that remote examinations face issues such as potential malpractices and suspicious activities due to the physical separation between students and teachers, identification and verification concerns, infrastructural barriers like internet connectivity, and the high labor costs associated with human proctoring. These factors collectively threaten the integrity, security, and objectivity of the examination process.

To address these issues, the author developed TestTime, an online examination system designed to streamline the examination process while maintaining integrity. The system provides distinct functionalities for different user roles. Teachers can register, manage examinations (add, edit, or delete), and manage grades. Students can register, browse, take, and review exams, submit answers, and provide feedback for clarifications or regrading. A key feature of the system is the integrated proctoring functionality, which allows faculty members to monitor students in real-time via webcam or screen capture.

The project utilized a prototyping approach, which allowed for continuous communication and feedback from users during the development process. The system was built using open-source web technologies to ensure cost-effectiveness and accessibility. The technical stack included the Ubuntu operating system, Apache web server, PHP as the server-side programming language, MySQL for database management, and JavaScript libraries such as Parsley for form validation and PeerJS for webcam streaming. The development was hosted on an Amazon AWS virtual machine instance.

The methodology involved a review of existing alternatives, such as Moodle, Canvas LMS, and other specialized systems like SIETTE and EMS, to implement industry best practices. Following development, the system underwent user testing and security assessment. User acceptance testing was conducted with students using a System Usability Scale (SUS) questionnaire to evaluate the system's effectiveness and ease of use. Security testing was performed using the OWASP Zed Attack Proxy (ZAP) to identify potential vulnerabilities.

The findings from the user testing phase were highly positive. The system achieved a mean SUS score of 75.5, which falls within the "good" to "excellent" range according to established scales. Student feedback indicated that the integrated proctoring feature was particularly beneficial because it provided convenience by eliminating the need for external applications like Google Meet. Users noted that having the webcam and screen-sharing capabilities built directly into the application saved time and offered better control to the proctor. Security testing revealed no high-risk vulnerabilities, although some medium-level risks were identified, such as the need for anti-CSRF tokens and Content Security Policy headers.

In conclusion, the author concludes that TestTime successfully addresses the identified gaps in the UPOU online examination system. The system provides a streamlined way for teachers to manage exams and for students to take them, while the integrated proctoring feature helps promote exam integrity. The research demonstrates that convenience and user satisfaction are key drivers in the perceived benefits of online examinations.

The project offers several recommendations for future development. To enhance the proctoring experience, the author suggests adding support for non-text questions (images and video), enabling multiple webcam streams for double proctoring, and capturing audio to record sessions for later review. Additionally, implementing natural language processing for grading essay-type answers was proposed as a future research area. For system maintenance, the author recommends addressing the medium-level security risks identified by the ZAP scan and upgrading the virtual machine's disk space, memory, and bandwidth to support a larger number of users.
