title: Awaken the Bodhi Mind: A Meditation Guide and Chanting Tracker Mobile Application
abstract: The global pandemic has impacted our lives in ways unimaginable. It changes the way we interact with each other and how we live. Alcohol, mask, and face shield for some have been part of our daily necessities and routine. A number of companies switched to teleworking to avoid contact and to maintain business as usual. Schools implemented modular learning, online classes, and blended learning. Traveling was also one of the hardest parts of the pandemic as most of the borders were closed. Face-to-face meetings and religious gatherings were also stopped but were allowed eventually as long as attendees are limited and the venue is not in full capacity. In spite of that, we learn to adapt and leverage the resources that we have to be able to adjust to the new normal. Due to the global crisis, meditation classes and ceremonies have been canceled however, the community still continues to meditate and chant Sutras as part of their practice. The free classes allow the students to practice meditation and learn Buddhist principles. Sutra chanting is part of the Buddhist liturgy where one’s karma is purified and a way to dedicate our merits to all sentient beings. The practitioners are using a manual card and prayer beads to keep track of their total chants. These total counts per person are consolidated by the organization as they have a certain goal to achieve. By chanting, we dedicate the merits to world peace and wish for everyone to be free from suffering. This project aims to focus on the individual users to help them track their chant counts and meditation minutes. A collection of Sutras and Gathas for readings that are portable is also beneficial. For better quality results and fast development, Agile methodology was used. Since it is an iterative and incremental development approach, it reduces the risk for possible issues and at the end of each sprint, there is an application ready to be tested and presented. As a result, the mobile application was well designed and coded and has undergone several quality assurance tests to assure the excellence of the application. Overall, the meditation guide and chanting tracker mobile application has solved the issue of the manual approach and encourages the practitioner even more to practice mindfulness through chanting and meditation. A recommended additional feature to the application would be a function to be able to download a backup of the user data so that it can be restored if the app has been reinstalled.

In the thesis "Awaken the Bodhi Mind: A Meditation Guide and Chanting Tracker Mobile Application," Maria Carina Z. Santos addresses the challenges Buddhist practitioners faced during the global pandemic when face-to-face ceremonies were restricted. The study identifies that manual tracking methods, such as prayer beads and physical cards, were inefficient for both individuals and supporting non-profit organizations. Specifically, there was a lack of a streamlined digital system for tracking meditation and chanting, as well as a need for portable access to Buddhist teachings.

To solve these issues, the author developed a mobile application using the Agile methodology, which involved four 30-day sprints. The app was built using the Flutter framework and Dart for Android, utilizing the Hive NoSQL database for local data management. Designed with a demographic of practitioners aged 40 to 60 in mind, the application emphasizes simplicity and intuitive navigation. Key features include a meditation timer, a daily and overall chant counter with automatic saving, a visualization graph for meditation minutes, and a digital library containing Zen teachings, ceremony information, and class listings.

User Acceptance Testing yielded highly positive results, with all functional specifications successful and no performance bugs identified. The study concludes that the application effectively provides an automated, offline resource to simplify spiritual practice management. Future recommendations include adding data backup, user profiles, and audio assets.

The project underwent rigorous assessment through user testing. The author conducted one-on-one discussions with a diverse group of testers across various age brackets and technical skill levels. Testing was performed using an APK (Android Package) file to ensure the application functioned correctly in a pre-release state. The results of the User Acceptance Testing (UAT) were highly positive, with all functional test specifications yielding successful outcomes. No bugs were identified during the UAT regarding performance or loading times; instead, user feedback focused on aesthetic preferences and minor UI enhancements, such as color gradients and the addition of a profile page.

The study concludes that the "Awaken the Bodhi Mind" application successfully provides an automated, offline resource that simplifies the management of chanting records and the study of Buddhist teachings. The application offers convenience by systematically storing data and provides a portable way for practitioners to engage with their faith. The author notes that the project demonstrates how technology can be leveraged to maintain spiritual practices during periods of social restriction.

The implications of this work suggest that specialized, lightweight mobile applications can effectively serve niche religious or community-based needs by replacing inefficient manual processes. By using cross-platform tools like Flutter, developers can create highly customized tools that are accessible to specific demographics. For future development, the author recommends several enhancements, categorized by priority. High-priority features include the implementation of a data backup and restore function to prevent data loss during reinstallation, the creation of user profiles, and a dedicated settings page. Medium-priority improvements involve redesigning the user interface to replace the hamburger menu with bottom navigation, while low-priority goals include adding audio assets and daily motivational quotes to increase user engagement.

title: 1KYUSI: A Centralized Web-Based Information Management System for the Local Government Of Quezon City
abstract:
This paper aims to design and develop a centralized web-based management information system for efficient and accessible recordkeeping that will in turn, improve the delivery of basic social services by the local government units and their preparedness for disaster response.

1Kyusi will therefore serve as the data bank of every person residing in every barangay in Quezon City. The system aims to have an updated record of every individual but still adheres to Republic Act 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.

1Kyusi will greatly impact the project initiatives and disaster response of the Quezon City local government through its implementation at the barangay level under the management of the local government.

Simbulan addresses the critical need for modernized, real-time data management within local government units (LGUs). The author identifies a significant problem in how city governments and barangays collect, update, and manage constituent data. Currently, much of this information relies on national census data from the Philippine Statistics Authority, which is only updated every four to five years. This lack of real-time, centralized data creates significant hurdles for the efficient delivery of social services, the distribution of relief goods, and the implementation of cash aid programs. These deficiencies were acutely highlighted during the COVID-19 pandemic, where the absence of digitized, up-to-date records led to delays in disaster response and social amelioration programs, causing public dissatisfaction and logistical confusion.

While some local governments have begun digitalizing records, many still rely on manual, paper-based processes or fragmented digital files like Excel and Word. This fragmentation means that data collected at the barangay level is often not integrated with the city government's database, leading to redundant data entry and inefficient service delivery. The author notes that while the Quezon City government has launched the QCitizen ID, the 1Kyusi project offers a distinct approach by focusing on a mandated, bottom-up data collection method where barangay officials conduct house-to-house censuses to ensure the legitimacy and accuracy of the information.

The theoretical framework for the study is the Adaptive Structuration Theory (AST), which emphasizes the social aspects of technology use and how organizational groups perceive and apply information systems to their specific activities. The system utilizes data warehouse modeling and predictive analytics through machine learning to help the LGU forecast the needs of its constituents based on demographic trends.

The findings from the project's development and testing phases are positive. The system underwent User Acceptance Testing (UAT) using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) with a diverse group of ten respondents. The results indicated that the system is perceived as both useful and easy to use across various demographics. While the participants generally agreed on the system's effectiveness, the study did find that the "movement tracker" feature caused some confusion regarding its design, with testers suggesting the use of graphs or charts to make the data more intuitive. The implementation of such a system allows the LGU to move away from outdated, manual processes toward a data-driven approach to governance.

title: Chemical Inventory System for Chemistry Department of Liberal Arts College
abstract:
Within the Chemistry department of a given liberal arts college in the US, chemical inventory has been managed through a traditionally manual process using spreadsheets and documents that quickly became unstructured, inefficient, and disorganized. As such, this project aimed for the development of a custom-built, open-source, web-based Chemical inventory system. This project has been intended to
help streamline the client’s chemical management process and migrate physical or paper-based data into a more efficient and structured digital environment. This project also intended to serve as a pioneer in IT modernization initiatives through increased adoption of software-based solutions within the department.

The proposed system has been developed using a distributed logical architecture consisting of separate front-end (web), back-end (application), and database (data) layers. The front-end has been built as a Single Page Application (SPA) using Angular/Typescript. The back-end has been built as a Java Spring Boot web services application with various RESTful API endpoints for serving and accepting structured JSON data. The relational database has been built using PostgreSQL. System components have been deployed and hosted on the Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud infrastructure.

Commercial software was deemed unsuitable due to outdated interfaces and a lack of customization.

two:
The thesis titled "Chemical Inventory System for Chemistry Department of Liberal Arts College" by Michael Anthony V. Ygnacio addresses the inefficiencies inherent in manual chemical management within an academic setting. The research focuses on developing a custom, web-based solution to replace outdated, disorganized, and manual workflows used by professors, laboratory assistants, and students.

**Problem**
The Chemistry department at the client's institution lacked a dedicated software system for managing chemical inventories. Instead, staff relied on manual processes involving Excel spreadsheets, Word documents, and physical notes to track the ordering, delivery, storage, consumption, and disposal of chemicals. This manual approach led to several critical issues: the duplication and disconnection of information across different users, loss of data due to missed manual updates, and the creation of multiple conflicting document versions. Furthermore, the lack of a structured format made analysis and reporting difficult. The client also noted that previous commercial software solutions were unsuitable due to outdated user interfaces, cumbersome navigation, external dependencies for barcode generation, and a lack of customization.

**Context**
The project is situated within a liberal arts college in South Carolina, USA. Unlike large research universities, liberal arts colleges often operate with limited budgets and lower institutional priority for specialized software-based solutions. This financial and priority constraint necessitated a solution that was both cost-effective and highly functional. The client, a Chemistry Professor with a Ph.D., sought a system that could modernize the department's IT infrastructure while addressing specific pain points experienced with previous commercial products.

**Method**
The developer utilized the Kanban framework to manage the project, which allowed for an iterative, flexible, and transparent development process. This methodology facilitated continuous collaboration with the client through regular demos, testing, and feedback loops. The system was designed using a distributed logical architecture consisting of a front-end (Single Page Application), a back-end (web services), and a relational database. 

The technology stack included Angular and TypeScript for the front-end, Java with Spring Boot for the back-end RESTful APIs, and PostgreSQL for the database. The system was deployed on Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud infrastructure. To manage costs, the developer transitioned from a complex, multi-server proof-of-concept architecture to a more streamlined, single EC2 server deployment. The developer also adhered to industry best practices, including Object-Oriented Analysis and Design (OOAD), the "Don't Repeat Yourself" (DRY) principle, and the implementation of security measures such as JWT (JSON Web Tokens) and SSL/TLS encryption via Let's Encrypt.

**Findings**
The developed system successfully implemented core inventory functions alongside several "special features" not found in the client's previous alternatives. These features included web notifications for low inventory and audits, integrated barcode printing and scanning, an inventory dashboard for visual metrics, and CAS registry integration for looking up chemical information via public APIs.

Usability testing was conducted with five professionals from the Chemistry and IT industries. The system achieved a mean System Usability Scale (SUS) score of 85.5, which is interpreted as "usable" and above average. The results indicated that users with a chemistry background could interact with the system without difficulty, even without formal instructions. The client and another professor confirmed the successful adoption of the system for their laboratory workflows.

**Conclusions**
The project demonstrates that a custom-built, open-source, web-based system can effectively modernize chemical management in resource-constrained academic environments. The use of the Kanban framework was instrumental in delivering the project within a tight schedule and limited resources. The research highlights that while commercial software exists, custom development allows for specific feature integration (like CAS lookup and integrated barcode management) and significant cost control. However, the study also concludes that cost remains a primary driver in architectural decisions, necessitating trade-offs between high-level scalability and long-term affordability.

**Implications**
The project serves as a pioneer for IT modernization within the department, proving that software-based solutions can increase work efficiency and productivity. For other small-scale academic institutions, the study implies that leveraging cloud infrastructure (AWS) and open-source frameworks can provide a high-quality, professional-grade solution without the prohibitive costs of commercial enterprise software. Future work suggested by the author includes enhancing the system with automated image-based container recognition, more advanced reporting (such as consumption patterns), and more robust user management and security layers.

title: Content-based Original Pilipino Music (OPM) Recommender System Centered on Mood
abstract:
Recommender systems have become increasingly relevant due to the userfocused service delivery of streaming giants like Netflix and Spotify. Systems like this make it possible to offer media content that is highly similar to a user's preference and, if available, streaming history. Despite the availability of these enterprise recommender systems, recommendations are very global and general, requiring highly technical proficiency before one can use the technology to get recommendations for a very narrow genre like Original Pilipino Music (OPM).

This special project proposes a web-based recommender system using content-based filtering to recommend Original Pilipino Music (OPM) to music based on their mood, with recommendations subject to the user's input (e.g. is this song happy or sad?) that will be considered in the final recommendation. This project will also leverage audio content features available from the Spotify database for the model training part of the recommender system. 

Both objective and subjective evaluations of the implemented recommender system are scoped down to the available audio features of available OPM or Filipino songs on the Spotify Database. While this project concurs with the findings of many researchers that music
based solely on audio content or features does not provide very accurate recommendations, this project is a good minimum viable product (MVP) for music enthusiasts. Furthermore, the project is also proof of concept for a more robust OPM recommender system in the future, as detailed in the results and recommendations.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
Jimson M. Sulit’s capstone project, "Content-based Original Pilipino Music (OPM) Recommender System Centered on Mood," addresses the visibility challenges faced by local Filipino music on major streaming platforms. Current enterprise-level systems rely heavily on collaborative filtering, which creates a "cold start" problem for new or niche OPM artists who lack extensive listening history. These algorithms often prioritize Western music and fail to incorporate subjective emotional responses.

To address this, the project proposes a web-based system utilizing content-based filtering, which relies on the inherent properties of the music rather than user interaction data. The system uses a K-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) algorithm to group songs based on six audio features: acousticness, danceability, energy, instrumentalness, valence, and tempo. To incorporate mood, the author engineered a "mood label value" by calculating the product of energy and valence, creating a scale from "Saddest" to "Happiest."

Technical findings confirmed a visibility gap, revealing that OPM artists comprise only approximately 20.16% of the Spotify Top 200 in the Philippines. User testing indicated the system is a successful minimum viable product, with testers expressing enthusiasm for discovering indie and hip-hop OPM artists. The author concludes that the system is a functional management information system that satisfies the core requirement of OPM discovery, serving as a proof of concept that content-based filtering can democratize music discovery.

two:
The capstone project titled "Content-based Original Pilipino Music (OPM) Recommender System Centered on Mood" by Jimson M. Sulit addresses the challenges of music discovery within the specific context of the Philippine music market. The author identifies a significant problem regarding the dominance of Western music on major streaming platforms like Spotify and Apple Music. Because these enterprise-level systems rely heavily on collaborative filtering—which uses user-generated metadata and extensive listening histories—they often suffer from a "cold start" problem. This means new or unpopular songs lack the necessary data to be recommended. Furthermore, these systems often fail to cater to specific local markets like OPM and do not allow users to provide subjective input, such as how a song makes them feel, to direct the recommendation process.

The context of the study is framed by the observation that while OPM has garnered billions of streams, it still faces visibility issues compared to global Western hits. The author notes that users are often "boxed" into their existing listening habits by algorithms, making it difficult to discover niche or new local artists. To address this, the project proposes a web-based recommender system that utilizes content-based filtering. Unlike collaborative filtering, content-based methods rely on the inherent properties of the music itself, allowing the system to recommend new or unpopular OPM songs that do not yet have significant user interaction data.

The methodology of the project underwent several iterations based on technical challenges and user feedback. The initial approach intended to use cosine similarity to measure the distance between song features, allowing users to label songs as "happy" or "sad" to train the model. However, due to complexities in manual standardization, vectorization, and deployment issues with Spotify API dependencies, the author pivoted to a more efficient approach. The final method implemented a K-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) algorithm to group songs based on six audio features: acousticness, danceability, energy, instrumentalness, valence, and tempo. To incorporate the "mood" aspect, the author engineered a "mood label value" by calculating the product of energy and valence, creating a scale ranging from "Saddest" to "Happiest." The system was developed using Python, scikit-learn, and Streamlit, with a web interface built using Bootstrap and DevExpress.

The findings of the project are divided into technical results and user feedback. Technically, the k-NN approach successfully categorized songs into mood tiers. Exploratory data analysis revealed that OPM artists only make up approximately 20.16% of the Spotify Top 200 in the Philippines, confirming the visibility gap. The analysis also showed a correlation between song popularity and danceability, and noted that OPM audio features have undergone musical evolutions between 1980 and 2021. User testing results indicated that the system was a successful "minimum viable product" (MVP). Testers expressed enthusiasm for using the tool to discover indie and hip-hop OPM artists. While users found the mood slider helpful, some noted that the nuances in mood transitions were subtle. The project also successfully passed security testing, with no critical vulnerabilities found in the web application.

The author concludes that while the system is not an absolute necessity for all users, it is a functional and operational management information system that satisfies the core requirement of OPM discovery. A significant conclusion of the work is the importance of the software development trade-off: the author chose to deliver a simpler, working system (k-NN) rather than a more complex, unfinished one (cosine similarity). The project serves as a proof of concept that content-based filtering can democratize music discovery for users without premium subscriptions and for artists without established metadata.

The implications of this work are both social and technical. Socially, the project highlights the need for technological interventions to support local music industries and help OPM artists compete with global mainstream content. Technically, the project demonstrates that user-centric input (subjective mood labeling) can supplement automated audio features to create more personalized experiences. The author offers several recommendations for future work, including the development of a more granular classification model that can explicitly label songs with various emotions beyond just happy and sad. Additionally, the author suggests expanding the system to include search functions for similar artists, integration with user listening histories from streaming services, and the creation of personalized dashboards for music analytics. Finally, the study suggests that further research into why OPM artists represent a minority in the Top 200 could provide actionable insights for local artists to increase their streaming success.

title: Online Applicant Tracking System
abstract: Systemantech, Inc, is a small/medium business company committed to providing competent professionals and technology for the improvements of the clients' business. The demand for competent professionals is high due to attrition or new projects that required manpower. Because of this, the monitoring of the applicant from sourcing to deployment is necessary which is currently a big challenge. The company uses different platforms to track the recruitment process. With the use of the existing ticketing tool to track all the movements from sourcing up to deployment, Onedrive to save all the data of the applicants, and Microsoft Excel for the manual creation of reports. There is also a shortage of technical interviewers due to the availability of time. The proposed customized system as agreed by the client to deliver in a given timeframe resolved the mentioned challenges with the following features such as Web Applicant Tracking Portal where the recruiter can add new candidates and track the movement based on the Candidate status from shortlisted up to the employment in a given time. This feature uses an existing OrangeHRM framework and customized the recruitment module to align with the client’s process. Another feature is the Interview Chatbot in which the new candidate experiences on-the-spot initial interviews. It is added under Job Posting Career Site as another way for the candidate to apply with interaction to a virtual agent. It captures not only the candidate data but how the candidate communicates and answers the question honestly. For the Descriptive Analytic Reporting, it can view the summary count of hired candidates. The dashboard shows the subunits percentage based on the organizational structure of the company. The participation of the company through testing of the customized system resulted in a successful implementation. The comments provided show that the system is ready to use and more recommendation for future works. Therefore, this customized system deployed as a new Online Applicant Tracking System for Systemantech, Inc.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
Systemantech, Inc., a small to medium-sized business providing professional technology services, faces significant recruitment and monitoring challenges due to high attrition rates and continuous project demands. The company currently relies on a fragmented process involving a ticketing tool, OneDrive, and manual Excel reports, which creates inefficiencies in tracking and reporting. title: Upgrading of Clark Development Corporation Electronic Records Management System
abstract:
In 2018, Clark Development Corporation (CDC) Records Management Division (RMD) implemented the Clark Development Corporation Electronic Records Management System (CDC-eRMS). The CDC-eRMS’s objective was to automate some of the processes of RMD. For over 2 years of the system being implemented, RMD received some feedback and suggestions from the management and end-users. To address these, an upgrade to the existing system is needed. 

This project is going to bring new features to the existing system such as customized GUI, streamlined workflow, notification through multiple communication channels, monitoring/tracking module and reporting dashboard. With these new features, CDCeRMS effectiveness is going to improve. The development of this project is done using a rapid development style of methodology which focuses on rapidly developing high quality software that meets the requirements of the users. One of the limitations of the system is that the system is dependent on the old system, so customization and adding of new features may become impossible or hard to implement in the future, especially if the current administrator of the system would leave without proper documentation of the system. 

After the implementation of the proposed system, the feedback from the users has been good, especially the usability and simplicity of the system. With this feedback, the objective of the proposed system was met with satisfaction

This project aimed to transition the system from a basic automated state to a more robust, user-centric platform.

Using a rapid development methodology, the author integrated new functionalities into the existing framework. The upgrade introduced several features to enhance operational efficiency and user experience, including a customized Graphical User Interface (GUI), streamlined workflows, and a notification system utilizing multiple communication channels. Additionally, the upgrade incorporated a monitoring and tracking module for record oversight and a reporting dashboard for data visualization and management oversight.

Findings indicate that these features successfully improved the effectiveness of the CDC-eRMS. User feedback was overwhelmingly positive, specifically highlighting the system's usability and simplicity. Consequently, the project met its objectives. However, the study identifies technical and institutional limitations. Architecturally, the new system remains dependent on the original, older system, which creates risks for future development and customization. Furthermore, there is a risk regarding institutional knowledge; if the current system administrator leaves without providing proper documentation, the ability to maintain or evolve the software would be severely compromised.

title: Electronic Document Management And Tracking System
abstract:
The PhilHealth Regional Office of National Capital Region (PRO NCR) is an office under the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PHIC) that has created and manages the different types of documents internally that disseminates and routed to various offices. Documents such as Advisory, Corporate Office Order, and other pertinent documents are the most common to create and process. Over the year, most of the problems gathered through interviews and personal experience are missing documents, ineffective dissemination, poor tracking, retrieving, and printing documents.

The Electronic Document Management and Tracking System (EDMTS) can manage and transmit various documents. It also centralizes storing information and electronic documents through a web application to quickly retrieve, share, disseminate, and monitor documents' status. 

The web-based system comprises different modules such as user management, location library management, document type, action management, and document management, which can create new documents and route and publish the electronic document.

EDTMS was developed using PHP Laravel framework for the frontend, MySQL to store information, and Apache server as a web application server. As a result, the corporation improved its performance and increased its productivity in managing the documents.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
The PhilHealth Regional Office of National Capital Region (PRO NCR) faces operational challenges regarding internal document management, including missing documents, ineffective dissemination, and poor retrieval processes. Reliance on manual methods like logbooks and spreadsheets leads to excessive search times, while hard copies increase paper waste and procurement costs.

To address these issues, the Electronic Document Management and Tracking System (EDMTS) was developed. This web-based application centralizes the storage, retrieval, sharing, and monitoring of electronic documents. The system features modules for user management, location library management, document type and action management, routing, and document management. It supports five user roles: maintainer, administrator, document creator and publisher, router, and viewer. The system supports scanners and barcode readers to facilitate the encoding and uploading of physical documents.

The project utilized the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to evaluate perceived usefulness and ease of use. Testing included user testing with five personnel and security testing using the OWASP ZAP tool. Findings indicate the EDMTS is highly effective, with a System Usability Scale (SUS) score of 84.5, categorized as "excellent." TAM analysis concluded the system is both useful and easy to use. Implementation successfully transitioned the office toward a digitalized workflow, improving the speed of document movement and providing a centralized, auto-backed-up repository. The EDMTS mitigates the risks of lost documents, enhances productivity, and contributes to environmental sustainability.

The primary problems identified through interviews and personal experience include missing documents due to mishandling or misfiling, ineffective dissemination, and poor tracking and retrieval processes. Manual methods, such as using logbooks, Google Sheets, or Excel files, result in excessive time spent searching for information. Furthermore, the reliance on hard copies leads to high paper waste and increased procurement costs, while the use of email for large files consumes server storage space.

The system is a web-based application designed to centralize the storage, retrieval, sharing, and monitoring of electronic documents. The EDMTS features several modules, including user management, location library management, document type and action management, routing, and document management. It supports five user roles: maintainer, administrator, document creator and publisher, router, and viewer. The system aims to provide a digital paper trail, reduce the need for physical printing through electronic signatures, and improve workflow efficiency by providing immediate notifications to users when documents require action.

The project utilized the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) as its theoretical framework to evaluate the system's perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use. The development followed established system design principles, including the use of database models to reduce redundancy, iterative development, and rapid prototyping. The technical stack for the EDMTS includes the PHP Laravel framework for the frontend, MySQL for data storage, and an Apache server running on Windows Server 2016. The system also supports the use of scanners and barcode readers to facilitate the encoding and uploading of physical documents into the digital repository.

The implementation process involved requirements gathering through stakeholder interviews, followed by prototyping, database design, and iterative coding. The system underwent rigorous testing, including user testing with five personnel and security testing using the OWASP ZAP tool. User testing focused on various functions such as registration, routing, and searching. While some bugs were identified regarding email notifications during the testing phase, regression testing was used to ensure stability after fixes were applied. Security testing revealed several medium to informational priority alerts, such as outdated JavaScript libraries and cookie security issues (HttpOnly and SameSite attributes), which were subsequently addressed.

It also contributes to environmental sustainability and cost reduction by minimizing paper usage and physical storage requirements. title: Access Control Management System
abstract:
Access control management is an essential component of the data center security to ensure that only authorized individuals at allowed visiting times can access data center facilities. Currently, the Data Center Management Division (DCMD) is implementing a paper-based registration process for managing access. With the current process, there are challenges such as maintaining an organized and easily searchable records of the date and time persons have entered the data center. The objective of this project is to streamline the access control registration and management by digitalizing the process of requesting and approving access pass, registering data center visitor information, recording visits, and leasing access cards.

Using the Unified Software Development Process, the web-based Access Control Management System was conceptualized and constructed. In the inception phase, the requirements were gathered through correspondence and interviews with the end-user. In the elaboration phase, the requirements were refined in coordination with the end-user. The use case suite and feature set, along with the project proposal was presented to the end-user. Then, in the construction phase, with iterative implementation, the system was built using PHP and MySQL with the Laravel framework, extending the functionalities with third-party packages and solutions. Lastly, in the transition phase, the system was deployed to a test cloud server.

System functional testing was performed manually using the test case suite. The system was presented to the end-users for their feedback and usability testing. Security testing was also performed using the open-source ZAP software and Qualys SSL Labs. It is concluded that the Access Control Management System is ready  for use of the DCMD, with confidence that the functionalities satisfies the client’s requirements, there is a low risk for cybersecurity attacks, and that the users will have a positive experience in using the system.

half:
The Data Center Management Division faces operational challenges due to a paper-based registration process for managing facility access. This manual system for recording visitor names, signatures, companies, and entry and exit times presents risks such as difficulty in searching records, potential loss of documentation, compromised information, and the physical labor required for maintenance. While an Access Control System using RFID cards exists, the software lacks a dedicated database for managing the leasing of unnamed access cards to visitors, requiring manual registration and deregistration for every visit. Additionally, the existing software is not accessible to front desk guards, forcing continued reliance on manual logbooks.

The objective of this project was to design and develop a web-based Access Control Management System to digitalize and streamline registration and management processes. The system aims to automate requesting and approving access passes, registering visitor and company information, recording visits, and the leasing and returning of access cards. The project utilized the Unified Software Development Process and was built using a client-server model with a Linux-based server, Apache HTTP Server, PHP, and a MySQL database within the Laravel framework. Security was addressed through Role-Based Access Control and TLS/SSL certificates, including digital signatures using x.509v3 certificates.

Functional testing achieved a 100% pass rate across all key features. Security testing using OWASP ZAP initially identified 69 alerts, but after addressing these via Apache and PHP updates, the remaining alerts were acknowledged as low-risk. Usability testing with ten respondents resulted in a System Usability Scale score of 73.5, indicating the system is effective and provides ease of use. The project concludes the system is ready for use, satisfies functional requirements, and maintains low risk for cybersecurity attacks.

The Data Center Management Division (DCMD) faces significant operational challenges due to its reliance on a paper-based registration process for managing access to data center facilities. The current manual system for recording visitor information, including names, signatures, companies, and time of entry and exit, presents several risks. These include the difficulty of searching and sorting through physical records, the potential for losing important documentation, the high probability of compromised information, and the physical labor required to maintain paper logs. Furthermore, while the DCMD has implemented an existing Access Control System using RFID cards, the software lacks a dedicated database for managing the leasing of unnamed access cards to visitors. This limitation necessitates the manual registration and deregistration of visitors for every visit if a per-visit leasing scheme is used. Additionally, the existing software is not accessible to the guards at the front desk, forcing them to continue using manual logbooks.

The objective of this project was to design and develop a web-based Access Control Management System to digitalize and streamline the registration and management processes. The system aims to automate the requesting and approving of access passes, the registration of visitor and company information, the recording of visits, and the leasing and returning of access cards. By providing a digital audit trail and utilizing digital signatures, the project seeks to improve physical security and facilitate a paperless environment. The scope includes computerized registration and monitoring but excludes the configuration of actual access card privileges, which remains handled by the existing hardware-based system.

The project utilized the Unified Software Development Process, moving through inception, elaboration, construction, and transition phases. The system was built using a client-server model, specifically a web-based information system, to allow multiple authorized users to access centralized data from various devices. The technology stack included a Linux-based server, the Apache HTTP Server, PHP, and a MySQL database, organized within the Laravel framework. To ensure security, the developer implemented Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) using the Spatie Laravel-permission package, and utilized TLS/SSL certificates for secure communication. The system also incorporates digital signatures using x.509v3 certificates to ensure integrity and non-repudiation of access requests.

The development followed an iterative approach, transitioning from a waterfall methodology to the Unified Process to accommodate user feedback. The system features several pre-configured roles: Administrator, Registration Officer, Client, DC Manager, and Guard. Key functionalities include user authentication, visitor and company registration, access card management, access pass request and approval, visit recording, card leasing, a calendar view for current visits, and report generation in CSV and Excel formats.

The results of the testing phases demonstrated the system's readiness for deployment. Functional testing achieved a 100% pass rate across all key features, including user authentication, registration, card management, and reporting. Security testing was conducted using OWASP ZAP. An initial scan identified 69 alerts, many of which were related to HTTP headers and information disclosure. After addressing these by updating Apache configurations and PHP settings, the number of alerts was significantly reduced, with the remaining alerts being acknowledged as low-risk. Usability testing was conducted with ten respondents representing various user roles. The system achieved a System Usability Scale (SUS) score of 73.5, which is considered above average and indicates that the system is effective and provides ease of use.

The project concludes that the Access Control Management System is ready for use by the DCMD. The system successfully satisfies the client's functional requirements, maintains a low risk for cybersecurity attacks, and provides a positive user experience. While the system is effective, the study notes that there are opportunities to further strengthen security by reducing information disclosure and to improve usability by increasing user familiarity through training.

Future recommendations include enhancing the dashboards for administrators and managers to include real-time charts and activity overviews. While the current scope excluded integration with the existing hardware-based access control system, future work could explore database connections to achieve this, provided rigorous security testing is conducted to prevent the web system from becoming a gateway for unauthorized access. Additionally, the developer suggests exploring more advanced authentication mechanisms and refining digital signing capabilities, such as allowing signatures to be called directly from a client's keystore or enabling multiple programmatic signatures.

title: Leverage WEBRTC For Online Class
abstract: The proponent started this project during the pandemic, where the face-to- face class is prohibited to prevent the spread of coronavirus (Covid-19). The proponent thinks of a way how to conduct an online conference call that is secured, easy to use, and low-cost solution because currently, the client is using Zoom free-tier that has a limited 40 minutes. When the 40 minutes expired, the students need to connect again in a few minutes but some of the students tend to not enter again to the class thinking that the class is over. The proponent starts using WebRTC as an alternate solution to the Zoom app. Now the clients can now go beyond 40 minutes without interruption in the class.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
In the 2021 Master of Information Systems project "Leverage WEBRTC For Online Class," Jeric G. Cruz addresses logistical challenges in remote learning caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. The research identifies a core problem regarding the limitations of free-tier communication tools, specifically Zoom, which imposes a 40-minute time limit per session. These interruptions caused significant disruption, as students often mistakenly believed classes had concluded when sessions expired, leading to missed instructional time and confusion.

To address the need for a reliable, continuous, and low-cost alternative to subscription-based services, the author utilized WebRTC (Web Real-Time Communication) as the foundational technology. The methodology involved leveraging WebRTC to develop a platform capable of facilitating online conferences without specific time restrictions, ensuring an uninterrupted instructional flow.

The findings demonstrate that the implementation of WebRTC successfully resolved the primary issue of session duration. By moving away from the Zoom free-tier, the client was able to conduct online classes that extended beyond the 40-minute limit. This transition eliminated the need for students to repeatedly reconnect to meetings and prevented the loss of students who previously failed to rejoin sessions. The project proves that WebRTC serves as a viable, low-cost alternative for conducting online classes, providing a stable communication environment that avoids the technical limitations and subscription costs of mainstream conferencing applications.

faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
In the thesis "Alertness and Fatigue Reporting System," Michelle C. Garcia addresses the safety risks posed by fatigue in the aviation industry. While airlines must implement Fatigue Risk Management Systems, many still rely on manual, paper-based processes. In the author's specific case study, flight crews submit paper reports that safety staff must manually encode into spreadsheets, creating data bottlenecks and delays. Furthermore, these manual systems are often limited to flight crews, preventing a holistic view of safety risks that includes ground personnel.

To address these issues, the author developed the Alertness and Fatigue Reporting System (AFRS), a mobile application developed as a Minimum Viable Product (MVP). Built using Flutter and hosted on the Google Cloud Platform with a Firebase backend, the Android application allows users to authenticate via Google Sign-in, submit reports, and view personalized analytics.

The findings demonstrate that the AFRS effectively automates the reporting process and eliminates manual encoding bottlenecks. The application provides users with a personalized dashboard featuring time-series line graphs to track daily alertness scores and pie charts to identify fatigue contributors like stress or overwork. By allowing both flight crews and ground personnel to report experiences directly, the system provides a more comprehensive view of organizational safety risks. The study concludes that transitioning to automated, mobile-based reporting improves the timeliness and accuracy of safety data.

In the thesis "Alertness and Fatigue Reporting System," Michelle C. Garcia addresses the critical need for monitoring employee engagement and mindfulness, particularly within the aviation industry. Fatigue, defined as exhaustion resulting from stress, lack of sleep, or extensive labor, poses significant safety risks in this sector. While airlines are required to implement Fatigue Risk Management Systems (FRMS), many still rely on manual, paper-based processes. In the specific case of the author's airline client, flight crews submit paper reports that must be manually encoded into spreadsheets by safety staff. This creates a bottleneck and causes delays in data availability, especially when crews and back-office staff work different shifts. Furthermore, the current system is limited to flight crews, preventing a holistic view of safety risks that includes ground personnel.

To address these challenges, the author developed the Alertness and Fatigue Reporting System (AFRS), a mobile application designed as a Minimum Viable Product (MVP). The methodology involved the development and implementation of an Android application hosted on the Google Cloud Platform. The technical stack utilized Flutter for cross-platform development, Firebase for the backend, and Google Sign-in for user access. The system follows a client-server model where the Android app communicates with a NoSQL database in the cloud, allowing users to authenticate via Gmail, submit reports, and view personalized analytics.

The findings demonstrate that the AFRS effectively automates the reporting process and eliminates the manual encoding bottleneck. The application provides end-users with a personalized dashboard featuring time-series line graphs to track daily average alertness scores. Additionally, the system includes a pie chart to identify top contributors to fatigue, such as stress, overwork, or poor diet. By aggregating this data, the system provides a more comprehensive view of safety risks by allowing both flight crews and ground personnel to report their experiences directly. This centralized data collection serves as a preliminary step in managing operational risks across the entire organization.

The study concludes that the AFRS MVP successfully demonstrates how a mobile application can improve upon traditional paper-based reporting. By enabling employees to self-report and view their own trends, the system raises individual awareness regarding personal fatigue triggers. However, the author notes that the MVP is a starting point that requires further enhancements and budget approval for hosting and additional features before a wider rollout. The work suggests that transitioning to automated, mobile-based reporting can improve the timeliness and accuracy of safety data in high-stakes industries. For successful implementation, organizations must prepare for the technical and financial requirements of cloud hosting and app distribution.

title: Web-based Internship Management System for Lyceum of the Philippines University - Cavite
abstract:
One of the missions of Lyceum of the Philippines University – Cavite (LPU–Cavite) is to provide equitable access to learning through relevant, innovative, industry-based, and environment-conscious programs and services for their stakeholders. The internship is one of the programs of the University that provides students the opportunity to determine their career goals, apply the knowledge they have acquired from the University, and secure their network and good recommendations before they graduate. Being mentioned how important an internship is, LPU – Cavite is expected to have an efficient procedure and an effective system that could support the program throughout the years. However, it is discovered that the University is using the traditional manual system with the process of the internship.

After a thorough review of the existing procedures, the proponent proposed to apply digital modernization to the current process. A web-based internship management system was developed to eliminate problems that are caused by the manual procedure and provide the client definite solutions and improve the customer service quality that they can offer to their stakeholders. The system aims to bring convenience to the students, create easier communication between the affiliated Host Training Establishments and students, and provide a platform for efficient monitoring of the submitted documents and handling of reports.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
Alyssa Paola A. Pocaan’s thesis, "Web-based Internship Management System for Lyceum of the Philippines University - Cavite," addresses inefficiencies in the manual, paper-based internship processes used by the Center for Career Services and Industry Relations (CCSIR). Since 2014, these manual methods have caused challenges regarding material reproduction, coordination with Host Training Establishments, document storage for accreditation, and student monitoring.

Using an Input-Process-Output framework, the researcher developed a digital solution using PHP, MySQL, HTML, CSS, Javascript, and JQuery. The system was evaluated using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and security testing via OWASP ZAP. Findings show the system is highly effective and user-friendly, earning an SUS score of 87.50, categorized as "Best Imaginable." While users reported high confidence in navigating the interface, security testing identified vulnerabilities such as Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), potential SQL injection, and the need for proper Content-Security-Policy headers.

The study concludes that the web-based system successfully meets stakeholder requirements by providing a centralized platform for communication and documentation, enabling paperless submissions and accurate monitoring. Future improvements suggested include email notifications, mobile responsiveness, and batch uploading. A significant recommendation is the integration of the system with the university's existing grading portal (AIMS). Finally, it is recommended that the University's ICT Department take over system maintenance to ensure long-term stability.

The thesis titled "Web-based Internship Management System for Lyceum of the Philippines University - Cavite" by Alyssa Paola A. Pocaan addresses the inefficiencies inherent in the manual internship management processes at LPU-Cavite. The research focuses on modernizing the operations of the Center for Career Services and Industry Relations (CCSIR) to better serve students, university staff, and Host Training Establishments (HTEs).

**Problem and Context**
The internship program at LPU-Cavite is a vital component of the university's mission to provide industry-based learning, allowing students to apply academic knowledge in professional settings. However, the CCSIR has relied on manual, paper-based processes since its founding in 2014. This traditional approach creates several challenges, including the tedious reproduction of physical materials, difficulties in coordinating with HTEs, and the cumbersome task of storing and organizing large volumes of physical documents for university accreditation. The manual system complicates communication between stakeholders and makes the efficient monitoring of student internship statuses and document submissions difficult for staff.

**Method**
The proponent utilized an Input-Process-Output (IPO) theoretical framework to guide the development of the web-based system. The "Input" phase involved gathering knowledge regarding CCSIR business processes and existing internship templates, alongside specifying software and hardware requirements. The "Process" phase encompassed system design, prototyping, testing, and debugging. The "Output" phase focused on the implementation of the digital solution.

The system was developed using a modern web stack: PHP and MySQL for the database layer, and HTML, CSS, Javascript, and JQuery for the client-side interface. The application layer utilized the HTTP protocol to facilitate secure data transfer. To evaluate the system, the proponent employed the System Usability Scale (SUS), a reliable tool for measuring usability. The evaluation included testing by IT experts, non-IT experts, students, industry partners, and CCSIR staff. Additionally, security testing was conducted using OWASP ZAP to identify potential vulnerabilities such as Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and SQL injection.

**Findings**
The assessment results indicated that the system is highly effective and user-friendly. The overall SUS score was 87.50, which corresponds to an "A+" grade, categorized as "Best Imaginable." Specific findings from the user testing showed that respondents strongly agreed that the system was easy to use, well-integrated, and that they would like to use it frequently. Users reported high levels of confidence in navigating the system and noted that it was not unnecessarily complex.

Security testing revealed some vulnerabilities that required addressing before full deployment. Specifically, the OWASP scan identified risks related to Cross-Site Scripting, a potential SQL injection on one web page, the need for proper Content-Security-Policy headers, the use of an outdated Javascript library, and the need to disable directory browsing.

**Conclusions**
The study concludes that the Web-based Internship Management System provides a user-friendly interface that is easily managed by all intended users. The system successfully meets the requirements provided by the stakeholders and was accepted by target users with high satisfaction regarding its performance, functionality, and ease of use. The digital modernization of the internship process effectively addresses the dilemmas of the manual system by providing a centralized platform for communication and documentation.

**Implications**
The research implies that digital modernization is essential for educational institutions to maintain efficient service delivery and adapt to technological advancements. For LPU-Cavite, the system offers a path toward paperless submissions, streamlined communication, and more accurate monitoring of student progress. 

The proponent suggests several areas for future work and improvement. To enhance user experience, future iterations could include email notifications for application approvals, more detailed address forms, and a mobile-responsive layout for smartphone users. Technical improvements, such as batch uploading for applications and the integration of a modal pop-up dialog box, were also recommended. A significant implication for future research is the potential integration of the system with the university's existing grading portal (AIMS) to allow instructors to input internship grades within the same platform. title: E-BAGAM: Barangay SMS-Based Grievance with Action Team Management System
abstract:
The information system aims to aid the barangay in resolving incidents within the community. The researcher was able to identify the problems within the community that contributes to the unresolved and unreported incidents. One of the problems that were identified as the inability to report an incident due to distance from the Barangay Hall to do it personally, this was addressed through the addition of the SMS feature of e-BAGAM from which it uses a local API that processes the incoming SMS. The problem of the provision of immediate response to the incidents from which could be resolved within the area was also addressed by e-BAGAM through the incident management by assigning the incident to the appropriate Team Leader of the Area. Another feature of the information system is the ability to provide the registered users with the status of their reported incident which is also available on the barangay official's page.

The researcher used the 4+1 approach as a guide in Software Architecture wherein this model focuses on the viewpoint of different stakeholders. The views considered were necessary for the software development from which some were changed a bit to suffice those that are necessary to the information system. The researcher was able to identify Use Case View, Logical View, Data View, and the Development view as the views necessary for e-BAGAM. Using this method the researcher was able to identify those modules and classes that are necessary to the information system from which contributed to its success.

Furthermore, the absence of a tracking mechanism makes it difficult for officials to prioritize incidents by severity and prevents residents from knowing the status of their reported grievances.

To address these issues, the researcher developed an information system designed to record incidents, manage them effectively, and allow for real-time monitoring. A key feature is the integration of an SMS function using a local API, which allows residents to report incidents via text message. The system also includes a cluster-based approach for incident management, where incidents are assigned to appropriate Area Team Leaders based on geographical locations like Purok.

The methodology was guided by the 4+1 software architecture approach. The system was designed with an administrator module for barangay officials and a user module for residents, built as a web-based application. Final usability surveys showed significant improvement, with respondents rating the system in the range of 87.5 to 95. The study concludes that E-BAGAM is an effective tool for improving service delivery. It allows administrators to manage grievances through statuses such as Newly Received Grievance, Pending Grievance, and Closed Grievance, while providing transparency by allowing residents to monitor their reported incidents.

The E-BAGAM system was developed to address significant challenges in incident reporting and management within the barangay, specifically focusing on Barangay Irisan. The researcher identified several critical problems that contribute to unreported and unresolved incidents. One primary issue is the physical distance between residents and the Barangay Hall, which prevents some community members from reporting incidents in person due to the cost and effort involved. Additionally, the barangay lacks a dedicated information system, relying instead on manual methods such as encoding data into computer files or writing in logbooks. This manual process, combined with a lack of internet connectivity and reliance on the personal mobile load of officials, hinders the ability to provide immediate responses. Furthermore, the absence of a tracking mechanism makes it difficult for officials to prioritize incidents by severity and prevents residents from knowing the status of their reported grievances.

To address these issues, the researcher developed an information system designed to bridge the gap between community members and officials. The system aims to record incidents, manage them effectively, and allow for real-time monitoring by administrators and residents. A key feature is the integration of an SMS function using a local API, which allows residents to report incidents via text message. This feature is specifically intended to cater to those living far from the Barangay Hall and those without reliable internet access. The system also includes a cluster-based approach for incident management, inspired by Japan's Cluster-Based Development, where incidents are assigned to appropriate Area Team Leaders based on geographical locations like Purok.

The methodology employed for the development of E-BAGAM was guided by the 4+1 software architecture approach. This model allowed the researcher to consider the viewpoints of various stakeholders through several specific views: the Use Case View to describe scenarios and actor interactions, the Logical View to define functional requirements and the object model, the Data View to describe data flow and persistence, and the Development View to map the software onto the hardware. The system was designed with two primary modules: an administrator module for barangay officials and a user module for residents. The system was built using a web-based application running on a localhost environment, utilizing a stack that includes Apache, MySQL, PHP, HTML, CSS, and Bootstrap.

The findings from the development and testing phases indicate that the system successfully meets the needs of the stakeholders. During the development process, the researcher conducted interviews with barangay officials and residents. Officials expressed satisfaction with the SMS feature as a cost-efficient way to improve service delivery, while residents emphasized the need to monitor the status of their reports. Initial usability assessments using the usability scale yielded relatively low scores, prompting the researcher to revise the prototype from a Windows form to a web-based application. Following these revisions, final usability surveys showed significant improvement, with respondents rating the system in the range of 87.5 to 95, indicating they were ready to use the system.

The study concludes that E-BAGAM is an effective tool for improving service delivery within the barangay. By providing an SMS-based reporting feature, the system ensures that incidents are recorded regardless of the distance of the resident from the Barangay Hall. The system allows administrators to manage grievances through various statuses: Newly Received Grievance, Pending Grievance, and Closed Grievance. It also provides a security feature by including timestamps in the edit history of incidents. The system successfully enables residents to monitor their reported incidents and see which official is acting upon them, thereby increasing transparency and engagement.

Based on the results, several implications and recommendations for future work are identified. The system demonstrates how localized technology, such as SMS APIs, can be leveraged to overcome infrastructure limitations like a lack of internet connectivity. To further enhance the system, the researcher recommends adding the ability for the system to reply to incoming SMS messages and implementing a notification system to alert users when their inquiry status is updated. Other proposed improvements include the inclusion of pre-formatted forms for incident reporting, the development of a web-based API for other barangays with internet access, and further enhancements to the web user interface.

title: Digital Contact Tracing to Slow Down Disease Transmission
abstract:
This Covid-19 pandemic has severely affected everyone around the world. During its infancy, no one thought that it would grow in this magnitude. Although there are a few countries that have now managed its spread, most of the countries are still struggling to contain it and flatten the curve. This is not the first time that a pandemic like this has happened and it definitely would not be the last. Aside from awareness of the disease and following strict self-quarantine, contact tracing is an important part of the strategy to minimize the risk of spreading the infection.

The objective of this project is to improve the methods for contact tracing and quicker data analysis for better decision-making when it comes to containing the disease. An important aspect to consider as well is the quick dissemination of information from a reliable and trusted source. The output is a web application that allows establishments to track the public who visits their establishments while health facilities are responsible for updating the public’s status when it comes to having the disease. This then allows the administrators to have the information they need for contact tracing such as a possible disease carrier’s whereabouts and trace those who may have been exposed.

The development of the project started with analysis of the current situation such as how contact tracing is done, who is trying to solve the problem and what are the alternatives available to solve this problem. A design was made based on the problems identified. During the development stage, each module was built and tested separately and as a whole. Automated testing was done for functionalities while usability was tested by asking a group of test users to try the application and answer some questions and rate their experience. Evaluation of feedback from test users show that the application is simple to use even for non-technical people and that features available for them are working properly. Future work for this project will be to automate notifications for users who gets exposed and to add GIS features for better data analysis.

Furthermore, existing digital alternatives often require high-specification devices or private management, which can undermine public trust. The author argues that digital technologies can help flatten the curve through faster data analysis and more efficient tracking of exposures.

To address these challenges, the author developed a platform-independent Progressive Web Application (PWA) using the Django web framework and a MySQL database. The system utilizes a Model-View-Template architecture and includes four user roles: Visitors, Establishments, Health Facilities, and Administrators. This PWA approach allows the application to function like a native app without requiring app store downloads or high-end hardware.

Project assessment findings indicate the application is functional and user-friendly. Automated unit testing achieved a 100% passing rate, and manual usability testing yielded a System Usability Scale rating of over 90%. Testing confirmed the system successfully manages registration, QR code generation, visit recording, status updates, and push notifications for Android users. The author concludes that a web-based application is a viable alternative to traditional mobile apps because it overcomes device compatibility barriers and addresses privacy concerns through centralized control. two:
The thesis "Digital Contact Tracing to Slow Down Disease Transmission" by Michael V. Torres addresses the critical need for efficient disease containment strategies, specifically focusing on the limitations of manual contact tracing during the COVID-19 pandemic. The author identifies a significant problem in the current approach to contact tracing, noting that many countries rely on manual methods, such as asking patients to recall every location they visited. This process is slow, prone to human error, and lacks real-time data capabilities. Furthermore, existing digital alternatives often present challenges, such as requiring high-specification mobile devices or being managed by private entities rather than government agencies, which raises concerns regarding data privacy and public trust.

The context of this research is the global COVID-19 pandemic, which disrupted economies and overwhelmed healthcare systems. The author argues that while no country was fully prepared for such an event, the implementation of digital technologies can significantly increase the probability of "flattening the curve" by providing quicker data analysis and more efficient tracking of disease carriers and their exposures.

To address these issues, the author developed a Progressive Web Application (PWA) designed to be platform-independent and accessible to users with older mobile devices. The method involved a structured development process starting with an analysis of current contact tracing methods and existing technological alternatives. The system design utilizes a Model-View-Template (MVT) architecture via the Django web framework. The proposed system includes several distinct user roles: Visitors, who register once to generate a unique QR code; Establishments, who scan these QR codes to record visits; Health Facilities, who update a visitor's health status; and Administrators, who oversee the system and perform data analysis. The technical stack includes Python for server-side scripting, JavaScript for frontend functionality, and a MySQL database for production. The PWA approach was specifically chosen to allow the application to function like a native mobile app—including having a home screen icon—without requiring users to download it from an app store or possess high-end hardware.

The findings from the project assessment indicate that the application is both functional and user-friendly. The author conducted multiple stages of testing, including automated unit testing for models, URLs, and views, as well as manual usability testing. The automated tests achieved a 100% passing rate for all functionalities. Usability testing, conducted with ten respondents using the System Usability Scale, yielded a rating of over 90%. The results showed that 70% of users found the application to be at a "Professional" level of technical proficiency, and 70% rated its user-friendliness as "Excellent." While one user found the system complex, this was noted as an outlier. The testing confirmed that the system successfully handles registration, QR code generation, visit recording, status updates, and push notifications (for Android users).

The conclusions drawn from this work emphasize that a platform-independent, web-based application offers a viable alternative to traditional mobile apps. By utilizing PWA technology, the system overcomes the barrier of device compatibility, which is a major hurdle for widespread adoption. The author concludes that the ability to provide data through an API allows for better integration with other software, and the centralized control by a government agency (rather than a private company) addresses significant privacy concerns. The project demonstrates that digital tools, when designed for simplicity and accessibility, can significantly improve the speed and accuracy of contact tracing.

The implications of this research suggest that future pandemic responses should prioritize technologies that ensure high adoption rates through simplicity and low hardware requirements. The author recommends that to maintain public trust, no private entity should act as the sole custodian of sensitive health data; instead, government agencies should manage the information. Furthermore, the research implies that the modular nature of the system—specifically the inclusion of an API—allows for scalability and integration into broader public health infrastructures.

For future work, the author proposes several enhancements to increase the system's utility. These include the integration of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to provide better spatial data analysis and the implementation of automated notifications for exposed users. The author also notes that while web push notifications are currently limited on iOS, future platform updates could enable real-time notifications for all users. Finally, the author suggests incorporating disaster recovery and resilience planning by migrating the application to major cloud service providers to ensure stability during large-scale public health crises.

title: SSS Member Personalized Inquiry Chatbot System
abstract:

Employees in the Member Communications and Assistance Department is having a hard time dealing resulting in overtime and shifting schedules. Realizing this, the study has created a system to cater massive inquiries of members.
