two:
The Social Security System (SSS) is a government agency in the Philippines providing essential financial services, including loans and benefits for sickness, maternity, disability, death, and retirement. With approximately 50 million registered members, the agency faces a significant challenge regarding information dissemination. The core problem identified is the overwhelming volume of inquiries and complaints from members regarding application requirements, status updates, and benefit amounts. This high volume of repetitive questions places a heavy burden on the Member Communications and Assistance Department (MCAD), where employees must manage inquiries through hotlines, email, and Facebook. This workload frequently necessitates overtime and shifting schedules to meet quotas, creating an inefficient cycle where the volume of incoming inquiries often exceeds the capacity of human staff to respond promptly.

To address these challenges, the study developed the Social Security System – Member Personalized Inquiry Chatbot System (SSS-MPICS). The context of the project is rooted in the need for a more efficient, cost-effective, and scalable communication tool. While SSS currently utilizes official Facebook pages and email services, these methods rely heavily on manual human intervention. The proposed chatbot aims to leverage modern conversational AI to provide 24/7 automated support, allowing members to receive immediate, accurate responses to frequently asked questions regarding their contributions, salary loans, benefits, and eligibility.

The methodology employed for this project was the Agile Scrum framework. This iterative approach allowed the development team to manage the project through successive sprints, typically lasting 30 days, where features and bug fixes were prioritized in a product backlog. The technical architecture of SSS-MPICS is built upon several key technologies. The application layer utilizes Node.js for its event-driven, non-blocking I/O model, which is essential for the AI server to fetch incoming chats. Dialogflow serves as the chatbot platform and AI server, using intents and entities to understand and parse user requests. Facebook Messenger acts as the client layer, providing the interface for members to interact with the bot. To ensure security and data privacy, the system implements two-factor authentication via a One-Time Password (OTP) sent through the Twilio API. The data layer relies on a MySQL database to store and retrieve member information, and Heroku was used as the cloud platform for deployment and user acceptance testing.

The findings from the implementation and testing phases indicate that the SSS-MPICS is a highly effective solution. During user acceptance testing, the system demonstrated high precision in its responses. Users reported positive feedback, particularly regarding the "quick replies" feature, which allows them to navigate inquiries by simply tapping options rather than typing complex queries. The testing results showed that the chatbot successfully fulfilled its objective of providing prompt and accurate responses. Furthermore, the implementation of the chatbot has had a direct positive impact on organizational productivity. By automating the responses to mundane and repetitive inquiries, the system has relieved the workload of the MCAD employees, allowing them to meet their quotas without the need for excessive overtime. This shift has improved the work-life balance of the staff while increasing the overall efficiency of the department.

In conclusion, the SSS-MPICS successfully demonstrates how chatbot technology can be leveraged to improve public service delivery. The integration of Dialogflow, Twilio, and Facebook Messenger created a seamless communication channel that is more cost-effective than traditional manual methods. The project achieved its primary goal of reducing the burden on SSS employees and providing members with a fast, reliable way to access their personal information. The study proves that automating routine inquiries through an intelligent, personalized system can significantly enhance the operational capacity of a large-scale government agency.

The implications of this study suggest that as SSS continues to evolve and introduce new benefits or financial assistance programs, the chatbot must also adapt. Future work should focus on upgrading the system to include a wider range of services and potentially incorporating language selection to cater to different dialects or overseas Filipino workers. There is also an opportunity to further optimize the system to achieve more human-like interactions. As the chatbot industry continues to advance, the SSS-MPICS will require continuous updates to remain compatible with new trends and the expanding service offerings of the Social Security System.

title: Certificate of Land Ownership Awards Information System (CLOA-IS) with LDIS Status Prediction Tool using Decision Tree Algorithm for the Department of Agrarian Reform Province of Iloilo
abstract:
In every agency in the government, there has always been a need to improve access to the information available intended solely for the public in a more electronic way. With the advancement of information and communications technology in a developing country, like the Philippines, the government should take advantage of upgrading the traditional manual approach with regard to its record-keeping systems. The Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) 1151 is the lead government agency that upholds and implements comprehensive and genuine agrarian reform towards the improvement of the quality of life of its beneficiaries. Due to lack of a more automated method from the department's end, doing tasks such as card indexing and encoding to excel files in a client-oriented setup can sometimes be time-consuming and difficult in a sense that employees tend to be unsystematic. To carry out most of the work, the researcher developed the Certificate of Land Ownership Awards Information System (CLOA-1S) with Land Distribution Information Schedule (LDIS) Status Prediction Tool Using Decision Tree Algorithm, a database management system for the use of the DAR - lloilo Provincial Office. Through the system, retrieval of CLOA 1151 title's current status, as well as generation of accurate reports, are now attainable. CLOA-IS is needed to subsist the day to day survival of the department and to cut administration costs as it increases mobility and productivity - that is, to accomplish certain tasks, employees from different municipalities are no longer curbed to walls of the Provincial Office because they can access desired information from anywhere. Given that, the system helped reduce the amount of time on unnecessary errands, which makes the department operate more efficiently and improve client communications.

Furthermore, the LOIS Prediction Tool feature has provided the management with an analysis on which of the CLOA Titles registered in the system are ready for LOIS processing by analyzing input data such as the LOIS documentary requirements. LOIS is needed for the agrarian reform beneficiaries to pay their amortization to the Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP) and to claim their CLOA Titles. 

Using the System Usability Scale (SUS), expected users categorized as IT Expert and DAR Employee assessed the system. The test provides an at-a-glance snapshot of how usable or unusable the system is. After the evaluation, it is noteworthy to highlight that the SUS interpretation for the SUS result of CLOA-IS with LOIS Prediction Tool is Graded "A" with an adjectival rating of "Excellent/' Acceptability as "Acceptable" and Net Promoter Score as "Promoter." Thus, this special project concluded that the significant goals attained had enabled faster traceability, minimize inconsistencies, and provide satisfactory services to the clients of DAR-ILOILO as well as to the end-users of the system.

title: Artscience, cultural policy, and epistemological empathy: Towards imaginaries of the future as a new commons in the Philippines
abstract: Who gets to imagine the future? In the Philippines, there is a governance gap surrounding this question: government agencies for science, technology, and trade drive discussion of the future around innovation, growth, and "creative industries", while the agencies for culture and the arts are mandated to focus on the past and on culture as heritage. Drawing on Justin O'Connor's proposition that culture is neither a luxury or an industry, but a foundational capability—one that equips citizens to participate in shared meaning-making and democratic decision-making, this talk argues that there is a potential for science institutions to be "safe spaces" where democratic futures are co-imagined, through artscience practiced on equal footing with cultural workers and artists.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
Diego S. Maranan identifies a systemic governance gap in the Philippines regarding the collective imagination of the future. A disconnect exists between agencies driving science and economic growth and those focused on heritage preservation and decolonial recovery. Consequently, cultural governance is absent from national foresight, and foresight is absent from cultural governance. This issue is compounded by the nation's socio-economic and environmental realities, which necessitate resilient futures-making. Current strategic documents either ignore culture entirely or reduce it to economic utility for exports. Furthermore, the Philippines lacks investment in cultural institutions as national infrastructure, as its prominent science-focused museum is a private entity.

To address these gaps, Maranan proposes cultivating "epistemological empathy" between artists and scientists, treating both as intellectual equals and partners. This approach moves beyond a "consultant and client" relationship toward co-authoring preferable futures. Maranan illustrates this through Space Ecologies Art and Design (SEADS) projects, such as *Continuum*, *Biomodd*, *Seeker*, and *Engines of Eternity*. These works demonstrate that when artists and scientists work as equals, they produce frameworks for imagining futures that neither could generate in isolation. Maranan argues that science institutions can serve as "third spaces" for this work. He advocates for dedicated resources where diverse practitioners can convene as equal partners to achieve a model of genuine co-governance, where culture serves as a foundational capability for democratic decision-making and collective co-imagination.

The presentation by Diego S. Maranan addresses a critical governance gap in the Philippines regarding the collective imagination of the future. Maranan identifies a systemic disconnect between the agencies responsible for science, technology, and economic growth and those responsible for culture and the arts. In the Philippine context, science and economic agencies drive discussions of the future through the lenses of innovation, growth, and "creative industries." Conversely, cultural agencies are primarily mandated to focus on the past, specifically through heritage preservation and decolonial recovery. This creates a dual problem: cultural governance is absent from national foresight, and foresight is absent from cultural governance.

The context of this problem is rooted in the specific socio-economic and environmental realities of the Philippines. As a lower-middle-income country prone to frequent natural disasters—such as typhoons, earthquakes, and volcanic eruptions—the nation faces cascading risks that require collective, resilient, and equitable futures-making. Maranan notes that while international bodies like UNESCO recognize the ability to imagine futures as a learnable and distributable capability, the Philippines lacks a national cultural futures strategy. Current strategic documents, such as PAGTANAW 2050, focus on science and technology without mentioning arts or culture, while the Creative Industries Development Plan reduces culture to its economic utility for exports and job creation. Furthermore, unlike countries such as Singapore or Brazil, which invest in cultural institutions as national infrastructure for public futures-making, the Philippines' prominent science-focused museum is a private entity that must sustain itself through ticket sales and sponsorship.

To address these gaps, Maranan proposes the cultivation of "epistemological empathy" between artists and scientists. This concept goes beyond mere appreciation of different disciplines; it involves treating artists and scientists as genuine intellectual equals and epistemological partners. By leveraging their shared commitments to discovery, experimentation, risk-taking, and curiosity, these disciplines can move beyond a "consultant and client" relationship to co-author possible and preferable futures.

Maranan illustrates the potential of this artscience approach through several projects initiated by Space Ecologies Art and Design (SEADS). These projects serve as practical examples of how interdisciplinary collaboration can generate new ways of knowing. *Continuum* is a kinetic sculpture that uses gears to make the passage of vast stretches of time palpable, helping audiences reflect on their place in the universe. *Biomodd* uses computer technology and upcycled components to create symbiotic ecosystems where plants and electronics co-evolve, fostering "systems literacy" regarding the relationship between technology and nature. *Seeker* involves participatory art where communities design and inhabit experimental, DIY starship habitats, serving as a laboratory for learning how to negotiate resources and social rituals in a "prototyped future." Finally, *Engines of Eternity* collaborated with space biologists to explore the philosophical dimensions of deep space settlement by using genomic data from rotifers on the International Space Station to create data visualizations and video essays.

The findings from these artistic endeavors suggest that when artists and scientists work as equals, they produce frameworks for imagining futures that neither discipline could generate in isolation. These collaborations move beyond intellectual inquiry to create profound, affective, and visceral responses in participants, helping individuals navigate their relationship with the universe and their role within complex systems.

In conclusion, Maranan argues that science institutions—which already possess foresight mandates, research infrastructure, and policy legitimacy—offer a unique opportunity to serve as "safe spaces" or "third spaces" for this work. He advocates for the creation of dedicated institutional resources where artists, scientists, designers, and cultural workers can convene as equal partners. The ultimate goal is to move toward a model of genuine co-governance, where culture is not merely a tool for economic growth or a relic of the past, but a foundational capability for democratic decision-making and the collective co-imagination of a shared future.

title: Filipino Muslims' Representations in K to 12 Basic Education Social Studies Textbooks (2016-2022)
abstract: This study examines how Filipino Muslims are represented in Social Studies textbooks and evaluates their alignment with the “Kultura, Pagkakakilanlan at Pagkabansa” theme of Social Studies education and the Department of Education’s mandate for culturally sensitive curriculum. Guided by Curriculum Alignment Theory and using qualitative content analysis, ten DepEd-approved textbooks (2016–2022) were analyzed for tone and historical accuracy. Findings show that representations fall into four typologies: (1) positive and accurate, (2) positive but inaccurate, (3) negative but accurate, and (4) negative and inaccurate. Positive and accurate portrayals were most common in Grade 5 textbooks, especially in themes such as Political Contributions, General Descriptions of Islam, Cultural Practices, and Architecture and Maritime Traditions. However, inconsistencies remain. In both Grade 5 and Grade 6 textbooks, the theme of Resistance and History appeared frequently but was depicted with varying levels of accuracy and tone—ranging from empowering narratives to distorted portrayals. Visual representations were generally positive, though one instance lacked accuracy. While some representations align with the curriculum’s goals, others— marked by factual errors, misdated events, or stereotypical framing—indicate partial or clear misalignment. This study affirms the value of Curriculum Alignment Theory in evaluating textbook content and recommends the revision of learning materials to reflect accurate, respectful, and inclusive narratives. It also calls for the engagement of Muslim scholars and communities in textbook development, integration of reflective and context-sensitive pedagogy, and strengthened teacher training in intercultural competence. Continued evaluation of textbooks, particularly under the new Matatag Curriculum, will be vital to ensuring sustained alignment with the principles of cultural sensitivity and inclusivity. Ultimately, the study advocates for collaborative efforts among educators, policymakers, and curriculum developers to produce educational materials that foster respect for cultural diversity.

The research specifically evaluates how these representations align with the "Kultura, Pagkakakilanlan at Pagkabansa" theme of Social Studies education and the Department of Education’s mandate to provide a culturally sensitive curriculum. The core problem addressed is the potential for misalignment between educational materials and the goal of fostering inclusive, accurate, and respectful narratives regarding Muslim Filipinos.

The context of the research is situated within the Philippine educational landscape, specifically focusing on the period between 2016 and 2022. During this time, the Department of Education (DepEd) has emphasized the importance of cultural sensitivity in curriculum development to promote national identity and unity. The study seeks to determine whether the textbooks approved by the department during this timeframe successfully fulfill these mandates or if they perpetuate inaccuracies and stereotypes.

To address this problem, the researcher employed a qualitative content analysis method. The study was guided by Curriculum Alignment Theory, which provided the framework for evaluating how well the textbook content matches the intended educational goals and cultural mandates. The sample consisted of ten DepEd-approved Social Studies textbooks spanning various grade levels. The analysis focused on two primary dimensions: the tone of the representations and their historical accuracy.

The findings of the study reveal that representations of Filipino Muslims are not uniform and can be categorized into four distinct typologies: positive and accurate, positive but inaccurate, negative but accurate, and negative and inaccurate. The most common type of representation found was positive and accurate, particularly in Grade 5 textbooks. These accurate portrayals were most evident in themes concerning political contributions, general descriptions of Islam, cultural practices, and architecture and maritime traditions.

Despite these positive findings, the study identified significant inconsistencies across different grade levels. In both Grade 5 and Grade 6 textbooks, the theme of "Resistance and History" appeared frequently, but the quality of these representations varied widely. The narratives ranged from empowering accounts to distorted portrayals, indicating that historical struggles are not always depicted with consistent accuracy or a respectful tone. Furthermore, while visual representations were generally positive, the researcher identified at least one instance where the imagery lacked accuracy.

The study concludes that while some representations align with the curriculum’s goals of inclusivity and cultural sensitivity, others demonstrate partial or clear misalignment. This misalignment is manifested through factual errors, misdated historical events, and the use of stereotypical framing. While the Curriculum Alignment Theory proved to be a valuable tool for evaluating these materials, the results suggest that the current textbooks do not fully meet the standards of accuracy and respect required by the Department of Education's mandates.

The implications of these findings are significant for educators, policymakers, and curriculum developers. The study recommends a thorough revision of learning materials to ensure they reflect accurate, respectful, and inclusive narratives of Filipino Muslims. A key recommendation is the active engagement of Muslim scholars and communities in the textbook development process to prevent the occurrence of inaccuracies and stereotypes.

Furthermore, the study suggests the integration of reflective and context-sensitive pedagogy in the classroom to complement the textbooks. There is also a highlighted need for strengthened teacher training focused on intercultural competence, ensuring that educators are equipped to navigate and teach diverse cultural histories effectively. The researcher notes that continued evaluation of textbooks will be essential, particularly as the educational system transitions under the new Matatag Curriculum. Ultimately, the study advocates for a collaborative approach among all stakeholders to produce educational materials that truly foster respect for cultural diversity and support the principles of inclusivity in the Philippine education system.

title: Communicative (Re)Production of Teacher Authority in a Generative AI-Infused and Gamified Multicultural Classroom: An Exchange ESL Teacher's Autoethnography
abstract:
Throughout the teaching-learning process, I have noticed how the act of communication shapes the ongoing practice of meaning-making among members in the classroom, especially within my regards to my identity as the classroom’s figure of authority. The classroom possesses a social order, created at the micro level through communication, headed by the authority of the teacher with the students as learners. With the encroachment of generative AI-infused technologies (GAI) however, this concept of teacher identity as authority within classroom social order has to be (re)created, maintained, repaired, and transformed (Craig, 1999) to accommodate new developments in space and time.

This study sought to explore how generative AI-infused educational technologies and gamification (re)produces the identity of the teacher as the authority in the multicultural classroom. It sought to answer the questions: (1) How has generative AI in a multicultural classroom threatened teachers' authority?; and (2) How does GAI and gamification integration in  communicative practices (re)produce teacher authority in a multicultural classroom? This study made use of a qualitative research design, specifically autoethnography. Drawing from my lived experiences as a Filipino cultural exchange ESL teacher, I analyzed naturally-occurring data as situated descriptions of how my authority and identity are constructed through communication. Data was thematically organized using codes, sub-themes, and overarching themes related to GAI and gamification.

This study found that teacher authority has been threatened by GAI in four ways: (1) threatening self-image as a content expert; (2) tendency to outsource thinking with GAI; (3) challenging traditional teacher roles; and (4) weakening teacher authority. The study then found that teacher authority is (re)produced through five themes processes: (1) Creating fun and engaging lessons through data-driven decision making; (2) monitoring progress and motivating learners through pleasurable learning; (3) using gamification to improve student performance; (4) partnering with parents and tailoring lessons to fit learners’ needs; and (5) assessing learner’s progress and awarding performance. The idea that authority is enacted not merely through formal institutional structures but through active engagement with GAI and gamified strategies shape and legitimize the teacher’s central role emerged in the analysis, as well GAI’s role as a tool for reflexivity which (re)constructs the professional identity and pedagogical interventions of the teacher.

Paradela’s dissertation examines the shifting dynamics of teacher authority within modern, technologically complex classrooms, specifically focusing on the intersection of Generative AI (GAI), gamification, and multicultural teaching environments. Using an autoethnographic qualitative research design, the study explores the lived experiences of the researcher, a Filipino cultural exchange teacher in a North Carolina ESL classroom. Grounded in sociocultural tradition and symbolic interactionism, the research views teacher authority as a communicatively constructed identity negotiated through social interaction.

The findings indicate that GAI threatens traditional teacher authority by challenging the teacher's self-image as a content expert, encouraging the outsourcing of thinking, disrupting traditional roles, and weakening overall authority. However, the study also finds that GAI and gamification can reproduce authority. Through these tools, teachers become creators of engaging lessons, monitors of progress, strategic performers, partners to parents, and assessors who use digital recognition.

The study concludes that teacher authority is a dynamic, relational construct rather than a product of formal institutional structures. Rather than diminishing the teacher's role, GAI and gamification allow teachers to reconstruct their professional identity from being the sole source of content to becoming facilitators, gamification strategists, and data-driven designers. The research suggests that successful technology integration depends on the teacher's ability to use these tools to enhance the communicative and relational aspects of teaching.

This dissertation by Gino P. Paradela explores the shifting dynamics of teacher authority within a modern, technologically complex classroom environment. The study focuses on the intersection of three specific variables: the use of Generative AI (GAI), the implementation of gamification, and the unique challenges of teaching in a multicultural setting.

The problem addressed by the researcher is the tension and disruption caused by the encroachment of Generative AI into the classroom, which threatens traditional notions of teacher identity and authority. The author notes that as AI tools become more prevalent, teachers face a crisis of meaning, fearing that their roles as content experts may be marginalized or replaced. This tension is compounded by the complexities of being a cultural exchange teacher in the United States, where the researcher had to navigate different cultural frameworks, varying student expectations regarding respect, and the need to engage a diverse, multicultural student body.

The context of the study is a multicultural ESL (English as a Second Language) classroom in the State of North Carolina, USA. The researcher served as a Filipino cultural exchange teacher, navigating the intersection of his own cultural background and the American educational system. The classroom was characterized by a diverse student population with varied linguistic and cultural realities, and the instructional environment was increasingly infused with digital tools and gamified strategies.

To investigate these dynamics, the researcher employed a qualitative research design, specifically autoethnography. This method allowed the author to use his own lived experiences as a primary source of data to understand broader cultural phenomena. The data collection spanned from 2023 to 2025 and included naturally occurring data such as talker diary entries, lesson plans, recommendation letters, slide presentations, emails, and generative AI-generated reports. The researcher utilized inductive thematic analysis to organize the data into codes, sub-themes, and overarching themes. The theoretical framework for the study was grounded in the sociocultural tradition and symbolic interactionism, viewing teacher authority as a communicatively constructed identity that is constantly negotiated through social interaction.

The findings of the study are divided into two primary dimensions: how GAI threatens authority and how GAI and gamification (re)produce it. The research found that teacher authority is threatened by GAI in four specific ways: the threat to the teacher's self-image as a content expert, the tendency for both teachers and students to outsource thinking to GAI, the challenge to traditional teacher roles, and the overall weakening of traditional teacher authority.

However, the study also found that teacher authority is (re)produced through five key processes facilitated by these technologies. First, the teacher becomes a creator of fun and engaging lessons through data-driven decision-making. Second, the teacher monitors progress and motivates learners through pleasurable, gamified learning experiences. Third, gamification is used as a strategic tool to improve student performance. Fourth, the teacher acts as a partner to parents, using technology to tailor lessons to specific learner needs. Finally, the teacher uses these tools to assess learner progress and award performance through digital recognition.

The study concludes that teacher authority is not merely a product of formal institutional structures but is a dynamic, relational construct that is enacted through active engagement with new technologies. Rather than simply diminishing the teacher's role, GAI and gamification serve as tools for reflexivity, allowing the teacher to reconstruct their professional identity and pedagogical interventions. The teacher's role shifts from being a sole source of content to becoming a facilitator, a gamification strategist, and a data-driven designer of learning experiences.

The implications of this research are significant for various stakeholders in the educational sector. For cultural exchange teachers, the study provides a framework for navigating identity shifts in technologically advancing and culturally diverse environments. For exchange program sponsors and policymakers, the findings suggest a need for professional development programs that focus on AI literacy, prompt engineering, and the integration of gamified strategies to better equip international educators. Ultimately, the research suggests that the successful integration of AI and gamification in the classroom depends on the teacher's ability to use these tools to enhance, rather than replace, the communicative and relational aspects of teaching.

title: Job Satisfaction and Job Performance among Nurses in a Tertiary Hospital in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
abstract:

The study examines job satisfaction factors such as extrinsic rewards, scheduling, work-life balance, professional growth opportunities, interpersonal relationships, and recognition. Ma. Fe Adelle N. Barua's thesis, "Job Satisfaction and Job Performance among Nurses in a Tertiary Hospital in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," investigates the link between nurse satisfaction and professional efficacy. Framed by Herzberg’s Two-Factor Theory, the study addresses concerns regarding nurse turnover, increased workloads, and risks to patient safety, particularly in the Emergency Room. Using a descriptive correlational research design, data were collected from 384 staff nurses at Dr. Soliman Fakeeh Hospital in Jeddah through purposive sampling.

The findings reveal a significant positive relationship between job satisfaction and job performance, indicating that higher satisfaction levels consistently lead to better performance. Regarding satisfaction, nurses identified extrinsic rewards, professional growth opportunities, and work-life balance as the most relevant variables. In terms of performance, nurses demonstrated strong leadership and teamwork skills, though critical care and professional development were identified as areas for potential growth. Additionally, salary and years of work experience were found to be important predictors of both job satisfaction and performance.

The study concludes that job satisfaction is vital for improving performance, reducing turnover, and ensuring high-quality healthcare. The implications suggest that prioritizing employee satisfaction can lead to higher productivity and improved patient outcomes. For administrators, the results highlight the need for retention strategies like career advancement and training, while providing policymakers a basis for developing motivational strategies to improve clinical care quality.

Barua investigates the relationship between how satisfied nurses are with their work and how effectively they perform their professional duties. The research problem stems from the critical role nurses play in healthcare delivery and the significant impact their performance has on patient outcomes and service quality. The author notes that hospitals face challenges in attracting and retaining qualified staff, and dissatisfaction can lead to high turnover rates, increased workloads for remaining staff, and potential risks to patient safety, such as medication errors or negligence. The study's objectives were to describe the levels of job satisfaction and job performance among nurses, examine how socio-demographic characteristics (such as age, sex, education, experience, marital status, nationality, and salary) relate to these levels, and determine the correlation between job satisfaction and job performance.

The researcher employed a descriptive correlational research design. The study was conducted at Dr. Soliman Fakeeh Hospital in Jeddah. Using purposive sampling, the researcher collected data from 384 staff nurses across various departments. The data collection utilized a validated three-part survey instrument. Statistical analysis was performed using descriptive statistics (mean and standard deviation) and inferential statistics, specifically Pearson’s Correlation Coefficient, to test the relationships between variables.

The findings revealed a significant positive relationship between job satisfaction and job performance, indicating that higher levels of satisfaction consistently lead to better performance. Regarding satisfaction, nurses ranked extrinsic rewards, professional growth opportunities, and work-life balance as the most relevant variables. In terms of performance, nurses demonstrated strong leadership and teamwork skills, while critical care and professional development were identified as areas for potential growth. The study also found that salary and years of work experience were important predictors of both job satisfaction and performance.

The study concludes that job satisfaction is a vital component in improving job performance, reducing staff turnover, and ensuring the delivery of high-quality healthcare. Because satisfaction and performance are inextricably linked, addressing the needs of nurses is essential for organizational success and patient safety.

title: The Intention for Seasonal Influenza Vaccine (SIV) Uptake and the Perceived Beliefs of Healthcare Providers in a Private Tertiary Hospital in Metro Manila
abstract:
Healthcare providers' (HCPs) uptake of the seasonal influenza vaccine (SIV) vis-à-vis their perceived beliefs remain a fundamental international health concern. This study investigated the HCPs' intention to receive the SIV at a private tertiary hospital in Metro Manila and examined the perceived beliefs that influenced their decisions. The study based its theoretical framework on the Health Belief Model and used a cross-sectional, questionnaire-based study with total enumeration sampling. Chi-square and logistic regression analyses were performed to identify associations between the intent to vaccinate and perceived beliefs and the modifying factors.

Results showed a significant proportion of HCPs’ expressed intention to receive the SIV. The perceived beliefs including perceived susceptibility, severity, benefits, barriers, and cues to action played a major role in shaping vaccination intention, whereas socio-demographic and role-related factors showed little and non-significant influence apart from the history of seasonal influenza vaccination.

The findings revealed the need for interventions at both the targeted and broad-level health approaches to address vaccine hesitancy among HCPs. Educational activities, institution-led interventions, as well as suitably framed policy measures, were recommended to improve HCPs' vaccine uptake, ultimately contributing to better patient outcomes and a resilient healthcare workforce.

title: Knowledge, Attitude and Compliance on Pressure Injury Prevention among Nurses in the Teaching-Training Public Hospital in Cebu City, Philippines
abstract:
Introduction: Pressure injuries are a traditional nursing issue. This study determines the nurses’ knowledge, attitude and compliance on pressure injury prevention.

Materials and Methods: A descriptive correlational quantitative design was used in the study. A total of 196 nurses were selected using stratified random sampling. The knowledge was measured using the Pieper pressure ulcer knowledge test, while the nurses’ attitude was measured by the staff attitude scale, and compliance on pressure injuries was assessed using the pressure injury prevention care bundle. Participants were nurses assigned to the medical–surgical units in the teaching-training public hospital in Cebu City, Philippines. The participants were asked using a paper-to-pen test.

Results: In this study, among all indicators, 88.15% of the nurses were knowledgeable in terms of the use of devices, followed by other preventive measures with 87.46% and lastly, 85.86% of the nurses knew how to identify risk factors that causes PI. On the other hand, 67.86% of the nurses were least knowledgeable in determining stages I, II, III, IV and classification of pressure injuries, followed by mobility with 75.92% then skin care with 77.30%. Majority of the nurses had a favorable attitude with a mean score of m=4.03 (SD=0.13). In terms of compliance of nurses on PI prevention, across all indicators, nurses were highly compliant in risk assessment (m=3.51, SD=0.74), but least performed in  moisture/incontinence management (m=3.11, SD=0.79). The following variables had a significant relationship with each other; knowledge vs compliance  X2=1230.954a,p=0.00), attitude vs compliance (X2=1389.378a, p=0.00), knowledge vs length of service (rho=.162*, p=0.02), attitude vs length of service (rho= -.144*, p=0.04), length of service vs compliance (rho= -.145*, p=0.04), training on PI vs compliance (X2=22.534*p=0.03). 

Conclusion/Implications: As a result of their high level of knowledge, favorable attitude with high level of compliance, development of pressure injuries among patients in the medical-surgical units in the teaching-training public hospital in Cebu City, Philippines, may be prevented through proper application by the nurses of the preventive measures or interventions to prevent PI. The correlation between variable is deemed necessary for the nurses assigned to the units so that they can provide a quality skin care, thus, control the occurrence of pressure injuries.

Findings revealed varying levels of proficiency. The thesis titled "Knowledge, Attitude and Compliance on Pressure Injury Prevention among Nurses in the Teaching-Training Public Hospital in Cebu City, Philippines" by Sherwin C. Garces investigates the factors influencing the prevention of pressure injuries (PI) among nursing staff. The study is motivated by the significant clinical burden of pressure injuries, which increase mortality, morbidity, and healthcare costs. Specifically, the researcher noted an alarming incidence rate at the study site—a 1,500-bed tertiary government hospital in Cebu City—where approximately 9 to 10 pressure injuries were recorded every month over an 18-month period.

The research problem centers on the need to determine whether nurses' levels of knowledge and their attitudes toward prevention directly correlate with their actual compliance with established prevention protocols. The researcher sought to identify if demographic factors, such as sex, educational attainment, length of service, and specialized training, serve as significant predictors of a nurse's ability to prevent these injuries.

To address these questions, the study employed a descriptive-correlational quantitative research design. The researcher utilized stratified random sampling to select participants from the medical and surgical units of the hospital. A total of 196 nurses participated in the study, completing a paper-and-pen test to ensure data integrity. The research instruments included the Pieper Pressure Ulcer Knowledge Test to measure knowledge, a Staff Attitude Scale to assess attitudes, and the Pressure Injury Prevention Care Bundle to evaluate compliance across various indicators such as risk assessment, skin care, and moisture management. The study was grounded in the Neuman Systems Model, which views the patient as a holistic system and treats pressure injuries as stressors that require primary, secondary, or tertiary prevention.

The findings revealed varying levels of proficiency among the nursing staff. In terms of knowledge, nurses demonstrated high proficiency in the use of devices (88.15%) and other preventive measures (87.46%), but were significantly less knowledgeable regarding the identification of risk factors (85.86%), mobility (75.92%), skin care (77.30%), and the classification and staging of pressure injuries (67.86%). Regarding attitudes, the majority of nurses exhibited a favorable attitude toward PI prevention, with a mean score of 4.03. In terms of compliance, nurses were highly compliant in performing risk assessments (mean = 3.51) but showed the lowest compliance in moisture and incontinence management (mean = 3.11).

Statistical analysis confirmed several significant relationships between the variables. There were significant correlations between knowledge and compliance, and between attitude and compliance. Furthermore, demographic profiles were found to influence these factors: length of service was significantly related to knowledge, attitude, and compliance; training on PI prevention was significantly related to compliance; and the relationship between knowledge/attitude and length of service was also statistically significant.

The study concludes that while nurses possess high levels of knowledge in certain areas and maintain favorable attitudes, their compliance is not uniform across all preventive measures. The development of pressure injuries in the medical-surgical units can be mitigated through the proper application of preventive interventions. The researcher emphasizes that the correlation between knowledge, attitude, and compliance is vital for providing quality skin care and controlling the occurrence of pressure injuries.

The implications of this research suggest a need for targeted educational interventions. Since compliance was lowest in moisture and incontinence management, and knowledge was lowest in staging and classification, the study implies that nursing education and hospital training programs should be specifically tailored to address these gaps. The researcher recommends that the institution develop continuing education programs and potentially refine policies to ensure that nurses are not only knowledgeable but also consistently compliant with all aspects of the pressure injury prevention care bundle. This approach aims to improve patient outcomes, reduce the incidence of hospital-acquired injuries, and decrease the overall burden on the healthcare system.

title: Child Labor in the Philippines and Cambodia - A Comparative Analysis of Causes, Interventions, and Implications for ASEAN Commitments
abstract:
Child labor remains common among ASEAN countries, both countries have ratified the relevant ILO conventions (Minimum Age and Worst Forms of Child Labor), but ongoing challenges, especially in enforcement and data precision persist. In 2022, about 56% of Filipino children and 7.5% of Cambodian children were in hazardous labor both aged 5 to 17. In the Philippines, mostly older children worked in services, while in Cambodia, younger children (ages 5 to 14) worked more in agriculture.

In Cambodia, while progress has been noted (e.g., reduction from 37% to 17% of working children), hazardous labor remains alarmingly high, particularly among older children. As a consequence of the ratification of the ILO core conventions 138 and 182, both Cambodia and the Philippines have enacted laws, regulations and related policies to eliminate child labor. However, despite all these efforts, child labor persists to become one of the major challenges in a country. For these reasons, this study therefore attempted to explore child labor and the underlying factors as to why it remains prevalent despite the interventions and policies crafted to combat it. The findings showed differences in child labor conditions, but both countries share similar policies, having ratified ILO Conventions 138 and 182. The ASEAN roadmap 2025 also has a similar thrust to eliminate child labor in other ASEAN countries as a commitment to ILO conventions 138 and 182. The 2025 roadmap also clearly outlined that ASEAN member states must undertake to realize an inclusive community that promotes quality of life, particularly to the children and youth. Similar studies to assess policies, programs, and actions to eliminate child labor should be done in other ASEAN countries aside from Cambodia and the Philippines. It is recommended that meticulous and stringent monitoring measures be taken to eliminate child labor.

The study concludes that existing laws and ratifications have not been sufficient to eliminate the practice, suggesting that implementation gaps prevent policies from being fully effective. To combat this, the study recommends implementing meticulous and stringent monitoring measures to ensure policies translate into actual protection for children.

title: Global Health Governance Communication: Cascading Health Security Policies during the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: The study is a qualitative content analysis on how the cascade of information and knowledge, through the language and framing of the policies at global, national, and subnational levels, may influence social norms and sociopolitical structures as well as the dynamics of interdependencies towards international cooperation. It answered three questions in terms of ideas, information, and feelings that are communicated through the policies coming from global health institutions; mechanisms of power and interdependence, that were communicated and normalized through the policies at the national and subnational levels; and the policies’ communicative constitution of cooperation for global health security. The analysis focused on health policies issued during the COVID-19 pandemic that targeted vaccination, health workers, discrimination, community quarantine, and face masks/shields. A typology of global health governance communication (GHG-C) is recommended based on the thorough reading, coding process, and code document and code co-occurrence analyses, using Norbert Elias’ concepts, that were done on 210 health policies cascading from the global (n=28), national (n=86) and subnational (n=96) levels. This includes Figuration Architecture, Sentiment Building, Power Diffusion, Norms Setting, Reinforcement, and Global Connect. Based on the results of the study, Global Health Governance Communication (GHG-C) is a field of communication that examines the thread of messages and language conveying ideas, information and emotions that cascades from global guidance to national and subnational policies and weaves the social fabric covering institutional and socialvalues, relationships, controls, behaviors and norms on health.

title: Host as Storyteller: An Autoethnographic Inquiry of Narrative Construction as a Communicative Act
abstract:
This study explores the multifaceted role of the host as a storyteller, focusing on the analysis of the narrative construction as a performative and communicative practice in live events, as well as an act of cultural mediation. While the act of storytelling is a vital component of human social behavior and has been extensively researched in the context of media and literature, very few studies have examined live event hosts as narrative agents. This gap in scholarship is addressed in the present study through an autoethnographic lens. The researcher has taken on the role of both participant and observer to preserve the intricacies surrounding hosting as a performative and spontaneous practice.

The analysis incorporates communicative ecology and performance theory within a cultural narrative framework as a starting point for understanding a host’s function as a cultural mediator and emotional intercessor. The host’s narrative sculpting, resonating with a wide-ranging audience, is built on literature concerning media hosting, live event storytelling, and the psychology of narrative transport. The participant’s data came from direct observation, reflective journaling, and narrative analysis, along with the improvisational activities and storytelling mastery of the hosts, capturing their lived experiences. Analysis was carried out iteratively on emergent themes concerning how hosts develop and perform coherent, emotionally engaging, and culturally sensitive narratives for different audiences.

The study demonstrates that the host functions as a storyteller, co-constructing narratives with both participants and the audience. Instead of merely facilitating, the host shapes the event’s emotional and cultural significance. Through fragmented and multi-vocal storytelling, the host captures spoken and unspoken elements, ensuring the representation of diverse perspectives. The host’s responsibilities extend beyond storytelling, encompassing the role of a cultural custodian who sustains the event’s meaning and connects it to community values. Reflexivity further enables the host to
examine this evolving role. Accordingly, storytelling in hosting is active, affective, and participatory, thus enriching the event’s depth and cultural resonance.

title: Reproducing Media and Information Literacy Through the Digital Papacy and the Discursive Strategies of Pope Francis:  An Intertextual Analysis
abstract:
This study examines the discursive tactics utilized by Pope Francis in his social encyclicals, emphasizing their function in articulating intricate theological concepts, ethical mandates, and social justice matters to a worldwide audience. Anchored in Mumby’s theoretical framework of discourse, the research highlights the interpretive essence of communication, the impact of socio-cultural circumstances, and the significance of conversation. The conceptual framework includes intertextual analysis, demonstrating how texts reference and engage with each other in the digital environment. The key issue identified is the necessity for improved Media and Information Literacy (MIL) in response to modern issues, including misinformation and digital
saturation. This study seeks to accomplish three objectives: to examine the discursive techniques of the encyclicals, to investigate the implications of the digital pope for religious communication, and to evaluate the incorporation of Media and Information Literacy principles within the Pope’s teachings.
The study employs a qualitative research design based on intertextual analysis, concentrating on three units: (1) Pope Francis’s encyclicals—Lumen Fidei, Laudato Si, and Fratelli Tutti; (2) messages from World Communications Day; and (3) pertinent secondary literature on Media and Information Literacy (MIL). The results indicate that Pope Francis's discursive strategy successfully foster critical thinking and ethical media participation, hence augmenting the Church's significance in the digital era. The study boosts social order within the universal Catholic Church by demonstrating how
these encyclicals cultivate a unified narrative that promotes active engagement in confronting modern difficulties. The research suggests that the digital pope functions as an essential channel for Media and Information Literacy, enabling individuals to traverse the digital
environment responsibly. Recommendations encompass enhanced incorporation of MIL principles within Church doctrines and the formulation of digital engagement tactics that promote community and ethical dialogue.

title: Exploring Communication Patterns and Work Value Fulfillment Through Network Analysis among International Professors in a Korean Christian University
abstract:
A Korean Christian university is characterized by hierarchical, top-down, centralized communication patterns that are deeply ingrained by strong Confucian values. Universities were encouraged to hire international professors in response to the Global Declaration “Segyehwa” of Kim Young-san’s Administration in 1994, which aimed to transform South Korea into a first-rate nation and drew national attention to education. A specific support network categorized as “international professors” in a Christian university that comprised twenty-four actors which was 100% of the network (62.5% males, and 37.5% females) were surveyed through discourses of work value fulfillment to analyze the network using UCINET 6 to identify ties created
by each actor and its characteristics, the central actors in each discourse, and to evaluate the most valued work values of professors through communicative patterns. Findings revealed that the significant ties created a star or all-channel network that was decentralized and enabled members to communicate freely. Similarities in demographic and personality attributes, such as nationality and cultural backgrounds, gender, age, and expertise, created both constraints and opportunities from how they were embedded in the networks. The central actors who were consistently well-positioned across all discourses accounted for 29% of the network. They were all male and demonstrated extensive knowledge and experience in technology and innovation. As reflected in professors' communication patterns, coworkers’ work value, supervision, and work itself were most valued in their profession. The not-well-connected nodes in the network exhibited that communication for them is “satisficing”.

This research investigates the communication dynamics and work value fulfillment of twenty-four international professors at a Korean Christian university. The study is situated within a cultural context defined by hierarchical, top-down, and centralized communication patterns rooted in Confucian values, occurring against the backdrop of South Korea's "Segyehwa" Global Declaration. Utilizing surveys and UCINET 6 software for network analysis, the researcher identified ties created by individual actors, pinpointed central actors, and evaluated valued work values through communicative patterns.

The network analysis revealed a decentralized structure characterized by star or all-channel networks, which enabled members to communicate freely. Demographic and personality attributes, such as nationality, gender, age, and expertise, functioned as both constraints and opportunities within these social networks. A key finding identified that individuals consistently well-positioned across all discourses accounted for 29% of the total network; notably, all these central actors were male with extensive knowledge in technology and innovation. Regarding professional values, coworkers’ work values, supervision, and the work itself were the most highly valued aspects.

The study concludes that while traditional Confucian hierarchy suggests centralization, the actual communicative ties among international professors are decentralized. However, a gendered dimension to professional influence exists, as the most central actors were exclusively male with specific technical expertise. Furthermore, less-connected nodes exhibited "satisficing" communication, suggesting that international professors do not experience uniform levels of integration.

title: Health Communication in Digital Spaces: Selected FIlipino Medical Influencers’ ‘Clout’ and Parasocial Relationships
abstract: This study explores how Filipino medical influencers build and sustain parasocial relationships (PSRs) to promote health information in digital spaces such as social media. Through an exploratory-descriptive qualitative research design, the study utilized semi-structured interviews with two medical influencers and six active followers. The research is grounded in socio-cultural and phenomenological traditions that allow for an examination of the co-construction of meaning and lived experiences within these one-sided but meaningful online bonds. Findings reveal that influencer motivations stem from a desire to combat misinformation and provide accessible, bite-sized health advice. Influencers employ strategic self-presentation by balancing clinical rigor with conversational communication to humanize their expertise. Followers are primarily motivated by financial pragmatism and the need to alleviate health-related anxiety, viewing influencers as credible, cost- free intermediaries. The study introduces the Dynamic Digital Authority (DDA) Model, which posits that online influence functions as a continually negotiated performance rather than a static marker of expertise. It concludes that effective digital health communication is a reciprocal process. This process transforms passive consumers into active health advocates. title: Work-Life Balance and Resilience Among Nurse Educators in Baguio City
abstract:
Work-Life Balance (WLB) and resilience of nurse educators are examined in this study, with the demographic profiles of the participants: age, sex, marital status, and years of experience considered. A descriptive-correlational design was employed to determine the relationships among the variables. A total of 120 nurse educators participated, completing an adopted survey questionnaire that included the FisherMcAuley Work–Life Balance Scale and the 10-item Connor–Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC-10). The results show that many nursing faculty respondents are aged 35 - 44,
female, married, and have 2 - 5 years of experience, which is considered an advanced beginner level. Meanwhile, the demographic profiles of the respondents, including age, sex, marital status, and years of experience, are not significantly associated with WLB. This finding implies that personal and professional harmony is affected by the workplace setting and the support for individuals' characteristics. The respondents reported a neutral WLB (M = 3.37), indicating moderate worklife and life-work interference, yet robust work-life fulfillment. The nursing education is then considered professionally satisfying amid the challenges teachers face. Likewise, nurse educators display an elevated level of resilience (M= 3.16), characterized by adaptation, emotional regulation, and perseverance in times of stress. Findings further reveal that, despite no significant relationship between demographic variables and resilience, sex is an essential factor, with females exhibiting variable levels of resilience. Such an outcome suggests that men and women in the profession have varying levels of resilience that may be due to context-based support mechanisms and expected roles. Finally, there is no association between WLB and resilience among nurse educators, which may be due to the independence of resilience from homeostasis in both personal and professional domains.Based on the results, the recommendations include reinforcing faculty loadmanagement, strengthening agile work systems, and streamlining supportive culture and mechanisms for nurse educators. Moreover, the institutionalization of mentorship programs for beginning faculty members and the development of gender-responsive health initiatives are crucial. Accordingly, future research may focus on conducting longitudinal studies to examine thoroughly the organizational factors that progressivelyaffect WLB and resilience among professionals.

The research employed a descriptive-correlational research design involving 120 nurse educators from five nursing institutions. Participants were selected through purposive sampling based on criteria including a minimum of two years of teaching experience, an age between 25 and 59, and experience in supervising student nurses in clinical rotations. Data were collected using an adopted survey questionnaire consisting of a demographic profile, the Fisher-McAuley Work–Life Balance Scale, and the 10-item Connor–Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC-10).

The demographic profile revealed that the majority of participants were female, married, aged 35–44 years, and had 2–5 years of experience. Regarding work-life balance, respondents reported a neutral overall mean of 3.37. There was moderate interference from work on personal life and a neutral level of personal life interference with work, though respondents reported a high level of work-personal life enhancement. The level of resilience was found to be elevated, with a mean of 3.16, characterized by adaptation, emotional regulation, and perseverance.

Findings showed that demographic profiles, including age, sex, marital status, and years of experience, were not significantly associated with work-life balance. Regarding resilience, there was no significant relationship with most demographic variables, though sex was identified as an essential factor, with females exhibiting variable levels of resilience. Finally, the study found no significant association between work-life balance and resilience among the nurse educators, suggesting these constructs may operate independently.

Regarding work-life balance, the respondents reported a neutral overall mean of 3.37, indicating a balanced relationship between job demands and personal life. This suggests that personal and professional harmony is influenced more by the workplace setting and support mechanisms than by individual characteristics. Regarding resilience, there was no significant relationship with most demographic variables, though sex was identified as an essential factor, with females exhibiting variable levels of resilience. Finally, the study found no significant association between work-life balance and resilience among the nurse educators. This lack of association may be due to the independence of resilience from homeostasis in both personal and professional domains.

The study concludes that while nurse educators face moderate interference between their work and personal lives, they maintain a sense of professional satisfaction through work-personal life enhancement. They also demonstrate robust resilience, allowing them to manage stress and adapt to the complexities of their roles. The lack of a significant link between work-life balance and resilience suggests that these two constructs may operate independently within the professional context of nursing education.

title: Communicating Disaster Risks in a State University in the Philippines
abstract:
In a disaster-prone country like the Philippines, schools and universities play an important role in promoting a culture of preparedness and resilience. However, such practice is seldom observed. Thus, the study examined how disaster risks are communicated within a state university in the Philippines. Specifically, the study attempted aimed to: identify the existing communication methods used to convey disaster information or protocols to stakeholders in the university; assess how constituents respond to these protocols; find out how prepared are they to respond to disaster risks to various stakeholders; and analyze the existing mechanisms for stakeholders’ feedback on disaster communication efforts. This study examined the
gaps in disaster communication, acknowledging that clear, inclusive, and practical communication are keys for ensuring campus safety. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study combined surveys, interviews, and a review of existing data to understand current communication practices, stakeholder responses, preparedness levels, and barriers. The findings showed that while the university has existing systems such as memos and social media announcements, these are not always consistent, inclusive, or engaging. Many students and faculty members are still unaware of some
safety procedures. There are also few opportunities that are often lacking for people to give feedback, and visual materials that could help explain risks. This research suggests that communication efforts should be more participatory and tailored to the campus context. The lack of effective disaster risk communication makes it difficult to build a strong risk culture among members of the university community. Without clear, consistent, and inclusive communication, awareness about risks will not develop into shared values, habits, and actions that support preparedness and resilience. Steps like regular training, more accessible materials (such as visuals or audio aids), and greater involvement from all stakeholders of the university can help improve how disaster risks are understood. With these interventions, the university can strengthen its communication strategies and build a more resilient and prepared academic institution to develop a risk culture with shared values, beliefs, attitudes, and behaviuoral norms that shape how a community views and reacts to hazards.

title: Campus Journalism in Cavite Public High Schools: A Qualitative Case Study of Stakeholders’ Perspectives
abstract:
This qualitative case study explores the views of stakeholders which include student journalists, advisers, and school administrators, in secondary schools in Cavite, focusing on the implementation of campus journalism programs within the framework of the Campus Journalism Act of 1991.
The study aimed to examine the views and perspectives of the stakeholders, particularly in light of evolving technological advancements and the rise of digital media. Findings indicate a significant shift from print to online platforms, with students embracing digital publishing tools such as social media and AI-based applications. Despite the benefits, stakeholders highlighted issues such as resource disparities, inadequate infrastructure, and insufficient professional training in digital media. Stakeholders expressed a shared belief in the need to amend the Campus Journalism Act of 1991 to better align with the digital age, emphasizing the importance of incorporating provisions for online publishing, digital censorship, and the ethical use of technologies like AI. The study advocates for reforms in policy and the programs, proposing the integration of digital media into campus journalism training, enhanced resource allocation, and professional development for both students and educators. By addressing these gaps, the study sought to strengthen the role of campus journalism as a tool for student empowerment, media literacy, and civic engagement in the 21st century.

Ruiz investigates the implementation of campus journalism programs in the Division of Cavite Province under Republic Act No. 7079. The research examines how the Campus Journalism Act of 1991 functions amidst rapid digital transformation, noting a misalignment between the pre-digital legal framework and the contemporary media landscape. Specifically, the Act lacks provisions regarding online publishing, social media, digital censorship, and the ethical implications of Artificial Intelligence (AI).

Using a qualitative case study design involving semi-structured interviews with administrators, advisers, and student journalists, the study identifies several key findings. There is a significant shift toward digital-first journalism, yet this transition is often driven by necessity and informal peer-to-peer learning rather than formal curriculum design. Significant resource disparities exist, including inadequate infrastructure such as computers, cameras, and reliable internet. Furthermore, advisers struggle to provide technical guidance due to heavy teaching loads and a lack of specialized training. Stakeholders reached a consensus that the 1991 Act is outdated.

The study concludes that obsolete legal provisions and systemic resource gaps hinder the potential of campus journalism. Ruiz suggests that the Campus Journalism Act requires modernization to address multimedia production and digital ethics. Recommendations include legislative reforms, institutional investments in digital infrastructure by the Department of Education, and the creation of communities of practice.

Fourth, stakeholders expressed a strong consensus that the Campus Journalism Act of 1991 is outdated. While it remains a symbolic cornerstone for press freedom, it lacks specific provisions for online publishing, digital safety, and the ethical use of AI. Finally, the study found that while campus journalism positively impacts student career paths and civic engagement, the struggle to balance academic requirements with journalistic duties remains a persistent challenge for students.

The study concludes that while campus journalism remains a vital democratic practice in the Philippines, its full potential is hindered by obsolete legal provisions and systemic resource gaps. The Campus Journalism Act of 1991 requires modernization to encompass the realities of the digital age, particularly regarding online protections and multimedia production. Furthermore, the integration of digital media into the curriculum is currently inconsistent and lacks the institutional support necessary to equip students with essential 21st-century skills.

The implications of this research suggest a need for multi-level reforms. At the legislative level, the study advocates for amending RA 7079 to include directives for digital ethics, online publishing, and multimedia training. At the institutional level, it recommends that the Department of Education (DepEd) and school administrators prioritize investments in digital infrastructure and provide structured professional development for advisers. On a personal and community level, the study suggests fostering "communities of practice" where teachers and students can engage in peer-to-peer learning to navigate the changing media landscape. Ultimately, the research emphasizes that strengthening campus journalism through policy reform and resource allocation is essential for empowering students as responsible, critical, and digitally literate citizens.

title: Exploring Radyo DZLB's 'PAK!' as an Edutainment Program for Agriculture and the Environment
abstract:
With Radyo DZLB's move to the online space, various information and knowledge products are now transformed to cater to audiences from the legacy format and digital media. The station's online equivalent, DZLB Online! continues its advocacy in providing participatory broadcasting through engaging communities and organizations as partners in producing various programs.

Adding to DZLB Online's roster of programs is PAK! Para sa Agrikultura at Kalikasan. Or PAK!. PAK!, is a program that uses the Teleradyonet format to popularize and deliver scientific concepts, research projects, and advocacies about agriculture and the environment to the common audience. The episodes tackled various topics such as sustainable agriculture, agricultural modernization, permaculture, environmental protection and conservation, ridge-to-reef ecological frameworks, One Health, sustainable freshwater ecosystems, agriecotourism/naturetainment, the role of individuals and groups as a driver of change for the environment, and community farming as a social enterprise. Through the use of narrative structural analysis, the study looked at the presence of various storytelling elements within the program and how they fit with the program’s learning/education process via broadcast. These processes include (1) looking at PAK!’s narrative structure, (2) analyzing how the program facilitates learning and engagement,
(3) visiting the various technical elements present in the program when it comes to the production process, and (4) exploring how such technical elements aid in how educational content is delivered.

The study examines how this digital evolution facilitates the communication of complex scientific concepts regarding agriculture and the environment to a general audience. Using a qualitative research design involving narrative inquiry and content analysis of 26 episodes, the researcher explored the program's narrative structure, engagement strategies, and technical production elements.

The findings reveal that *PAK!* utilizes a narrative structure based on Freytag’s Pyramid to maintain entertainment value. The program aligns with the Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning through the use of personalization and voice principles, specifically through the relatable interactions between hosts Dr. Ronilo Flores and Dr. Maria Catalina de Luna. Additionally, the segmenting and pre-training principles help prevent cognitive overload. Technical elements, such as visual cutaways, shot framing, background music, and "chargens" to display summarized text, further aid in delivering educational content. The study concludes that *PAK!* successfully balances education and entertainment. For practitioners and policy developers, the research suggests that edutainment is a potent tool for social behavior change and promoting environmental initiatives. Future research should focus on measuring actual impact on audience behavior and knowledge retention.

Para sa Agrikultura at Kalikasan* (PAK!) functions as an edutainment tool. As Radyo DZLB transitioned from terrestrial radio to an online-only "TeleRadyoNet" format, the study sought to understand how this digital evolution allows the station to communicate complex scientific concepts regarding agriculture and the environment to a general audience through an engaging, entertaining medium.

The problem addressed by the research is the challenge of communicating critical development topics, such as agricultural modernization and environmental conservation, in a way that maintains audience interest. The author notes that development programs often struggle to compete with mainstream entertainment. By utilizing the "edutainment" approach—which blends educational content with entertainment formats—the study explores whether PAK! successfully navigates the tension between being informative and being engaging, particularly through the lens of the Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning (CTML).

The study's objectives were to describe the narrative structure of PAK!, discuss how that structure facilitates learning and engagement, analyze the technical elements used in production, and explain how these technical elements aid in the delivery of educational content. To achieve this, the researcher employed a qualitative research design using narrative inquiry and a paradigmatic approach to identify common themes within the program's storytelling. The data consisted of 26 episodes from the first four seasons of the program.

The methodology involved a detailed content analysis of the episodes, focusing on visual elements, audio elements, and narrative flow. The researcher utilized Atlas.ti for coding and thematic analysis to organize insights regarding the program's structure and technical execution.

The findings reveal that PAK! utilizes a structured narrative format based on Freytag’s Pyramid, moving through exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, and catastrophe. This storytelling approach helps maintain the "entertainment" aspect of the program. Regarding the facilitation of learning, the study found that the program aligns closely with the principles of the Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning (CTML). Specifically, the personalization and voice principles are prominently present through the relatable and casual interactions between the hosts, Dr. Ronilo Flores and Dr. Maria Catalina de Luna. The study notes that the "human aspect"—the presence of real people rather than AI-generated models—creates a welcoming atmosphere that encourages active cognitive processing. Additionally, the segmenting principle (dividing content into manageable chunks) and the pre-training principle (providing primers or summaries of what to expect) assist the audience in processing complex information without cognitive overload.

Technical elements also play a crucial role in the program's effectiveness. The use of visual cutaways, such as images and videos that correspond to the spoken topic, provides necessary visualization for the viewer. The study found that shot framing, such as medium shots and full shots, helps immerse the viewer in the location of the discussion. Audio elements, including background music and branding bumpers, add "flavor" and professional polish to the production. Furthermore, the use of "chargens" (character generators) to display summarized text helps simplify technical terminology for the common audience. The program's availability on social media platforms further enhances engagement by allowing for real-time interaction and feedback.

In conclusion, the researcher concludes that PAK! is a successful edutainment program that effectively balances education and entertainment. Its success is attributed to its well-planned narrative structure and its strategic use of multimedia elements that align with cognitive learning theories. The program's ability to transform scientific and research-based information into a relatable, human-centric, and visually supported format allows it to reach and engage its target audience effectively.

The implications of this study are significant for the field of development communication. For practitioners, the research suggests that the edutainment approach is a potent tool for social behavior change because it stimulates both the mind and the heart, making information more palatable. For policy developers, the study implies that edutainment can be a subtle and effective communication strategy for promoting government directives or environmental initiatives. Finally, the study recommends that future research should focus on measuring the actual impact of such programs on audience behavior and knowledge retention through longitudinal studies or focus group discussions to further refine these communication strategies.
