title: The Relationship Between the Perceived Digital Competency and Critical Thinking Instructional Skills of Social Studies Teachers in the Philippine Public Senior High Schools
abstract: This study investigated whether senior high school Social Studies teachers’ perceived digital competencies predict their perceived critical thinking instructional skills. Conducted in the Schools Division of Region 3, Philippines, the study employed a predictive-correlational research design. A total of 160 senior high school Social Studies teachers from across the four congressional districts of the Schools Division of Region 3 participated, selected through district quota sampling with eligibility-based screening. Data were collected using a validated survey instrument measuring five domains of digital competencies (based on DigComp 2.2) and five dimensions of critical thinking instructional skills. Findings revealed that senior high school Social Studies teachers demonstrated high levels of perceived digital competencies across all domains and very high competence in implementing critical thinking instructional skills. Multiple linear regression analysis indicated that perceived digital competencies, when combined, significantly predict critical thinking instructional skills, explaining 42% of the variance (R2 = 0.42). These findings are particularly relevant to Social Studies education, wherein teachers are uniquely positioned to integrate digital tools in facilitating evidence-based discussions, critical inquiry, and the analysis of complex social, political, and economic issues. Among the domains, problem-solving retained the largest unique predictive contribution in the simultaneous regression model (B = 0.329, p = 0.006). The non-significance of the remaining four domains in the simultaneous model should be interpreted cautiously, as it likely reflects the substantial shared variance among the five domains — a consequence of multicollinearity — rather than true pedagogical irrelevance. These findings suggest that digital competency, considered collectively, is a meaningful predictor of critical thinking instructional skills, and that problem-solving most distinctively contributes to this relationship among the five domains. The study concludes that digital competence, particularly problem-solving, is integral to enhancing critical thinking pedagogy in Social Studies. These findings provide empirical support for targeted professional development initiatives that strengthen senior high school Social Studies teachers’ problem-solving skills and promote the pedagogical integration of digital technologies to improve higher-order thinking instruction.

title: The Process of Redemption: Becoming Students and Constructing Support Infrastructure in Prison Distance Education
abstract:
This study explored how Persons Deprived of Liberty (PDLs) in the Philippines reconstruct themselves as students through participation in education, and how Distance Education (DE) institutions can scaffold that process. Grounded in Symbolic Interactionism and conducted through grounded theory methodology, the inquiry illuminated the redemptive arc by which incarcerated individuals initiate change, internalize learning under constraint, and perform studenthood as a sustained act of redemption. 
Findings revealed that becoming a student in prison is not a linear transition but a layered negotiation of identity, motivation, and constraint. The emergent theory, Redemption as Self-Reconstruction through Education, showed that redemption unfolds in three phases: Initiation of Redemption, Internalizing Education Amidst Prison Constraints, and Becoming and Being a Student as Redemption in Action. These phases were enacted within contextual layers of pre-incarceration history, the realities of incarceration, and the prison environment. Central to this process was the support infrastructure for prison education, comprised of seven supports: facilitating entry through administrative assistance, structuring time to reinforce motivation, tailoring study practices within a restricted system, drawing strength from redemption-oriented goals, sustaining learning engagement, having educational and skill-building activities, and experiencing the prison as a livable and enabling environment. The study contributes to the field of Distance Education by theorizing how learning becomes both a site of identity reconstruction and a medium of redemption within custodial settings. It highlights the need for ODeL institutions and correctional systems to design supports not as external add-ons but as integral to the very architecture of learning inside. 
The research affirms that education in prison is more than skill acquisition; it is a performance of selfhood. In the staged conditions of incarceration, PDLs do not simply rehearse compliance; they enact new scripts of possibility. In this light, Distance Education emerges as both a classroom and a stage, where the redemptive performance of becoming a student is sustained, even behind prison walls.

The study by Lexter J. Mangubat investigates the transformative process through which Persons Deprived of Liberty (PDLs) in the Philippines reconstruct their identities through participation in education. The research focuses on how these individuals transition from being incarcerated persons to becoming students, and how Distance Education (DE) institutions can provide the necessary scaffolding to support this identity shift. The core problem addressed is the need to understand the psychological and social mechanisms of identity reconstruction within the highly constrained environment of a prison, where learning serves as a vehicle for redemption.

The context of the study is situated within the Philippine correctional system, where distance education offers a unique pathway for learning despite the physical and social limitations of incarceration. The research is grounded in the theoretical framework of Symbolic Interactionism, which posits that identity is formed through social interaction and the interpretation of symbols. By applying this lens, the study examines how the act of studying allows PDLs to negotiate new meanings for themselves within the rigid structures of a custodial setting.

To explore this phenomenon, the researcher employed a grounded theory methodology. This qualitative approach allowed for the development of an emergent theory directly from the data, capturing the lived experiences of the participants. The methodology aimed to map the process of "becoming" a student, moving beyond simple academic achievement to understand the deeper, existential shifts occurring within the incarcerated individuals.

The findings reveal that the transition to studenthood is not a simple or linear progression. Instead, it is a complex, layered negotiation involving individual motivation, identity shifts, and the constant presence of institutional constraints. The study produced an emergent theory titled "Redemption as Self-Reconstruction through Education." This theory posits that redemption is a multi-phased process. The first phase is the Initiation of Redemption, where the individual begins the journey toward change. The second phase involves Internalizing Education Amidst Prison Constraints, where the learner must integrate academic pursuits into a life defined by restriction. The final phase is Becoming and Being a Student as Redemption in Action, where the performance of studenthood becomes a sustained way of living and a continuous act of self-reconstruction.

These three phases do not occur in a vacuum; they are enacted within specific contextual layers. These layers include the individual's pre-incarceration history, the immediate realities of being incarcerated, and the broader physical and social environment of the prison. The study suggests that the process of becoming a student is a way for PDLs to enact new "scripts of possibility," moving away from the identity imposed by the correctional system toward a self-defined identity as a learner.

A significant portion of the findings focuses on the support infrastructure required to make prison education successful. The study identifies seven essential supports that facilitate this redemptive process. First, administrative assistance is necessary to facilitate entry into educational programs. Second, the structuring of time is vital to reinforce and maintain motivation. Third, study practices must be specifically tailored to function within a restricted system. Fourth, learners need to draw strength from redemption-oriented goals to sustain their efforts. Fifth, there must be mechanisms to sustain long-term learning engagement. Sixth, the provision of educational and skill-building activities is essential for holistic development. Finally, the prison itself must be experienced as a livable and enabling environment that supports, rather than hinders, the learning process.

The conclusions of the research emphasize that education in a prison setting is far more than the mere acquisition of new skills or knowledge. It is a profound performance of selfhood. For PDLs, the act of studying is a way to rehearse a new way of being, allowing them to perform a version of themselves that is not defined solely by their crimes or their incarceration. Distance Education, therefore, serves a dual purpose: it acts as a classroom for academic instruction and a stage for the redemptive performance of identity reconstruction.

The implications of this study are significant for both Open Distance e-Learning (ODeL) institutions and correctional systems. The research suggests that educational supports should not be treated as external add-ons or secondary programs. Instead, they must be designed as integral components of the very architecture of learning within custodial settings. For institutions, this means developing specialized pedagogical approaches and administrative frameworks that account for the unique constraints of prison life. For correctional systems, it implies a need to view education as a fundamental tool for rehabilitation and identity reconstruction, requiring an environment that is conducive to the sustained engagement of learners. Ultimately, the study highlights that when distance education is properly scaffolded, it provides a vital medium for redemption, allowing individuals to reconstruct their lives even behind prison walls.

title: Antimicrobial Stewardship Through the Nurses’ Lens: Knowledge, Perceptions  and Challenges in a Mixed-Methods Study
abstract:
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remains a global health threat, and nurses play a pivotal yet often under-recognized role in antimicrobial stewardship (AMS). This study examined nurse’s knowledge, perceptions, and challenges related to their role in AMS using a mixed methods explanatory sequential design. The quantitative phase involved 313 registered nurses from various clinical settings who completed a validated online questionnaire assessing their AMS knowledge, perceptions, and perceived challenges. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, correlation, and logistic regression. The qualitative phase involved semi-structured interviews with 10 purposively selected nurses to explore and contextualize the quantitative findings.

Results indicated that most participants demonstrated high AMS knowledge (88.8%) and a generally positive perception of their role in AMS (WM = 3.97, “Agree”). However, gaps remained in application-level knowledge, particularly in areas such as intravenous-to-oral conversion and understanding environmental contributors to resistance. Linear regression analysis revealed that knowledge significantly predicted perception (B = -1.55, p < .001), suggesting that more knowledgeable nurses held more critical or realistic perspectives on AMS practice within hierarchical healthcare structures. Conversely, knowledge was not significantly associated with perceived challenges (p = .399), indicating that the barriers were primarily systemic rather than individual. The qualitative analysis identified six themes: fragmented and experience- driven knowledge, limited role perception, competing priorities and workload pressures, confidence and hierarchy, patient education limitations, and training and empowerment. The integration of findings indicated that although nurses demonstrated a strong foundational awareness of AMS, their potential contributions were constrained by institutional culture, workload demands, and the absence of structured AMS training programs.

The study concludes that empowering nurses through targeted AMS education, interprofessional collaboration, and organisational support is essential for strengthening their stewardship role and addressing antimicrobial resistance.

To address these issues, the study suggests that clinical practice requires improved interprofessional collaboration and clearer role delineation. Educational interventions should focus on targeted, simulation-based training that emphasizes clinical application over theory. Linear regression analysis indicated that higher knowledge levels significantly predicted more critical or realistic perceptions of AMS practice within hierarchical healthcare structures. Interestingly, knowledge was not significantly associated with perceived challenges, suggesting that the barriers faced by nurses are primarily systemic rather than individual.

Fourth, professional hierarchies and team culture often undermined nurse confidence, making them hesitant to challenge prescribing decisions. Fifth, while nurses felt confident in basic patient education, they felt limited in providing more complex information. Finally, there was a clear call for more structured training and empowerment to facilitate active participation.

The study concludes that empowering nurses is essential for strengthening health systems and addressing AMR.

Clinically, there is a need for improved interprofessional collaboration and clearer role delineation to ensure nurses feel empowered to participate in multidisciplinary AMS teams. Educationally, the study highlights a gap in nursing curricula and continuing professional development; there is a need for targeted, simulation-based, and practice-oriented AMS training that moves beyond theoretical knowledge to clinical application. title: Brand Audit of Marine Plastic Pollution In Four Coastal Barangays in Bulusan, Sorsogon, Philippines
abstract:
Plastic pollution has serious negative effects on marine ecosystems. It affects sectors like biodiversity, public health, and local economies. This study focuses on the Municipality of Bulusan in Sorsogon Province, which is a community heavily relying on fishing and agriculture. It aims to assess the sources and extent of marine plastic pollution in the area. With a comprehensive brand audit across four coastal barangays, this research identifies the top corporations that contribute to plastic waste, evaluates the existing waste management practices, and explores the social and economic impact of plastic pollution on local communities. Findings in the study reveal how prevalent specific plastic types and brands are
in Bulusan's coastal areas. Their origins were then traced back to major corporations. The study also highlights gaps in the municipality's waste management system, specifically in terms of plastic waste segregation and disposal, which are major contributors to the problems caused by the pollution. The results also emphasize the importance of public awareness in mitigating plastic pollution. It then proposes a sustainable waste management approach that is integrated within community engagement. This research provides actionable insights for Local Government Units (LGUs), including advocating for corporations to increase their accountability and for communities to be involved in addressing the crisis caused by plastic pollution. The study also aims to promote sustainable practices that are found to significantly reduce both the financial and environmental cost of marine plastic pollution in Bulusan, which is through fostering partnerships between stakeholders.

half:
Sarah Mae F. Fulleros investigated the prevalence and sources of marine plastic pollution in four coastal barangays in Bulusan, Sorsogon: Dancalan, Dapdap, Mabuhay, and Sabang. The study addresses ecological, social, and economic threats, such as habitat degradation and risks to food security, noting that local waste management often lacks adequate infrastructure. Using a brand audit methodology based on the Break Free From Plastic toolkit, the researcher conducted coastal clean-ups to collect and categorize waste by brand, item description, product type, and material composition.

The findings reveal that food packaging is the most prevalent type of plastic waste across all four barangays, accounting for 91.6% in Dapdap, 81.0% in Dancalan, 75.5% in Sabang, and 55.2% in Mabuhay. Low-Density Polyethylene (LDPE) was the most common material, frequently used for flexible wrappers and sachets, alongside difficult-to-recycle multi-layer plastics. Universal Robina Corp. was identified as the largest contributor at 25.48%, followed by Unilever (11.43%), Monde Nissin Corporation (9.52%), Liwayway Holdings Company Limited (8.57%), and Coca-Cola Beverages Philippines, Inc. (8.57%).

The study concludes that pollution is driven by a heavy reliance on single-use, multi-layer, and LDPE packaging. It suggests that responsibility must extend to producers through an Extended Producer Responsibility framework. A multi-stakeholder approach is recommended, involving local government enforcement of single-use plastic ordinances, enhanced community education on waste segregation, and partnerships between government, businesses, and the community.

two:
The research conducted by Sarah Mae F. Fulleros investigates the prevalence and sources of marine plastic pollution in the Municipality of Bulusan, Sorsogon, Philippines. The study focuses on four specific coastal barangays: Dancalan, Dapdap, Mabuhay, and Sabang.

**Problem and Context**
Marine plastic pollution is a global crisis with severe ecological, social, and economic consequences. It leads to the entanglement and ingestion of plastics by marine organisms, the release of toxic chemicals like bisphenol A, and the degradation of habitats. For coastal communities like Bulusan, which rely heavily on fishing and agriculture, this pollution threatens food security, damages fishing equipment, and reduces the aesthetic value necessary for tourism. While the Philippines is a significant contributor to global ocean pollution, local waste management often struggles due to inadequate infrastructure, leading to practices like open dumping and burning. The study addresses the need to move beyond blaming improper disposal by identifying the specific corporate entities responsible for the plastic waste entering the marine environment.

**Methodology**
The researcher employed a brand audit methodology based on the Break Free From Plastic (BFFP) toolkit. This involved conducting coastal clean-up activities across the four selected barangays. During these activities, plastic waste was systematically collected and categorized using standardized audit data cards. The items were classified based on four key parameters: brand name (the manufacturer), item description, type of product (e.g., food packaging, personal care), and material composition (including the specific type of plastic and the number of layers). The data was then analyzed to rank the top ten manufacturers contributing to the plastic waste in the municipality.

**Findings**
The findings reveal a consistent pattern across all four barangays: food packaging (FP) is the most prevalent type of plastic waste. In Barangay Dapdap, food packaging accounted for 91.6% of the waste, while in Dancalan, it was 81.0%, in Sabang 75.5%, and in Mabuhay 55.2%. The most common material identified was Low-Density Polyethylene (LDPE), which is frequently used for flexible wrappers and sachets. Furthermore, a significant portion of the waste consisted of multi-layer (ML) plastics, which are particularly problematic because their complex structures make them difficult to recycle.

The brand audit identified the top corporate contributors to plastic pollution in Bulusan. Universal Robina Corp. was the largest contributor, accounting for 25.48% of the total waste collected. Other major contributors included Unilever (11.43%), Monde Nissin Corporation (9.52%), Liwayway Holdings Company Limited (8.57%), and Coca-Cola Beverages Philippines, Inc. (8.57%). The results highlight that single-use, sachet-based products from these major corporations are primary drivers of local marine pollution.

**Conclusions and Implications**
The study concludes that marine plastic pollution in Bulusan is driven by a heavy reliance on single-use, multi-layer, and LDPE plastic packaging, particularly for food and personal care products. The high prevalence of these materials suggests that current waste management practices are insufficient to handle the volume and complexity of modern packaging. The research implies that while community behavior and local waste management infrastructure are important, they are only part of the solution; the responsibility must also extend to the producers of the plastic.

The implications of these findings suggest a need for a multi-stakeholder approach. For Local Government Units (LGUs), the study underscores the necessity of stricter enforcement of ordinances regarding single-use plastics and the implementation of the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework to hold manufacturers accountable. For the community, there is a clear need for enhanced education and awareness campaigns regarding waste segregation and sustainable consumption. Finally, the study suggests that fostering partnerships between the government, businesses, and the community is essential to creating a sustainable waste management system that can effectively mitigate the environmental and economic impacts of plastic pollution in Bulusan.

title: STEM Students' Direct and Deferred Conceptual Understanding and Self-efficacy Using the Inverted Learning Approach in Biology: An Explanatory Sequential Mixed Methods Study
abstract: This study employed an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design. It explored how an inverted learning approach affected the direct and deferred conceptual understanding, as well as self-efficacy of STEM students enrolled in a biology course. It also sought to understand the experiences of students who were taught using the Inverted Learning Approach (ILA). A total of 225 STEM students were involved in the study. Findings revealed that students who were exposed to ILA had higher normalized gains in both posttest and retention test scores than those who were taught using the expository online teaching (EOT). Likewise, there was also a significant difference on the self-efficacy level between ILA and EOT groups. It therefore showed that ILA improved students' direct and deferred conceptual understanding, and self efficacy levels than their counterparts. Reflexive thematic analysis was applied to elucidate the qualitative information gathered. Four (4) themes emerged from the researcher's engagement with the participants exposed to ILA, which include: 1) Developing into active and reflective learners; 2) Enabling students to engage and collaborate more freely; 3) Establishing a flexible, seamless, and nonpressuring space for learning; and, 4) Becoming disciplined and responsible for one’s own learning. Even though there was a significant increment in the levels of direct and deferred conceptual understanding and self-efficacy among students taught using ILA, it was indicated that conceptual understanding is not highly related or associated with self-efficacy. Given the paucity of research in this area, further study is still needed to elucidate the complex relationships between self-efficacy, and direct and deferred conceptual understanding.

half:
Rolly James F. Cheng investigated the impact of the Inverted Learning Approach (ILA) on the academic performance and psychological constructs of STEM students in a biology course. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, the study compared the ILA against an Expository Online Teaching (EOT) method. The research measured direct conceptual understanding, deferred conceptual understanding through retention tests, student self-efficacy, and the lived experiences of students using the ILA.

Quantitative findings indicate that the ILA is more effective than the EOT method. Students in the ILA group demonstrated higher normalized gains in both posttest scores and retention test scores. Additionally, the ILA group reported significantly higher self-efficacy levels than the EOT group, suggesting the model bolsters both subject mastery and confidence.

Qualitative analysis identified four themes explaining the ILA's effectiveness: it helps students become active and reflective learners, enables peer engagement and collaboration, creates a flexible and non-pressuring environment, and encourages discipline and responsibility for one's own learning.

In conclusion, while the ILA significantly improved conceptual understanding and self-efficacy, the researcher found no specific correlation between these variables, suggesting high comprehension does not automatically translate to higher self-efficacy or vice versa. The study implies that implementing ILA can improve comprehension, retention, and confidence while fostering soft skills like self-discipline and collaboration. Further study is required to understand the complex relationships between these cognitive and psychological constructs.

Furthermore, these students also showed higher normalized gains in their retention test scores, suggesting that the ILA is effective in fostering deferred conceptual understanding. Beyond academic performance, the study found a significant difference in self-efficacy levels, with the ILA group reporting higher self-efficacy than the EOT group. This suggests that the inverted model not only aids in subject mastery but also bolsters students' confidence in their academic abilities.

First, the approach helped students develop into active and reflective learners. Second, the ILA enabled students to engage and collaborate more freely with their peers. Third, the method established a learning environment that was perceived as flexible, seamless, and non-pressuring. Finally, the approach encouraged students to become more disciplined and responsible for their own learning processes. Specifically, the results indicated that conceptual understanding is not highly related or associated with self-efficacy. This finding suggests that while a student may understand the material well, it does not automatically translate to higher self-efficacy, or vice versa.

title: Mainspring Books Smart Financial Management System (MBSFMS)
abstract: MainSpring Books is a Book publishing company located in Salinas Drive, Lahug, Cebu City that offer services that give life to every author’s manuscript. The company provides publishing services, online marketing and editing services to authors. As the company grows, it is difficult for them to track their financial status due to manual accounting. Manual accounting involves the recording of their business’ financial information and transactions, in which orders, invoices, expenses, and bank reconciliation are maintained using Microsoft Excel Spreadsheets to store, classify and analyze financial transactions of the company [1]. This project introduces a system to the company that converts their manual accounting process to a centralized financial management system. The system is developed to improve their accounting process to a faster, efficient and accurate account reporting. The Agile Method is the method used by the researchers in order to properly manage the activities and system functionalities.

To address these challenges, the project introduces a centralized financial management system designed to convert existing manual accounting processes into a digital, integrated platform. The primary objective of the MBSFMS is to improve accounting processes by making them faster, more efficient, and more accurate regarding account reporting. The researcher utilized the Agile Method to manage the development of the system.

Findings indicate that the implementation of the MBSFMS provides a solution to the limitations of manual spreadsheet-based accounting. By transitioning to a centralized system, the company can move away from the complexities of manual data entry and classification in Excel, allowing for more streamlined financial management. The development of the MBSFMS serves as a technological intervention to modernize financial operations, allowing for more reliable and timely financial reporting.

title: Online Grading System for Mindanao State University Maigo School of Arts and Trades
abstract: This paper presents an online grading system for Mindanao State University Maigo School of Arts and Trades that was developed to collect, process, and return the grades produced by faculty members. It discusses the design requirements, features, and implementation of the online grading system, as well as reactions from Faculty members and Students. It is shown that this system has a number of advantages over analog grading methods, including scalability, real-time feedback on the status of grading, the reduced potential for human error in compiling grades, the ability for faculty members members to grade remotely and to revise their grades after submission, the ability to return both provisional and final grades to the course faculty, and students in a timely manner, and the ability to archive and export grading data for future use. Although the online system is a clear improvement over manual or paper based, it is also shown that small details can interfere with usability and thus user satisfaction and that compatibility with mobile devices is a necessary, but still unaddressed, requirement. The application can run locally on an on premise server, or hosted from a web-server on the Internet. It is developed using PHP and can be hosted on either a Linux or Windows server via XAMPP and using a MySQL server. The application itself will feature a front-end and a back-end system and will be secured by a user management module. The users will be grouped into either faculty, student, admin and super admin where all backend configurations are. The Online Grading System intends to solve the problems met in the manual process of the grading system.

half:
This research addresses the inefficiencies of manual, paper-based grading at Mindanao State University Maigo School of Arts and Trades, noting that traditional methods are prone to human error and lack modern administrative efficiency. To resolve these issues, the study proposes a web-based online grading system designed to streamline the grading lifecycle for faculty, students, administrators, and super administrators.

The methodology involved developing a PHP-based application compatible with Linux and Windows servers, which can be deployed locally via XAMPP and MySQL or hosted on the internet. The system architecture includes a front-end and a back-end secured by a user management module that categorizes users into four distinct groups.

Findings demonstrate that the online system offers significant advantages over analog methods, including scalability, real-time feedback, and increased transparency. The system reduces manual compilation errors and provides faculty with greater flexibility through remote grading and the ability to revise grades. It also facilitates the timely return of provisional and final grades and allows for the archiving and exporting of data.

The study concludes that while the system successfully solves manual process problems, refinements are needed regarding usability and mobile device compatibility. Digitalizing the grading process is essential for institutional efficiency and data accuracy, though developers must prioritize usability and mobile optimization to meet evolving technological needs.

title: Social Media as Platforms for Disclosure Among University Students Diagnosed with Clinical Depression
abstract:
In this grounded study, I aimed to understand the role social media plays in the disclosures of university students diagnosed with clinical depression. Using triangulation mixed-method design in gathering, analyzing and interpreting data, I extracted the following: (1) the reasons why university students diagnosed with clinical depression disclose online, (2) the characteristics of social media that entice them to use it, and (3) how social media as a communication platform became a common ground for disclosures. The Uses and Gratifications Theory was used as a lens in understanding and explaining integrated findings from the gathered data. 

It was found that university students diagnosed with clinical depression use and disclose on social media because of the following motivations: (1) social interaction, (2) identity-seeking, (3) information-seeking and sharing, and (4) escapism. 

On the other hand, the characteristics and features of social media platforms that entice them to disclose them are the following (1) Social Media Strengthens Different Expressions of Oneself, (2) Social Media Supports Creation of a Safe Online Environment/Space, (3) Social Media Allows Compartmentalization of Personalities, (4) Social Media Bridges Distance and Promotes Building of Communities, (5) Social Media Helps Make Online Help/Support Available Instantly, Immediately, and 24/7, (6) Social Media Encourages Content Brevity, (7) Social Media Promotes Understanding of Others, (8) Social Media Allows Audience to React on Posts, and (9) Social Media Encourages Promotion of Various Advocacies. 

Through social media content analysis, thefollowing findings also emerged: (1) Photos with Captions dominate post in Instagram with the use of emoticons, (2) Majority of the Facebook posts are photos and memes which are shared from other users' posts, and (3) Most Engagements Happen Through Replies and Retweets on Twitter. 

In the analysis of the contents shared on all the platforms, four themes emerged. These are advocacies, personal struggles, popular culture, and relationships. Another one emerged in Instagram: the emotions and feelings of introversion and isolation. Of all these, popular culture is the most frequent subject of the participants' posts in all three platforms. 

Another finding is the participants' consumption of memes. Memes have become a new format of addressing issues that rarely get talked about, in a funny way. While Instagram offers a more filtered but a more creative expression of oneself and Twitter is for the authentic and uncensored postings, Facebook is a mixture of both, and memes are becoming tools balancing authentic but less dramatic and more fun disclosures. 

This study further showed the need for social media as a communication space to be kept safe and conducive for healing and recovery. It is recommended that all stakeholders and all active social media users be mindful of our and other people's online behavior so we can respond well to those who are suffering and in need of our help.

half:
This grounded study investigates the role of social media in the disclosures of university students diagnosed with clinical depression. Using a triangulation mixed-method design and the Uses and Gratifications Theory, the research examines the motivations, platform characteristics, and functional roles of social media in these disclosures.

Findings indicate that students are motivated to disclose on social media for four primary reasons: social interaction, identity-seeking, information-seeking and sharing, and escapism. Social media platforms entice students by allowing for the compartmentalization of personalities, bridging distances, and building communities. These platforms provide 24/7 access to support and offer features such as content brevity, audience reactions, and the promotion of various advocacies.

Content analysis revealed platform-specific patterns: Instagram posts are dominated by photos with captions and emoticons; Facebook posts consist mostly of photos and shared memes; and Twitter engagement occurs through replies and retweets. Across all platforms, the most frequent subject of posts is popular culture, followed by themes of advocacies, personal struggles, and relationships. Instagram content specifically highlights emotions related to introversion and isolation. Additionally, memes serve as a format to address rare issues through humor. While Instagram offers creative self-expression and Twitter facilitates authentic, uncensored posting, Facebook provides a mixture of both. The study concludes that social media must remain a safe space for healing, recommending that users remain mindful of their online behavior toward those in need.

To achieve these objectives, the researcher employed a triangulation mixed-method design for the gathering, analysis, and interpretation of data, utilizing the Uses and Gratifications Theory as a theoretical lens.

The findings reveal that university students diagnosed with clinical depression are motivated to use and disclose on social media for four primary reasons: social interaction, identity-seeking, information-seeking and sharing, and escapism. These motivations drive students to utilize digital spaces to navigate their mental health challenges and social needs.

It allows for the compartmentalization of personalities, bridges distances, and promotes the building of communities. Furthermore, social media provides instant, immediate, and 24/7 access to online help and support. Other enticing features include the encouragement of content brevity, the promotion of understanding of others, the ability for audiences to react to posts, and the encouragement of various advocacies.

Through a content analysis of social media, specific patterns emerged regarding how different platforms are utilized. On Instagram, posts are dominated by photos accompanied by captions and emoticons. On Facebook, the majority of posts consist of photos and memes shared from other users. On Twitter, most engagement occurs through replies and retweets. When analyzing the actual content shared across all three platforms, four main themes emerged: advocacies, personal struggles, popular culture, and relationships. Instagram content specifically highlighted themes of emotions and feelings related to introversion and isolation. Among all the subjects analyzed, popular culture was found to be the most frequent subject of the participants' posts across all three platforms.

The study also highlights the role of memes in the disclosure process, noting they have emerged as a new format for addressing issues that are rarely discussed by using humor. The research notes distinct functional differences between the platforms: Instagram offers a more filtered but creative expression of the self, while Twitter is used for authentic and uncensored postings. Facebook serves as a mixture of both styles, and memes are increasingly used as tools to balance authentic disclosure with a less dramatic and more fun approach.

In conclusion, the study emphasizes the necessity of maintaining social media as a communication space that is safe and conducive to healing and recovery. The researcher recommends that all stakeholders and active social media users remain mindful of their online behavior toward others to ensure users respond effectively to those who are suffering and in need of assistance.

title: Nizwa College of Technology Mobile Library Assistant
abstract: NCT Mobile Library Assistant is a mobile application of library system of Nizwa College of Technology to run in Android platforms by providing a downloadable APK (Android Application Package), which aims to increase the rate of usage of the academic library and make collections more accessible to students, faculty members and staff. The application aims to take advantage of the technology that will help analyze user's usage and level of engagement and satisfaction to library that can benefit to the improvement of services and facilities currently being offered. Nowadays, Nizwa College of Technology has a high expenditure on the library system that is not being fully maximized by students and staff. The proposal of developing an accessible, adaptable and user-friendly mobile library application can lead to high percentage of usage and new method of engaging students and staff to further promotes the library services. NCT Mobile Library Assistant application was integrated to the existing online library system of the school using software development life cycle methodology, lonic which is a powerful HTML5 SDK that mainly focus on the look and feel, and UI interaction using web technologies like CSS, HTML and Javascript, AngularJS and Lumen which is a PHP micro framework to build an application interface. NCT Mobile Library Assistant application was tested out by several students, staff and faculty members of Nizwa College of Technology.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
The Nizwa College of Technology (NCT) Mobile Library Assistant is an Android-based application designed to increase library usage and improve accessibility for students, faculty, and staff. The project was prompted by inefficiencies in the current library system, where high expenditure on resources has not resulted in maximum utilization by the campus community. By leveraging mobile technology, the application aims to analyze user engagement, usage patterns, and satisfaction levels to assist the institution in improving library services and facilities.

To develop the solution, the developer followed a structured software development life cycle to integrate the mobile application with the college's existing online library system. The technical framework utilized the Ionic HTML5 SDK, HTML, CSS, and Javascript to focus on user interface interaction and aesthetics. Additionally, AngularJS and Lumen, a PHP micro framework, were employed to build the application interface.

Findings were derived from a testing phase involving a diverse group of students, staff, and faculty members to evaluate functionality and the application's capacity to meet the specific needs of the college environment. The conclusions suggest that an accessible, adaptable, and user-friendly mobile application can lead to higher library usage. The application serves as a vital tool for data collection, providing insights into user engagement and satisfaction to drive future improvements to library facilities and services.

title: The Booksale, The Main Classified Ads Website for Books
abstract: Online bookselling had been vibrant for years. However, for a private individual or small business, there were some challenges. Among them were restrictions put on sellers of used books, while major websites only sold new books. Although classified ads websites were an alternative, book ads often got buried under those websites' numerous categories. The proposed solution to tackle these challenges was the website called The Booksale, which aimed to become the main classified ads website for books. Among its objectives were to provide a new platform for online bookselling, allow sellers to post as many ads as they want for free, and be a dedicated ads site for books. During research, the Information System Theory utilized was Michael Porter's Differentiation Focus under Competitive Advantage. Based on The Booksale's focus on books, it allowed an increased competitive advantage for the booksellers. For the development of the website, the software development life cycle approach used was the Rapid Application Development (RAD) method. Several clients were approached who provided responses for a Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats (SWOT) Analysis. To assess the success of the project, the clients also gave feedback for the User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and System Usability Scale (SUS) survey. Based on these results, it was concluded that the project achieved its objectives. When fully implemented, this project could open opportunities for online booksellers, especially private individuals and small businesses. With nothing else like it today, it contributed to the current Information Systems knowledge.

The research addresses a gap in the online marketplace where major retailers focus primarily on new books, international platforms impose high barriers to entry for small sellers, and general classified sites lack the specialized categorization necessary for book enthusiasts to find specific titles.

The project aimed to create a dedicated environment for selling e-books, new books, and used paperbacks, allowing verified owners to post unlimited advertisements for free. Using Michael Porter’s Competitive Advantage theory, specifically the "Differentiation Focus" strategy, the author sought to provide a more relevant service to the niche book market than generalist competitors.

The development followed the Rapid Application Development (RAD) model, utilizing an iterative prototyping approach. The technical architecture included HTML, CSS, and jQuery for the client-side interface, with Microsoft ASP.NET and C# for server-side operations. Data was managed through a Microsoft SQL Server relational database and hosted via GearHost.com. To ensure efficiency, scalability, and maintainability, the author applied software design principles such as "Don't Repeat Yourself" (DRY), "Separation of Concerns," "You Ain't Gonna Need It" (YAGNI), and "Keep It Simple, Stupid" (KISS).

Evaluation of the system involved a SWOT analysis, User Acceptance Testing (UAT), and a System Usability Scale (SUS) survey. The SWOT analysis highlighted the opportunity to provide specialized categories, such as Textbooks and Graphic Novels, which are often buried on general sites. UAT involved clients testing functionalities like account registration, filtered searching, and ad posting. The SUS survey was used to measure overall usability.

The findings indicated that the project successfully achieved its objectives. UAT results showed that core features, such as searching, viewing ad details, and posting ads, functioned as expected. While users provided minor feedback regarding the visibility of remarks and the ability to rate one's own transactions, the SUS and UAT data confirmed the website was functional and met user requirements.

In conclusion, The Booksale provides a free, dedicated, and user-friendly platform for book commerce. The project demonstrates that a niche-focused approach can address specific pain points overlooked by larger platforms. The work suggests that specialized information systems can empower small-scale entrepreneurs and collectors by removing financial and administrative barriers. The Booksale, The Main Classified Ads Website for Books is a Master of Information Systems thesis by James L. Gagni Jr., submitted to the University of the Philippines Open University in December 2018. The project focuses on the development of a specialized web-based platform designed to facilitate the buying and selling of books through a dedicated classified ads interface.

The problem addressed by this research is the lack of a specialized, accessible, and cost-effective online marketplace for book enthusiasts, particularly private individuals and small businesses. The author identifies three primary challenges in the existing market. First, major online retailers like National Bookstore and Lulu.com focus almost exclusively on new books, leaving a gap for the used book market. Second, large-scale international platforms like Amazon and AbeBooks impose significant barriers to entry for small-scale sellers, including transaction fees and stringent seller requirements. Third, general classified ads websites like OLX Philippines often bury book-related advertisements under broad, unrelated categories such as "Sports and Hobbies," making it difficult for buyers to find specific titles.

To address these issues, the project established several objectives: to provide a new platform for selling e-books, new books, and used paperbacks; to allow verified owners to post unlimited ads for free; and to create a dedicated environment specifically for books. The theoretical framework for the project is based on Michael Porter’s Competitive Advantage theory, specifically the "Differentiation Focus" strategy. By focusing exclusively on the niche market of books, the platform aims to provide a more relevant and specialized service than generalist competitors.

The methodology employed for the development of the website followed the Rapid Application Development (RAD) model, which emphasizes iterative delivery and prototyping. The technical implementation utilized a web-based architecture consisting of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript (specifically jQuery) for the client-side interface, and the Microsoft ASP.NET framework with C# for server-side operations. Data was managed using a Microsoft SQL Server relational database, and the application was hosted via GearHost.com. The author also utilized several software design principles, including "Don't Repeat Yourself" (DRY), "Separation of Concerns," "You Ain't Gonna Need It" (YAGNI), and "Keep It Simple, Stupid" (KISS) to ensure the system was efficient, scalable, and maintainable.

To evaluate the system, the author conducted a SWOT analysis, User Acceptance Testing (UAT), and a System Usability Scale (SUS) survey. The SWOT analysis identified that while book ads on general sites had low visibility, The Booksale could capitalize on the opportunity to provide unlimited free posts and specialized categories (such as Textbooks and Graphic Novels). The UAT involved multiple clients who tested specific functionalities, such as account registration, searching with filters, posting ads, and reviewing sellers. The SUS survey was used to measure the overall usability of the application.

The findings from the testing phases indicated that the project successfully achieved its objectives. The UAT results showed that most features—including searching, viewing ad details, and posting new ads—functioned "as expected." While some users provided minor feedback regarding the visibility of certain remarks or the ability to rate one's own transactions, the core functionalities were validated. The SUS results and UAT data confirmed that the website was functional and met the requirements of the intended users.

In conclusion, the author states that The Booksale successfully met its goals of providing a free, dedicated, and user-friendly platform for book commerce. The project demonstrates that a niche-focused approach can provide a competitive advantage by addressing the specific pain points of a particular user group that larger, generalized platforms overlook.

The implications of this work suggest that specialized information systems can empower small-scale entrepreneurs and private collectors by removing the financial and administrative barriers present in larger marketplaces. The project contributes to the field of Information Systems by providing a practical application of Porter’s Differentiation Focus strategy in the context of e-commerce. The author suggests that the platform could further evolve by incorporating more advanced features, such as expanded statistical dashboards for sellers and enhanced recommendation systems.

title: Survey Management Information System for the Novaliches District Hospital
abstract: The Survey Statistics Information System is intended for use by the research and administrative staff of the Novaliches District Hospital to streamline their patient satisfaction survey process. Since the current process is, depending on department, either to get all patients, or to use convenience sampling, there would either be too much work (if all patients were surveyed), or a possibility of bias (since not all patients have an equal chance of selection). The objective of this information system is to move surveys towards a probability sampling, which saves time and effort on the staff implementing the survey. The information system also provides automated statistical reporting with visualizations, which translates into actionable insights on the part of hospital administration, without needing to hire trained statisticians to interpret statistical reports.

title: Integrated Information Systems for Enhanced Accounts Management
abstract: The University Computer Center, an office under the office of the Chancellor of the University of the Philippines Diliman, utilizes an increasing number of information systems to manage the Diliman Network accounts and related services To improve efficiency and raise productivity, this project integrated several information systems into one enhanced accounts management website The new website consolidated the functionalities of several information systems into one with three main (3) modules (1) accounts management module. (2) mail module, and (3) proxy module. It also enhanced the existing features of these modules. The development was divided into three (3) major phases covering each module Through the use of Technology Acceptance Model theory, the perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use of the integrated system was evaluated to determine if the project achieved its goal. The reported findings show there is a significant relationship between the perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness which affects the attitude of the administrators towards using the new website. There is a strong correlation between perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness. Perceived usefulness has stronger correlation compared to perceived ease of use on the attitude toward using. Based on these findings, the goal of the project to integrate and enhance the accounts management is achieved.

title: Blockchain-Based Diplomas Verification System for Higher Educational Institutions in the Philippines
abstract: Diploma forgery is a perennial problem in the Philippines. It invalidated the time, effort, and abilities required to obtain a degree in both the higher education system and the workplace. In recent years, there have been multiple instances of academic credential fabrication. One of them was of a high-ranking Department of Foreign Affairs official who fabricated her academic credentials and worked for the government as an Assistant Secretary, [1] a position that needed not only a bachelor's degree but also extensive experience and academic achievements. In this project, the proponent created a tamper-proof, efficient, and publicly available blockchain-based diploma verification system to expedite diploma verification for any higher educational institution in the Philippines. The platform did not require corporations, entities, or any other public entity to create and manage a blockchain wallet in order to access and verify diplomas minted on the blockchain network. To assess the project's success, a platform prototype was created and tested by (10) volunteers. Following the use of the system, a survey on the efficiency of the prototype in authenticating diplomas over the internet was supplied. Overall, the project aimed to demonstrate the dependability and effectiveness of using blockchain technology to authenticate academic credentials such as diplomas in order to prevent document fraud and forgery.

The issue of diploma forgery represents a perennial problem within the Philippines, creating significant negative consequences for both the higher education system and the professional workplace. When academic credentials are falsified, it effectively invalidates the time, effort, and genuine abilities that individuals invest in obtaining their degrees. This problem is not merely theoretical but has manifested in high-profile instances of academic credential fabrication. One notable example involved a high-ranking Department of Foreign Affairs official who fabricated her academic credentials to secure a position as an Assistant Secretary. This specific role required not only a bachelor's degree but also extensive experience and significant academic achievements, making the forgery a serious matter of professional integrity. Such instances highlight the urgent need for a more robust method to ensure the authenticity of academic documents.

To address these challenges, the proponent developed a blockchain-based diploma verification system designed to be tamper-proof, efficient, and publicly available. The primary goal of this project was to expedite the diploma verification process for any higher educational institution located in the Philippines. By utilizing blockchain technology, the system aims to provide a secure way to authenticate academic credentials and prevent the ongoing issues of document fraud and forgery. A key feature of this proposed platform is its accessibility; it was designed so that corporations, entities, or any other public entity would not be required to create and manage a blockchain wallet in order to access and verify diplomas that have been minted on the blockchain network. This design choice aims to lower the barrier to entry for employers and institutions that need to verify credentials quickly and reliably.

The methodology used to assess the success of this project involved the creation of a platform prototype. This prototype was subjected to testing by ten volunteers to evaluate its functionality and usability. Following the period of use, a survey was conducted to gather data regarding the efficiency of the prototype in authenticating diplomas over the internet. This testing phase was essential to determine whether the blockchain-based approach could meet the practical needs of stakeholders in the authentication process. Through this empirical approach, the project sought to gather direct feedback on how effectively the technology performs in a real-world simulation of diploma verification.

The findings and the overall aim of the project center on demonstrating the dependability and effectiveness of using blockchain technology for the authentication of academic credentials. By creating a system where diplomas are minted on a blockchain, the project seeks to provide a permanent and unalterable record of academic achievement. The goal is to move away from traditional, potentially vulnerable methods of verification toward a digital solution that is inherently resistant to tampering. The project aims to show that such a system can successfully prevent document fraud and forgery, thereby protecting the integrity of the educational system and ensuring that academic achievements are accurately represented in the workplace.

The implications of this work suggest that implementing blockchain technology could significantly transform how higher educational institutions in the Philippines manage and verify academic records. By providing a public and efficient verification tool, the system can help restore trust in academic credentials and protect the value of legitimate degrees. The ability for entities to verify diplomas without the complexity of managing blockchain wallets makes the technology more practical for widespread adoption by employers and government agencies. Ultimately, the project serves as a demonstration of how decentralized ledger technology can be applied to solve long-standing societal problems related to document authenticity and professional integrity.

title: Go Guro Mobile Application Built with Android and Firebase
abstract:
In universities or colleges, most students have control of their class schedule. There's also instances of irregular students, whose class times are different, depending on what's available during enrolment. Hence, there are times a student needs help with a lesson, making a project, or reviewing for exams, but there are no available professors or classmates. To find help, one must roam the campus and ask other students face-to-face. Often, they will be discouraged to ask because of fear of rejection or that they're too shy to ask.

The proposal is Go Guro, a mobile application for students who need help quick. The tutee selects the subject they need help and with a press of a button, the app instantly searches for nearby people who also have the app. The tutors can choose to accept or decline the tutee's invitation. Once accepted, a map shows the location of both which can be used to find each other. Once they meet in-person, the study session can now be started by the tutor.

Mobile devices using Android 4.0.3 "Ice Cream Sandwich" up to Android 8.0 "Oreo" was targeted. Android Studio was used for development with Java as the programming language. Firebase was used to provide backend services.

Testing resulted in satisfactory remarks from end-users, indicating that it is practical to use in their college. They would also like to see it published on Google Play for every student and teacher to use, regardless of school. The application lessened the user's rejection fears by making the invitations anonymous, meaning the tutee cannot see the name and face of the tutor and vice-versa. Only when the tutor accepts the invite will they see each other's names and faces. Go Guro does not show the tutors who have rejected the invite, but only those who accepted.
faculty: Faculty of Information and Communication Studies
half:
Jeano Frederick U. Ermitano developed the "Go Guro" Android application to address the difficulties students face when seeking academic assistance. Traditional methods of finding tutors, such as walking around campus, are often physically taxing and time-consuming. Furthermore, many students experience a fear of rejection when asking for help in person. To mitigate these issues, the application connects tutees with nearby tutors, reducing physical effort and minimizing the psychological impact of rejection through the use of anonymity.

The application was developed using Java in Android Studio, targeting Android versions 4.0.3 to 8.0. The developer utilized Firebase and GeoFire for location-based features and Glide for profile photo management. The development process included programming, testing, and revising the prototype over approximately ten weeks.

The project was evaluated through user testing with 21 participants from AMA Computer College - Las Piñas and De La Salle - College of Saint Benilde. Using the System Usability Scale (SUS), the study measured perceived ease of use. Findings were generally positive, with most respondents agreeing that the app was easy to use and that they would use it frequently. Participants felt the functions were well-integrated and could be learned quickly. Ultimately, "Go Guro" successfully provides a portable, user-friendly platform that lowers social and physical barriers to academic peer support.

The "Go Guro" mobile application project, authored by Jeano Frederick U. Ermitano, addresses the difficulties students face when seeking academic assistance. In many university settings, students—especially irregular students with non-standard schedules—often find it difficult to locate available tutors. Traditional methods of finding help, such as walking around campus to ask professors or peers, are physically taxing and time-consuming. Additionally, many students experience a fear of rejection when asking for help in person, which can discourage them from seeking necessary academic support.

To address these issues, the author developed "Go Guro," an Android application designed to connect tutees with nearby tutors efficiently. The primary objectives were to reduce the physical effort required to find a tutor, minimize the number of steps taken by the student, and lessen the psychological impact of personal rejection through the use of anonymity. The application allows a tutee to select a topic and search for nearby tutors; once a tutor accepts the invitation, a map displays the location for a study session. To protect users, the app maintains anonymity by not revealing names or faces until the invitation is accepted.

The application was developed using Java within the Android Studio IDE, targeting devices running from Android 4.0.3 to Android 8.0. The author employed Firebase, specifically GeoFire, to facilitate map and location-based features, and Glide for managing user profile photos. The development process spanned approximately ten weeks, including programming the prototype, testing, and revising the system based on user feedback.

The methodology for evaluating the application involved user testing with 21 participants from AMA Computer College - Las Piñas and De La Salle - College of Saint Benilde. Testing was conducted using the System Usability Scale (SUS) to measure perceived ease of use. Participants used the app in both tutee and tutor roles before completing an online survey.

The findings from the usability testing were generally positive. According to the SUS results, a majority of respondents agreed or strongly agreed that they would like to use the app frequently and that it was easy to use. Most participants felt the functions were well-integrated and that they could learn to use the app quickly without significant assistance. While some respondents expressed neutral feelings regarding consistency, the overall feedback indicated the application was practical and user-friendly.

In conclusion, "Go Guro" successfully meets its design goals of providing a portable, easy-to-use platform for academic peer support. By leveraging Android and Firebase technologies, the application provides a functional solution to physical exhaustion and the fear of social rejection. The project demonstrates that mobile applications can serve as vital tools for enhancing student engagement and academic success by lowering social and physical barriers to seeking help.

The application allows a tutee to select a topic and search for nearby tutors; once a tutor accepts the invitation, a map displays the location for a study session. To protect users, the app maintains anonymity by not revealing names or faces until the invitation is accepted.

The project was developed as an Android application targeting devices running from Android 4.0.3 (Ice Cream Sandwich) to Android 8.0 (Oreo). The development utilized Java as the programming language within the Android Studio IDE. For backend services, the author employed Firebase, specifically using GeoFire to facilitate the map and location-based features. Additionally, Glide was used for managing user profile photos. The development process spanned approximately ten weeks, including time for programming the prototype, testing, and revising the system based on user feedback.

The methodology for evaluating the application involved user testing with 21 participants from AMA Computer College - Las Piñas and De La Salle - College of Saint Benilde. The testing was conducted using the System Usability Scale (SUS), a standardized Likert scale used to measure the perceived ease of use of a system. Participants were instructed to use the app in both tutee and tutor roles before completing an online survey via Google Forms.

The findings from the usability testing were generally positive. According to the System Usability Scale results, a majority of respondents agreed or strongly agreed that they would like to use the app frequently and that the app was easy to use. Most participants also felt that the various functions were well-integrated and that they would be able to learn to use the app quickly without significant assistance. While some respondents expressed neutral feelings regarding the consistency of the app, the overall feedback indicated that the application was practical and user-friendly.

In conclusion, the Go Guro mobile application successfully meets its design goals of providing a portable, easy-to-use platform for academic peer support. By leveraging Android and Firebase technologies, the application provides a functional solution to the problems of physical exhaustion and the fear of social rejection in a campus environment. The results of the usability testing confirm that the application is a practical tool for students, regardless of their specific school.

The implications of this work suggest that mobile technology can effectively bridge the gap in peer-to-peer learning environments. By implementing anonymity and location-based services, educational institutions could potentially increase the frequency of student interactions and academic support sessions. The project demonstrates that mobile applications can serve as vital tools for enhancing student engagement and academic success by lowering the social and physical barriers to seeking help.

title: Exploring The Perception of UPOU Students in Using Note Taking Applications on Academic Productivity
abstract: This qualitative study examines the perceptions of students at UP Open University (UPOU) regarding their use of note-taking applications and the perceived impact on their academic productivity. The research investigates the factors that motivate UPOU students to prefer digital note-taking applications and notebooks over traditional methods, highlighting the perceived advantages and limitations of these tools, as well as their perceived necessity for UPOU students and distant learners in general. Utilizing thematic analysis, the study draws on data from surveys and interviews conducted with 16 UPOU students who regularly use digital note-taking applications for academic purposes and found various general themes that align with the participants’ answers. The findings indicate a strong preference among students due to its convenience, accessibility, and efficiency. Features such as synchronization across devices and organizational tools are identified as particularly beneficial in enhancing productivity. However, challenges such as technical issues, subscription costs, and health-related concerns are also found. The stud concludes that while digital note-taking applications provide substantial benefits for improving academic productivity, their use should be customized to individual preferences and needs. Recommendations for future research include expanding the sample size, assessing the long-term effects of digital note-taking on academic performance, and evaluating the effectiveness of specific application features.

title: Design and Development of the UPLB Vehicle Sticker Management System
abstract: The University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB) aims to revamp its Vehicle Sticker Application system through the Office of the Vice Chancellor for Community Affairs and the Security and Safety Office. The existing online platform, developed hastily during the pandemic, has proven inefficient and user unfriendly, leading to user dissatisfaction. Operating on outdated technology (CodeIgniter v3), the system faces security and functionality issues. This project proposes a redesign and technology update to enhance the application process, making it accessible, efficient, and secure. The new system will streamline the registration, payment, and appointment processes by transitioning to a modern technology stack, such as Laravel and FilamentPHP. It aims to provide a user-friendly interface, real-time tracking, and improved management functionalities. This initiative addresses current system inadequacies and aligns with UPLB's commitment to campus security and efficient traffic management.

title: Communicative Competence Approach for Developing Alternative Learning System Learners' English Communication Skills
abstract: One hundred fourteen ALS secondary respondents from Pasig City were surveyed to analyze how can the Communicative Competence Approach be used to develop English communication skills in learners of the Alternative Learning System. Thus, the study determined their level of communicative competence, the effective communication-based approach, and factors that influence their English language use in different communication contexts. Guided by Canale and Swain’s Communicative Competence Framework (1980), results of the study revealed that the ALS secondary learners’ level is between the needs improvement and basic levels. The Communicative Competence Approach was identified as effective for developing their communicative competence, encouraging participation in authentic communication scenarios and practices. Using Spearman’s Rank Correlation Coefficient and data triangulation, results showed no significant relationship between the dimensions of communicative competence: (1) grammatical competence and strategic competence and (2) sociolinguistic competence and discourse competence. However, other dimensions, such as technological competence, digital literacy, and establishing clear communication between teachers and learners, emerged as important aspects of language use and competence. As presented in the study, the respondents’ level of English communicative competence and use of the language in different communication settings were influenced by several factors such as age, employment status, learning experience, stage of development, exposure to the native language (Filipino and other dialects or Philippine languages) and English, and access and familiarity with ICT tools.

This study investigates how the Communicative Competence Approach can be utilized to develop the English communication skills of learners within the Alternative Learning System. The research focuses on one hundred fourteen ALS secondary respondents located in Pasig City. The primary objective was to analyze the effectiveness of this approach in enhancing language skills and to determine the specific levels of communicative competence possessed by these learners. Furthermore, the study sought to identify the most effective communication-based approaches and the various factors that influence how these learners use the English language across different communication contexts.

The theoretical foundation is guided by the Communicative Competence Framework established by Canale and Swain. To achieve the research goals, the study employed a methodology involving surveys and data triangulation. The researcher utilized Spearman’s Rank Correlation Coefficient to analyze the relationships between the different dimensions of communicative competence. This allowed for a detailed examination of how various linguistic and social competencies interact within the specific educational context of the Alternative Learning System.

The findings indicate that the English communicative competence level of the ALS secondary learners falls between the needs improvement and basic levels. When evaluating the effectiveness of the Communicative Competence Approach, the results revealed that this method is effective for developing the communicative competence of the learners. Specifically, the approach encourages active participation in authentic communication scenarios and practices. Through the application of Spearman’s Rank Correlation Coefficient, the study showed that there is no significant relationship between grammatical competence and strategic competence. Similarly, there was no significant relationship between sociolinguistic competence and discourse competence. Despite these lack of correlations, technological competence, digital literacy, and the establishment of clear communication between teachers and learners emerged as important aspects of language use and competence.

Several factors influence the respondents' level of English communicative competence and their use of the language in various communication settings. These include the age of the learners and their employment status. Additionally, the learners' previous learning experiences and their current stage of development play a role in their linguistic abilities. Exposure to the native language, including Filipino and other dialects or Philippine languages, as well as exposure to English, impacts their competence. Finally, access to and familiarity with ICT tools were identified as significant factors in how these learners navigate communication.

The implications suggest that the Communicative Competence Approach should be prioritized to effectively improve English communication skills. Because the learners' current levels are at the needs improvement and basic stages, instructional methods should focus on creating authentic communication opportunities. Language development in this context is not solely dependent on traditional grammatical mastery but is also deeply intertwined with digital literacy and technological competence. Integrating ICT tools and fostering digital literacy could be vital strategies. Educators must also consider the diverse backgrounds of the learners, including their age, employment status, and linguistic exposure, to create more effective and inclusive communicative environments.

title: E-Farming System Knowledge Transfer: Exploring Experiences in the Philippines and Indonesia
abstract: Agriculture is complex and hermeneutic having epistemology in communications, innovations, politics, and society. This sector faces challenges in attaining food security due to climate change, low crop productivity and farm income, and aging farmer population. Traditional communication of crop advisories requires more time and has limited reach to farmers compared to digital communications. Although, the advances in digitalization also pose "last mile" challenges. Complexity theory in communication offers pedagogy and practice in E-farming knowledge transfer to smallholder and marginalized farmers. The theory has been utilized in digital social advocacy, neo-diffusionism communication, management, and social science. This study aims to theorize Complexity theory in digital knowledge transfers in agriculture to drive social impact through effective utilization of crop advisories in digital media, mobile applications, and Internet of Things (IoT). Autoethnography, Focus Group Discussion, Key Informant Interviews, and User Acceptability Test qualitative research methods as well as desktop quantitative research were utilized in this study. One hundred (100) farmer respondents and ten (10) key informants were interviewed in the Philippines and Indonesia. Results of the study showed that farmer motivations and needs are vital in digital crop advisory' success. The PCE (Planning-Communication-Evaluation) model is proposed leveraging Complexity theory. This model covers different interactions of adaptive agents in the social system including content developers, farmer personas, and other agents in the e-farming system. The social, digital adaptiveness, and muted voices of various farmer personas offer discourse to unravel and drive success in e- farming. The research findings also provide pragmatic and pedagogical implications of adaptive agents or nodes in digital farming advisories anchored from Complexity theory. Digital e farming communication and the use of artificial intelligence (AI) offer a discourse in the production and adaptation of the sociality and reproduction of society through these agents interacting in a fluid or non linear pattern.
