title: Job Satisfaction and Motivation among Filipino Nurses in the United Arab Emirates
abstract:
The influx of Filipino nurses into the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has notably transformed the healthcare landscape, with these dedicated cadre of professionals constituting a significant portion of the nursing workforce. Filipino nurses have been a substantial and indispensable element, contributing significantly to the efficient functioning of the UAE's healthcare system. The Filipino diaspora in healthcare settings worldwide is marked by its resilience, adaptability, and unwavering dedication to patient care. These dedicated healthcare professionals contribute significantly to the country's healthcare infrastructure. However, their job satisfaction and motivation have remained relatively underexplored despite their pivotal role, creating a conspicuous void in existing research within the domain of nursing workforce management. 

The existing body of research on nursing in the UAE predominantly centers on clinical practices, healthcare management, and patient outcomes. However, the psychosocial dimensions of job satisfaction and motivation among Filipino nurses in this unique context have been left conspicuously understudied. This gap in the literature presents an urgent call for  investigation and this conspicuous lacuna in the literature necessitates a dedicated investigation into the job satisfaction and motivation levels of Filipino nurses in the UAE. Understanding the determinants that influence job satisfaction and motivation is not only academically pertinent but also imperative for healthcare practitioners, policymakers, and administrators. By exploring the unique experiences, challenges, and factors that influence the job satisfaction and motivation of Filipino nurses, this research seeks to contribute substantially to the ongoing intellectual discourse surrounding the healthcare labor force, not only for Filipino Nursing Expatriates around the world but moreover, those who are based in the Philippines, thereby underscoring its significance to scholars, educators, students, and practitioners alike.

Conducting the type of study for the first time among Kabayan Nurses in the Middle East, this quantitative research investigated the correlation of job satisfaction and motivation of 117 Filipino nursing participants employed across the seven states of the United Arab Emirates (UAE). All research participants were licensed nurses and certified members of the Philippine Nursing Association in the UAE, reflecting a homogeneous and well defined sample. The research received full support from the Philippine Embassy in Abu Dhabi, emphasizing its significance.

Data for this study were collected using structured questionnaires distributed through an online survey platform, specifically Google Forms. The study employed a descriptive correlational research design, utilizing statistical measures such as mode, percentage, and mean to provide an overview of key aspects within the collected data. Furthermore, inferential statistics, including Pearson's correlation coefficient and Chi- square analysis, were utilized to draw conclusions based on the sample data, enabling an exploration of the relationship between job satisfaction and motivation.

As a result, the research yielded significant insights, as the Filipino Nurses who took part in the study exhibited positive levels of job satisfaction and motivation. Their responses underscored a consensus across various dimensions of their work environment, including aspects like salary, job security, working conditions, responsibility, cooperation, technical supervision qualities, and interpersonal relationships.

Significantly, the research established a strong positive correlation between job satisfaction and motivation among Filipino nurses in the United Arab Emirates. This implies that as job satisfaction levels increase, motivation levels also tend to rise, underscoring the importance of enhancing job satisfaction to boost motivation among this demographic. This finding has profound implications for healthcare organizations and policymakers in the UAE, suggesting that improving job satisfaction can be an effective strategy for enhancing nurses' work motivation.

Interestingly, the study revealed that job satisfaction and motivation remained unaffected by the demographic and professional profiles of Filipino nurses in the UAE. This highlights the complexity of these constructs, suggesting that factors beyond traditional profiling have a more significant impact on job satisfaction and motivation. This underscores the need for healthcare organizations and policymakers to adopt a broader and more comprehensive approach to address nurses' well-being and job satisfaction.

This pedagogical research contributed significantly to the body of knowledge as it illuminated the relationship between job satisfaction and motivation among Filipino nurses in the UAE. The findings provided valuable insights for healthcare organizations and policymakers in the Emirates, underscoring the significance of prioritizing job satisfaction as a means to enhance nurses' motivation. As a result, it was recommended that healthcare organizations in the country should have focused on creating work environments conducive to job satisfaction. This would have included fair compensation, job security, and nurturing positive interpersonal relationships, all of which were believed to have the potential to increase motivation levels among their Filipino nursing workforces.

Furthermore, this study calls for further research into the complex dynamics of job satisfaction and motivation in nursing, with the aim of offering a more comprehensive understanding of these critical factors within healthcare settings.

The thesis titled "Job Satisfaction and Motivation among Filipino Nurses in the United Arab Emirates" by Meridein Sanchez Pacamana investigates the relationship between job satisfaction and work motivation among Filipino nursing expatriates working in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

**Problem and Context**
The study is situated within the context of the significant role Filipino nurses play in the UAE healthcare system, where they constitute a substantial portion of the nursing workforce. Despite their essential contribution to the healthcare infrastructure, the psychosocial dimensions of their employment—specifically job satisfaction and motivation—have remained underexplored in existing literature. Most research in the UAE focuses on clinical practices and patient outcomes, leaving a gap in understanding the workforce management aspects of the Filipino nursing diaspora. This gap is particularly relevant given the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, which increased job demands and emotional weariness for frontline healthcare workers. The researcher identifies a need to understand these factors to improve nursing performance, reduce turnover, and enhance the overall effectiveness of healthcare organizations.

**Methodology**
The researcher employed a quantitative, descriptive-correlational research design. The study utilized a sample of 117 licensed Filipino nurses who were members of the Philippine Nursing Association (PNA) in the UAE, representing all seven emirates. Data collection was conducted through an online survey using Google Forms. The research instrument consisted of structured questionnaires designed to measure job satisfaction across seven indicators: responsibilities, rewards, job nature, promotional opportunities, supervision, co-workers, and working conditions. Motivation was measured through seven indicators: salary, job security, working conditions, responsibility, cooperation, technical supervision qualities, and interpersonal relationship quality. Statistical analysis included the use of mode, percentage, and mean for descriptive data, while Pearson Product Moment Correlation Coefficient and Chi-square tests of independence were used for inferential analysis to determine relationships between variables.

**Findings**
The results indicated that Filipino nurses in the UAE exhibit positive levels of both job satisfaction and motivation. Respondents expressed consensus and satisfaction across various dimensions, including salary, job security, working conditions, responsibility, cooperation, technical supervision, and interpersonal relationships. A significant finding of the study was the existence of a strong positive correlation between job satisfaction and motivation; as job satisfaction levels increase, motivation levels also tend to rise. Interestingly, the study revealed that neither job satisfaction nor motivation was significantly affected by the demographic or professional profiles of the nurses, such as age, gender, income, or years of service. This suggests that the drivers of satisfaction and motivation are complex and influenced by factors beyond traditional demographic characteristics.

**Conclusions**
The study concludes that job satisfaction and motivation are deeply interconnected among Filipino nurses in the UAE. The positive levels of satisfaction and motivation reported suggest that the current working environments for many of these professionals are conducive to their psychological and professional needs. However, the strong correlation between the two constructs highlights that any effort to boost nursing motivation must be rooted in improving job satisfaction. Furthermore, because demographic profiles did not significantly impact these constructs, the researcher concludes that management strategies should not be tailored based on age or gender, but rather should focus on universal workplace improvements that address the core dimensions of satisfaction and motivation.

**Implications**
The findings have significant implications for healthcare administrators and policymakers in the UAE. To enhance the motivation and performance of the Filipino nursing workforce, organizations should prioritize creating work environments that foster job satisfaction. Specific recommendations include ensuring fair compensation, providing job security, and nurturing positive interpersonal relationships and cooperation among staff. By focusing on these areas, healthcare organizations can improve staff effectiveness and potentially reduce turnover. The study also serves as a pedagogical contribution to the field of nursing administration, providing a foundation for developing strategic human resource management frameworks specifically designed for the unique needs of migrant nursing professionals. Finally, the researcher calls for further studies to explore the complex dynamics of these constructs in more diverse or different healthcare settings.

title: Sociodemographic Factors and Quality of Life (QoL) Among Family Caregivers of Cancer Patients in Saudi Arabia
abstract: The current trend in cancer treatment involves inpatient hospital care and continuity of care in a home care setting; thus, the family caregiver plays an essential role in implementing the patient's treatment plan. The family caregiver provides support such as disease monitoring, management of signs and symptoms, pain management, homemedication administration, emotional support, and personal assistance. These complex responsibilities of the family caregiver put them under stress that may affect their quality of life (QoL). The findings of this study revealed that most family caregivers of cancer patients in Saudi Arabia have moderate QoL (55.71 %), while the rest have poor QoL (31.43%) or good QoL (12.86%). Results also showed that burden has low quality of life score and positive adaptation results in ahigher quality of life score. Furthermore, male family caregivers have a more impaired quality of life than female family caregivers. Likewise, family caregivers of male patients and patients with metastatic cancer have poorer quality of life. Several studies on the quality of life of family caregivers of cancer patients were conducted worldwide, but there is limited data and scarce literature that evaluates it in Saudi Arabian context. Thus, the results of this study may serve as baseline data in identifying the quality of life of family caregivers of cancer patients in Saudi Arabia and its relationship with sociodemographic factors. Moreover, the result may serve as a source for developing programs to improve the quality of life of family caregivers.

title: Caring Processes and Level of Engagement among Informal Caregivers of Older Persons in a Tertiary Hospital in Metro Manila, Philippines
abstract: Informal caregiver care is a critical aspect that is involved among hospitalized older persons. The study aims to identify the association between the caring processes and the level of informal caregiver engagement. The Caring process among informal caregivers of older persons was identified using a Likert style questionnaire. It is composed of five determinants, namely Knowing, Being With, Doing for, Enabling, and Maintaining Belief. The first phase of Knowing involved being overall aware of the condition of the informal caregivers admitted older person. Being with is the second caring process in which the informal caregiver was physically and emotionally with the patient. Doing for is the third phase in which care was rendered with dignity, as if the older person were doing it for himself. The fourth process is enabling, in which the transition of care was facilitated towards self-care. Lastly, maintaining belief focused on maintaining the older person¶s hope and faith-filled attitude as he or she continued with his or her life. The level of informal caregiver engagement was identified following the principles of caregiver engagement with a Likert scale questionnaire. This involved three categories namely Policy and structure, Culture and Mindset, and Procedures. The study is a correlational quantitative study that involved informal caregivers answering printed questionnaires within 30 minutes. The results involved obtaining the frequency and percentage among informal caregivers¶ age, gender, and relationship with the patient. The dominant relationship in informal caregiving was spouse, the gender for informal caregiving was female and the result of age range was 48-58 years old. The descriptive statistics for the mean and standard deviation of the caring process determinants and level of informal caregiver engagement were then obtained. Finally, the mean and standard deviation of the caring process and the level of informal caregiver engagement were correlated using the IBM SPSS statistics software for identification of association. Results showed a positive correlation between the caring processes and the following: Policy and Structure, Culture and Mindset, and Procedures.

title: Effects Of Disaster Risk Reduction Training On The Locus Of Control And Health-Promoting Behavior Among School Disaster Coordinators In San Pablo City, Laguna
abstract: The disaster management program has shifted its emphasis during the last few decades from reactive to proactive Disaster Risk Reduction and Management or DRRM. One of the factors on the promotion of proactiveness in disaster risk reduction and management is health promotion which reduces risks, increases resilience, and mitigates the impact of disaster on health. This study aims to determine the effects of Disaster Risk Reduction Training to the levels of locus of control and health-promoting behavior of School Disaster Coordinators. Specifically, to identify the levels of health locus of control and health-promoting behavior before and after the Disaster Risk Reduction Training. Quasi-experimental study using pre-, and post-test one-group design was used and the standardized questionnaires namely: Demographic Profile, Multidimensional Health Locus of Control Scale (MHLC) and Health Promoting Lifestyle Profile II (HPLP II) to gather data from 85 respondents. Majority of the participants are male, the mean age is 36.05 years old, married, with bachelor's degree and has a monthly income under Salary Grade 13 or below, or at most P30,547.00. Results show that the yielded p-value for the overall composite score of the HPLP II (0.001) indicates that there is a significant difference between the pre- and post-training health promoting behaviors. For the MHLC, the p-value of the internality LOC is 0.749. In this level, there is no significant difference in the participants' internality LOC before and after the disaster risk reduction training. In addition, the two other LOC, powerful others LOC and chance LOC have a p-value of both 0.000 which indicates training is effective in improving the externality LOC. These findings underscore the importance of enhancing learning programs in disaster risk reduction and disaster management to help develop and/or redesign such programs that will equip its learners towards disaster resiliency.

half:
Alexis Ray B. Janolino’s thesis investigates how specialized training influences the psychological and behavioral health profiles of school disaster coordinators in San Pablo City, Laguna. The study addresses a gap in literature regarding how training affects the specific psychological constructs and health behaviors of those managing school-based disasters as management shifts from reactive to proactive strategies.

Using a quasi-experimental one-group pre-test and post-test design, the researcher studied 85 coordinators. Data were collected via a Demographic Profile, the Multidimensional Health Locus of Control Scale (MHLC), and the Health Promoting Lifestyle Profile II (HPLP II). The intervention consisted of a two-day online School Disaster Risk Reduction and Management training facilitated by the Philippine Red Cross.

Findings showed that the training significantly improved health-promoting behaviors, as evidenced by a significant difference in the HPLP II composite scores (p=0.001). Regarding the MHLC, the training did not significantly alter the "internality" dimension (p=0.749), meaning participants' belief in their own ability to control their health remained unchanged. However, the training significantly impacted the "externality" dimensions of "powerful others" and "chance" (p=0.000).

The study concludes that while training does not change an individual's internal sense of control, it significantly influences perceptions of external factors and actual health-related lifestyle behaviors. The researcher suggests using these findings to redesign disaster risk reduction programs to foster resiliency by teaching both technical skills and personal health promotion.

Janolino’s thesis, "Effects Of Disaster Risk Reduction Training On The Locus Of Control And Health-Promoting Behavior Among School Disaster Coordinators In San Pablo City, Laguna," investigates how specialized training influences the psychological and behavioral health profiles of school disaster coordinators. The research addresses a gap in literature regarding how training affects the specific psychological constructs and health behaviors of those tasked with managing school-based disasters, particularly as disaster management shifts from reactive to proactive strategies.

The study utilized a quasi-experimental research design with a pre-test and post-test one-group approach. The participants consisted of 85 school disaster coordinators in San Pablo City, Laguna. Data were collected using a Demographic Profile, the Multidimensional Health Locus of Control Scale (MHLC), and the Health Promoting Lifestyle Profile II (HPLP II). The intervention was a two-day online training program on School Disaster Risk Reduction and Management facilitated by the Philippine Red Cross.

The findings indicated significant changes in the participants' health-related profiles following the training. Regarding health-promoting behaviors, the overall composite score of the HPLP II showed a significant difference between pre-training and post-training levels (p=0.001), suggesting the training was effective in improving the coordinators' health-promoting behaviors.

The results regarding the Multidimensional Health Locus of Control (MHLC) were more nuanced. There was no significant difference in the "internality" locus of control (p=0.749), meaning the training did not significantly alter the participants' belief in their own ability to control their health. However, the training was highly effective in improving the "externality" dimensions. Both "powerful others" and "chance" dimensions of the locus of control showed significant impacts (p=0.000), indicating the training influenced how participants perceived these external factors.

The study concludes that Disaster Risk Reduction Training has a significant positive effect on the health-promoting behaviors of School Disaster Coordinators. While the training does not fundamentally change an individual's internal sense of control over their health, it significantly influences perceptions of external factors and actual health-related lifestyle behaviors.

The researcher suggests that these findings should be used to enhance, redesign, or equip learning programs in disaster risk reduction to better foster disaster resiliency. By understanding that training can improve health-promoting behaviors, educational institutions and disaster management agencies can design curricula that teach both technical disaster skills and promote the personal health and resilience necessary for coordinators to perform their roles effectively during crises.

This thesis, titled "Effects Of Disaster Risk Reduction Training On The Locus Of Control And Health-Promoting Behavior Among School Disaster Coordinators In San Pablo City, Laguna," investigates how specialized training influences the psychological and behavioral health profiles of school disaster coordinators. The study was conducted by Alexis Ray B. Janolino at the University of the Philippines Open University.

The research problem stems from a shift in disaster management paradigms from reactive to proactive strategies, specifically Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRM). The author notes that while disaster management is moving toward proactiveness, there is a need to understand how health promotion and individual psychological factors, such as the locus of control, contribute to this resilience. The study addresses a gap in literature regarding how training affects the specific psychological constructs and health behaviors of those tasked with managing school-based disasters.

The context of the study is centered in San Pablo City, Laguna, specifically targeting School Disaster Coordinators. The researcher identifies that while many studies on work motivation and job performance are conducted in Western or developed countries, there is a lack of research focusing on specialized roles in the Philippine context. The study aims to determine the levels of health locus of control and health-promoting behavior among these coordinators before and after they undergo a specific DRR training program.

The researcher employed a quasi-experimental research design using a pre-test and post-test one-group design. The study population consisted of 85 respondents, the majority of whom were male, married, held bachelor's degrees, and had a monthly income at or below Salary Grade 13. Data were collected using three standardized instruments: a Demographic Profile, the Multidimensional Health Locus of Control Scale (MHLC), and the Health Promoting Lifestyle Profile II (HPLP II). The intervention consisted of a two-day online training program on School Disaster Risk Reduction and Management, facilitated by certified instructors from the Philippine Red Cross.

The findings revealed significant changes in the participants' health-related profiles following the training. Regarding health-promoting behaviors, the p-value for the overall composite score of the HPLP II was 0.001, indicating a significant difference between the pre-training and post-training levels. This suggests that the training was effective in improving the health-promoting behaviors of the coordinators. 

Regarding the Multidimensional Health Locus of Control (MHLC), the results were more nuanced. There was no significant difference in the "internality" locus of control (p=0.749), meaning the training did not significantly alter the participants' belief in their own ability to control their health. However, the training was highly effective in improving the "externality" dimensions of the locus of control. Both "powerful others" LOC and "chance" LOC showed p-values of 0.000, indicating that the training significantly impacted how participants perceived these external factors.

The study concludes that Disaster Risk Reduction Training has a significant positive effect on the health-promoting behaviors of School Disaster Coordinators. While the training does not fundamentally change an individual's internal sense of control over their health, it significantly influences their perceptions of external factors (powerful others and chance) and their actual health-related lifestyle behaviors.

The implications of this research are significant for the development of disaster management programs. The author suggests that these findings should be used to enhance, redesign, or equip learning programs in disaster risk reduction to better foster disaster resiliency. By understanding that training can improve health-promoting behaviors, educational institutions and disaster management agencies can better design curricula that not only teach technical disaster skills but also promote the personal health and resilience necessary for coordinators to perform their roles effectively during crises.

title: Caregiver Burden and Social Support Among Family Members of Stroke Survivors: A Community-Based Study in Sampaloc Manila, Philippines
abstract: Background: The objective of the study is to determine the family caregivers' level of caregiver burden, perceived level of social support, and the relationship between degree of burden and the perceived level of social support among the family members of stroke survivors. Another purpose of this study is to assess any association these variables have with patient's severity of illness, patient's age, caregiver's age, caregiver's gender, and caregiver's relationship to the patient. Methods: A total of eighty-two (82) respondents participated in the study, 63 among them are females, and the remaining 19 are males. They are Filipino family caregivers of stroke survivors living among eight (8) Barangays in Zone 41, Sampaloc City, Manila. Participants were interviewed via phone by a single Registered Nurse Research Assistant. The patient's stroke severity was determined using the Modified Rankin Scale. Participants' degree of Caregiver burden was assessed using the 22-question Zarit Burden Interview Scale, while their perceived level of Social Support including its subscales were assessed using the Medical Outcome Study Social Support Survey. Both Caregivers and Stroke survivors' sociodemographic details were taken. Results: The study revealed the negative correlation between caregiver burden to their perceived level of social support and to their degree relationship with the stroke survivors, which reflects that the closer the relationship between the caregiver and stroke survivor, the greater the burden experienced by the family caregivers. A positive relationship between the Caregiver burden and the caregiver's age was also shown, which suggests that the level of burden increases as the caregivers' age increase. Additionally, the study has also seen a negative relationship between the level of perceived social support and its subscales to the caregiver's age and suggests that as the age of caregivers increase the lesser the level of social support they perceived. Conclusion: During the Global Pandemic, Filipino family caregiver participants still reported to perceive good level of social support. However, despite the negative relationship good social support has with the degree of burden, significant number of family caregivers still verbalize experience of mild to severe degree of burden. Caregiver burden is truly multifaceted and was shown to be correlated with multiple factors.

half:
The study "Caregiver Burden and Social Support Among Family Members of Stroke Survivors: A Community-Based Study in Sampaloc, Manila, Philippines" investigates the psychosocial challenges faced by family caregivers. Because stroke often occurs abruptly, family members are frequently unprepared for the sudden transition into caregiving roles. In the Philippines, this burden is compounded by a private healthcare system that imposes financial strain on lower and middle-income families. The research addresses the lack of direct research in developing countries regarding how social support affects the caregiver's experience of burden, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Using a descriptive research design, the study surveyed eighty-two Filipino family caregivers in eight barangays in Sampaloc, Manila. Data collection was conducted via telephone interviews. The researcher utilized the Modified Rankin Scale to determine stroke severity, the Zarit Burden Interview Scale to measure caregiver burden, and the Medical Outcomes Study Social Support Survey to assess perceived social support.

Findings revealed a negative correlation between caregiver burden and perceived social support, indicating higher support is associated with lower burden. A negative correlation was also found between caregiver burden and the degree of relationship with the stroke survivor, suggesting caregivers with closer relationships experience greater burden. Regarding demographics, a positive relationship was identified between caregiver burden and the caregiver's age, while a negative relationship was found between age and perceived social support.

The study concluded that despite the pandemic, Filipino family caregivers perceived a good level of social support, yet many reported mild to severe degrees of burden. The researcher concluded that caregiver burden is a multifaceted phenomenon correlated with multiple demographic and clinical factors. Implications include the need for healthcare professionals to develop intervention strategies, for nursing education to provide training in mental and emotional support, and for community health officers to prioritize high-risk caregivers for targeted programs. Ultimately, the study emphasizes recognizing family caregivers as active members of the healthcare team.

The study titled "Caregiver Burden and Social Support Among Family Members of Stroke Survivors: A Community-Based Study in Sampaloc, Manila, Philippines" investigates the psychosocial challenges faced by family caregivers of stroke survivors. The research focuses on determining the levels of caregiver burden and perceived social support, and exploring the relationships between these variables and various demographic and clinical factors.

The problem addressed is the significant psychosocial and financial strain placed on family members who provide care for stroke survivors. Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability globally and in the Philippines. Because stroke often occurs abruptly, family members are frequently unprepared for the sudden transition into caregiving roles. In the Philippine context, this burden is compounded by a private healthcare system that imposes financial strain on lower and middle-income families. Furthermore, the study notes that while social support is known to ease the negative experiences of survivors, there is a lack of direct research in developing countries like the Philippines comparing how social support specifically affects the caregiver's experience of burden, particularly during the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic.

The research was conducted in Sampaloc, Manila, specifically across eight barangays in Zone 41. The study utilized a descriptive research design. The participants consisted of eighty-two Filipino family caregivers, of whom 63 were female and 19 were male. Data collection was performed via telephone interviews by a Registered Nurse Research Assistant to accommodate the limitations of the COVID-19 pandemic. To assess the variables, the researcher used the Modified Rankin Scale to determine the severity of the patient's stroke, the Zarit Burden Interview Scale to measure the degree of caregiver burden, and the Medical Outcomes Study Social Support Survey (MOSSS) to assess perceived social support across its subscales: emotional, concrete, loving, and positive interaction.

The findings revealed several significant correlations. There was a negative correlation between caregiver burden and the perceived level of social support, indicating that higher social support is associated with lower burden. Additionally, a negative correlation was found between caregiver burden and the degree of relationship with the stroke survivor, suggesting that caregivers with closer relationships to the patient experience greater burden. Regarding demographic factors, a positive relationship was identified between caregiver burden and the caregiver's age, meaning burden increases as the caregiver gets older. Conversely, a negative relationship was found between the caregiver's age and their perceived level of social support, suggesting that older caregivers perceive less social support.

The study concluded that despite the global pandemic, Filipino family caregivers still perceived a good level of social support. However, even with this support, a significant number of caregivers reported experiencing mild to severe degrees of burden. The researcher concluded that caregiver burden is a multifaceted phenomenon that is correlated with multiple demographic and clinical factors.

The implications of this study are significant for various sectors. For nursing practice, it serves as an eye-opener regarding the psychosocial concerns of families, highlighting the need for healthcare professionals to develop effective intervention strategies and health teachings to support families during the transition to caregiving. In nursing education, the findings suggest a need for training and seminars to equip nurses with the skills to provide mental and emotional support to families in distress. For community health officers, the study provides an objective reference to identify and prioritize caregivers at high risk of burden, allowing for the implementation of targeted community health programs. Ultimately, the study emphasizes the importance of recognizing family caregivers as active members of the healthcare team who facilitate the recovery and growth of stroke survivors.

title: The Effect of Experiential Ageing Simulation on the Attitudes Toward Older People Among Senior Nursing Students
abstract: Considering the Philippines' aging population, positive attitudes toward older people and senior sensitivity are essential for nurses. However, international studies showed that nursing students have unfavorable attitudes toward older people. Little is known about this in the Philippine setting. This study aims to determine the effect of experiential ageing simulation on the attitudes (on the Responding level of Bloom's Affective taxonomy) toward older people among 4th-year nursing students in a Philippine setting; and to determine if age, sex, and experience in elderly care are factors affecting their attitudes. Quasi-Experimental, One-group Pretest-Posttest design was utilized for this study on 51 graduating nursing students. The students attended a 4-hour ageing simulation seminar workshop that provided knowledge and firsthand experience on common challenges of older people through wearing sensory simulators that mimic age-related changes. Before and after the intervention, the students accomplished Kogan's Attitudes Toward Older People (KATOP) Scale and Work Preference Ranking Form. The data were analyzed using paired t-test, independent t-test, and one-way ANOVA using Jamovi 2.2 software. The results revealed a significant difference in the attitudes toward older people of nursing students before and after the intervention (p-value <0.001 and a Cohen's d of 0.978). Additionally, the results of work preference ranking showed an extreme shift in their preference for elderly care after the intervention. It was also determined that age, sex, and experience in elderly care are not significant factors in the students' attitudes. Based on these, experiential ageing simulation has improved the attitudes toward older people of graduating nursing students. Adopting experiential ageing simulation in schools and other institutions may help prepare students to be more senior-sensitive in facing the country's aging population.

half:
Vladimir Milaor’s research investigates how experiential ageing simulation impacts the attitudes of senior nursing students toward older people. Set against the backdrop of a rapidly aging population in the Philippines, the study addresses the problem of unfavorable attitudes, stereotypes, and inaccurate perceptions among nursing students, which can compromise the quality of geriatric nursing care.

The study employed a quasi-experimental, one-group pretest-posttest design involving 51 graduating Bachelor of Science in Nursing students from a public university in Marikina City. The intervention consisted of a four-hour "Senior Sensitivity Training Workshop" utilizing sensory simulators, such as glasses mimicking cataracts or glaucoma, earplugs for hearing loss, and walking on raw corn kernels to simulate peripheral neuropathy. Data were collected using Kogan’s Attitudes Toward Older People (KATOP) Scale and a Work Preference Ranking Form.

Findings revealed a significant improvement in students' attitudes following the intervention, with a significant difference between pretest and posttest scores and a large effect size. Work preference rankings indicated an extreme shift in preference for elderly care after the simulation. Demographic variables, including age, sex, and previous experience in elderly care, were not significant factors in determining attitudes. The researcher concludes that experiential ageing simulation is an effective tool for bridging the gap between theory and practice, mitigating negative stereotypes, and increasing sensitivity to functional declines.

The research conducted by Vladimir Milaor investigates the impact of experiential ageing simulation on the attitudes of senior nursing students toward older people. This study is situated within the context of a rapidly aging population in the Philippines, where older adults (aged 60 and above) are projected to comprise an increasing percentage of the total population. As the demand for geriatric nursing services grows, the researcher identifies a critical need for nurses who possess positive attitudes and high sensitivity toward the unique physiological, anatomical, and psychosocial needs of the elderly.

The problem addressed by this study is the prevalence of unfavorable attitudes, stereotypes, and inaccurate perceptions regarding older adults among nursing students. International literature suggests that many students view geriatric nursing as a less desirable career path due to the perceived intensity of care required and communication challenges. In the Philippine context, while respect for elders is a cultural cornerstone, ageism and misconceptions regarding the aging process still persist. The researcher notes that negative attitudes can directly compromise the quality of nursing care, making it essential to explore educational interventions that can foster empathy and understanding.

The study utilized a quasi-experimental, one-group pretest-posttest research design. The participants were 51 graduating (4th-year) Bachelor of Science in Nursing students from a public university in Marikina City. The intervention consisted of a four-hour "Senior Sensitivity Training Workshop" or experiential ageing simulation. This workshop provided students with firsthand experience of age-related changes through the use of sensory simulators, such as glasses that mimic cataracts or glaucoma, earplugs to simulate presbycusis (hearing loss), and walking on raw corn kernels to simulate peripheral neuropathy. Data were collected using Kogan’s Attitudes Toward Older People (KATOP) Scale to measure attitudes at the "responding" level of Bloom’s Affective Taxonomy, and a Work Preference Ranking Form was used to assess career interests. The data were analyzed using paired t-tests, independent t-tests, and one-way ANOVA.

The findings of the study revealed a significant improvement in the attitudes of nursing students toward older people following the intervention. Specifically, there was a significant difference between the pretest and posttest scores (p < 0.001) with a large effect size (Cohen’s d of 0.978). Furthermore, the results of the work preference ranking indicated an extreme shift in the students' preference for elderly care after participating in the simulation. Interestingly, the study determined that demographic variables—specifically age, sex, and previous experience in elderly care—were not significant factors in determining the students' attitudes.

The researcher concludes that experiential ageing simulation is an effective tool for improving the attitudes of graduating nursing students toward older adults. By allowing students to "step into the shoes" of the elderly, the simulation provides a meaningful learning experience that bridges the gap between theoretical knowledge and the lived reality of aging. The study confirms that such experiential methods can successfully mitigate negative stereotypes and increase sensitivity to the functional declines associated with aging.

The implications of this research are significant for nursing education and practice. For nursing educational institutions, the study suggests that adopting experiential ageing simulations can help prepare future nurses for the realities of an aging population, ensuring they enter the workforce with the necessary empathy and sensitivity. For the nursing profession, fostering these positive attitudes is vital for improving the quality of geriatric care and addressing the growing demand for specialized nursing services. Finally, the study provides a foundation for health institutions and private organizations to implement similar sensitivity training for staff to enhance the delivery of care to senior citizens.

title: Perceived Managerial Support And Practice Environment Among Nurses In A Selected Tertiary Hospital In Metro Manila, Philippines
abstract:
Managerial support in professional nursing practice is crucial in establishing and maintaining a healthy practice environment. It is believed that these variables play an important role in staff retention, job satisfaction, and turnover rates. This academic work determined the perceived managerial support, practice environment and its relation to staff nurse's demographic profile employed in a selected level 4 government-owned and controlled corporate tertiary healthcare facility located in Metro Manila, Philippines. 

The study used a descriptive correlational design and facilitated two international validated research instruments, namely Supervisory support scale (SSS) tool, and American Association of Critical-care Nursing Healthy Work Environment Assessment Tool (AACN-HWEAT). Pearson correlation coefficient was used to identify the relationship of perceived level managerial support and nurse-respondents' practice environment. The Chi-square test of independence was facilitated to identify the difference between practice environment and demographic profile of nurse-respondents. 

Data gathered from nurse-respondents (N = 519) showed a high level of perceived managerial support and positive practice environments. However, results highlighted that only one of the six healthy work environment essential standards, namely the true collaboration, scored the lowest mean value, ( M = 1.92 ; SD = 0.32 ) depicting a negative practice environment. While the SSS domains mostly show significant correlations on HWE essential standards, the effective decision-making essential standard found no significant correlation with SSS being reliable domain, r(517) = 0.063 p > 0.152 whereas the authentic leadership essential standard showed non-significant relationship with both SSS domains, namely respects uniqueness, r(517) = 0.005 p>.990; and being reliable, r(517) = - 0.054 p>.220. Also, study findings showed a significant association between practice environment essential standards and staff nurse's demographic profile, p < 0.0001. 

Nurse practice environment should be a priority for healthcare leaders and administrators because it is evidently a critical factor in the provision of quality patient care, organizational success, as well as in the improvement of the overall professional nursing practice.
faculty: Faculty of Management and Development Studies
half:
Simon Paul P. Navarro’s thesis investigates the relationship between perceived managerial support and the quality of the professional practice environment among nurses at a tertiary hospital in Metro Manila, Philippines. The study is framed by the global nursing crisis, characterized by workforce shortages and burnout, and specifically addresses the projected deficit of 250,000 nurses in the Philippines by 2030.

Utilizing a descriptive correlational research design, the researcher surveyed 519 bedside nurses through complete enumeration sampling. Data were collected using the Supervisory Support Scale (SSS) and the American Association of Critical-care Nursing Healthy Work Environment Assessment Tool (AACN-HWEAT). Statistical analysis was conducted using the Pearson correlation coefficient and the Chi-square test of independence.

The findings indicate that nurses report high levels of perceived managerial support and a generally positive practice environment. However, "true collaboration" received the lowest mean value, signaling a negative environment in that specific domain. While most SSS domains correlated significantly with AACN-HWE essential standards, "effective decision-making" did not correlate with "being reliable," and "authentic leadership" showed no significant relationship with "respects uniqueness" or "being reliable." Additionally, a significant association was found between practice environment standards and the respondents' demographic profiles. The study concludes that healthcare leaders should prioritize collaborative practices to improve patient care and suggests that policymakers implement strategic interventions to address nursing shortages and migration.
one:
Simon Paul P. Navarro’s thesis, "Perceived Managerial Support and Practice Environment Among Nurses In A Selected Tertiary Hospital In Metro Manila, Philippines," investigates the relationship between how nurses perceive managerial support and the quality of their professional practice environment. The study is framed by a global nursing crisis involving workforce shortages, high turnover, and burnout, which was intensified by the COVID-19 pandemic. In the Philippines, a projected deficit of 250,000 nurses by 2030 necessitates strategies for professional retention. The researcher notes that nursing managers are pivotal in this context, as their leadership styles influence job satisfaction and stress levels, yet there is a lack of local research examining the intersection of managerial support and the practice environment in the Philippines.

The study utilized a descriptive correlational research design at a level four government-owned and controlled corporate tertiary healthcare facility in Metro Manila. Using a complete enumeration sampling technique, the researcher surveyed 519 nurses providing direct bedside patient care who had been employed for at least six months. Data were collected via two validated instruments: the Supervisory Support Scale (SSS), which measures domains such as being reliable and respecting uniqueness, and the American Association of Critical-care Nursing Healthy Work Environment Assessment Tool (AACN-HWEAT), which assesses skilled communication, true collaboration, effective decision-making, appropriate staffing, meaningful recognition, and authentic leadership. Statistical analysis involved the Pearson correlation coefficient and the Chi-square test of independence.

The findings revealed that nurses reported high levels of perceived managerial support and a generally positive practice environment. However, "true collaboration" received the lowest mean value, indicating a negative practice environment in that specific domain. While most SSS domains showed significant relationships with the AACN-HWE essential standards, two non-significant relationships were identified: "effective decision-making" did not correlate with "being reliable," and "authentic leadership" showed no significant relationship with either "respects uniqueness" or "being reliable." The thesis titled "Perceived Managerial Support and Practice Environment Among Nurses In A Selected Tertiary Hospital In Metro Manila, Philippines" by Simon Paul P. Navarro investigates the relationship between how nurses perceive the support they receive from management and the quality of their professional practice environment.

**Problem and Context**
The study is situated within a global and local nursing crisis characterized by significant workforce shortages, high turnover rates, and burnout. The author notes that the COVID-19 pandemic exacerbated these issues, revealing poor working conditions and critical staffing deficiencies. In the Philippines, a projected deficit of 250,000 nurses by 2030 creates an urgent need for strategies to retain professionals. The researcher identifies that nursing managers are pivotal in this context, as their leadership styles directly influence job satisfaction, stress levels, and the overall practice environment. Despite the known importance of these variables, the author highlights a lack of local research in the Philippines that specifically examines the intersection of perceived managerial support and the practice environment within both public and private healthcare settings.

**Methodology**
The study employed a descriptive correlational research design to examine the relationships between the identified variables. The research was conducted at a level four government-owned and controlled corporate (GOCC) tertiary healthcare facility in Metro Manila, Philippines. The researcher utilized a total population or complete enumeration sampling technique, involving 519 nurse-respondents who were providing direct bedside patient care and had been employed for at least six months. Nurses in administrative roles were excluded from the study.

Data were collected using two internationally validated instruments: the Supervisory Support Scale (SSS), which measures domains such as respecting uniqueness and being reliable, and the American Association of Critical-care Nursing Healthy Work Environment Assessment Tool (AACN-HWEAT), which assesses six essential standards: skilled communication, true collaboration, effective decision-making, appropriate staffing, meaningful recognition, and authentic leadership. Statistical analysis included the Pearson correlation coefficient to determine the relationship between managerial support and the practice environment, and the Chi-square test of independence to identify associations between the practice environment and the nurses' demographic profiles.

**Findings**
The results indicated that nurses reported a high level of perceived managerial support and a generally positive practice environment. However, a specific deficiency was identified regarding "true collaboration," which received the lowest mean value (M=1.92; SD=0.32), indicating a negative practice environment in that specific domain.

Regarding the correlations, most SSS domains showed significant relationships with the AACN-HWE essential standards. However, two notable non-significant relationships were found: the "effective decision-making" standard showed no significant correlation with the "being reliable" domain, and "authentic leadership" showed no significant relationship with either the "respects uniqueness" or "being reliable" domains. Additionally, the study found a significant association between the practice environment essential standards and the demographic profiles of the nurse-respondents.

**Conclusions and Implications**
The study concludes that while managerial support is perceived highly, there are specific gaps in the practice environment, particularly concerning collaboration. The findings reinforce the idea that managerial support and the practice environment are critical factors in the professional lives of nurses.

The implications of this research are significant for several stakeholders. For healthcare leaders and administrators, the study suggests that prioritizing the practice environment is essential for ensuring quality patient care and organizational success. Specifically, interventions should target the improvement of collaborative practices. For policymakers and the government, the findings underscore the need for strategic interventions and retention programs to address the nursing shortage and the trend of international migration. Ultimately, the study serves as a foundation for future research aimed at developing evidence-based strategies to foster supportive work cultures and improve the overall professional nursing practice in the Philippines.

title: Work Motivation, Satisfaction, and Performance Among Nurses in Expanded Roles in a Magnet-Recognized Hospital in the Middle East
abstract:
Research studies about Nurses and their work motivation, satisfaction and performance were limited to those working at bedside or those in conventional nursing leadership. This situation left Nurses on expanded roles unheard and underrepresented. Moreover, these correlational studies were usually completed in the West which created an imbalance and possible misrepresentation of Nurses in other geographic location such as the Middle East. This rapid expansion of nursing roles is part of a new era which is supposed to give nursing profession a more unique identity. However, due to lack of attention and study, this may instead lead to some role confusion or conflict or worse to work demotivation, dissatisfaction and poor performance.

The study used a non-experimental, quantitative descriptive correlational research design. Three validated questionnaires such as Work Extrinsic and Intrinsic Motivation Scale (WEIMS), Index of Work Satisfaction (IWS) and the Six Dimension Scale of Nursing Performance (6-D Scale) were distributed to nurses to determine their level of work motivation, satisfaction, and performance. An analytical software tool SPSS was used to calculate Pearson r on a one-tailed test. Furthermore, mean scores and standard deviation per domain were also computed and interpreted.

Nurses in this study revealed a self-determined profile with a high W-SDI of 7.91 and IWS score of 193.7. Their satisfaction index of 13.53 is also higher than the median index of all collated studies which utilized the same questionnaire in the past. Furthermore, intrinsic motivation turned out to be their topmost source of work motivation hence staff engagement and retention programs can be based on this and other dimensions measured in this study. There is also significant evidence to demonstrate a positive linear correlation between work satisfaction and teaching & collaboration (.267) and professional development (.267) which are subscales of work performance. There is also enough evidence to prove that work motivation and leadership (.205), critical care (.252) and planning & evaluation (.219) which are subscales of work performance have a positive linear relationship. Lastly, there is significant evidence to conclude that work satisfaction and work motivation have a significant relationship (.372).

Maintaining staff turnover rate low can be critical to success of any healthcare organization. This study can help provide a better understanding on how Nurses on expanded roles can stay motivated and satisfied to relentlessly give their top performance in their respective subgroup and work environment. The results are also culturally and geographically sensitive and specific to the Middle East.

Several studies supported the impression that highly motivated and satisfied Nurses contributed to improved patient satisfaction and clinical outcomes. Hence, creating the right platform to leverage their skills and get them satisfied could be advantageous to patients and the organization. In addition, this study may perhaps bring an increase in public awareness about the robust expansion of nursing profession through vast diversification of roles which could further shape the profession’s unique identity and help establish a more independent practice in the future.

title: Emotional Intelligence and Psychological Well-Being Among Nurses in A Psychiatric Hospital in Kuwait
abstract:
Emotional intelligence is the ability of an individual to recognize his or her own feelings, rationalize among those feelings as well as incorporate such feelings into thinking and actions. Psychological well-being is recognized as the capability to actively participate in work and to create important relationships with others, and to establish positive emotions. In today’s practice, patients’ care is not only confined to the physical ailment but also to the psychological and emotional needs of the patients, hence, the role of emotional intelligence and psychological well-being must be taken seriously, as nurses are confronted not only by the patients’ emotions but also by their own.

This study aims to gain insight into the level of emotional intelligence and psychological well-being among nurses in a psychiatric hospital in Kuwait and to determine the significant relationship between the levels of emotional intelligence, psychological well-being and the profile of mental health nurses focusing on the field of caring.

Quantitative non-experimental descriptive correlational design was used, and the standardized questionnaires namely: Schutte Self-Report Emotional Test (SSRET) and Psychological Well-being Scale (PWBS) were used to gather data from 150 respondents. Results shows most of the surveyed respondents are male (58.7%), belongs to generation Y (23 – 38 years old) or the millennial age (65.3%). Mostly are married (90%), obtained a baccalaureate degree in nursing (74.7%). Majority are Indian national (66%) having 1 – 5 years of work experience (30%).

Pearson Product-Moment Correlation and chi square test were used to analyze the data. The results showed a high level of emotional intelligence of mental health nurses’ and low score in almost all the subscale of PWB with a low overall mean score of 141.40 (SD = 20.80). The correlation results also showed that there is no significant positive correlation between emotional intelligence and psychological well-being. Further, the result of the chi-squared test showed that there is no statistically significant correlation between demographic profile and psychological well-being and emotional intelligence of mental health nurses in Kuwait.

title: Perceived Leader Empowering Behaviors and Work Engagement of Staff Nurses in A Tertiary Hospital in the United Kingdom
abstract:
The empowering behavior of nursing leaders is a key factor in improving staff nurses’ work engagement. Empowering nurses to use their knowledge by recognizing their skills, supporting their career advancement, and allowing them to have control over their work improves organizational commitment, positive patient outcomes and job satisfaction, thereby increasing trust and engagement in the organization.

The purpose of this descriptive correlational study conducted at a tertiary hospital under the United Kingdom National Health Service (NHS) Trust is to describe leader empowering behavior (LEB) as perceived by staff nurses and their work engagement. This study also aims to examine the relationship of work engagement with leader empowering behavior and selected demographic profile. Sample from various units of the hospital was employed (N-100) and survey was completed online.

Overall, nurses have moderate to strong perception for the dimensions Accountability (μ=6.11), Information Sharing (μ=5.52) which means that they are given adequate information and are aware of their liability of their duties. Other LEB dimensions such as Delegation of Authority (μ=5.03), Self-Directed Decision Making (μ=5.28), Skill Development (μ=4.93), and Coaching for Innovative Performance (μ=4.65) have moderate perception among nurses. Nurses in this organization were also found to have moderate to strong work engagement, Vigor (μ=3.97), Dedication (μ=4.80), and Absorption (μ=4.50), with the overall work engagement mean (μ=4.42).

Using Pearson’s correlation test, a moderate to strong uphill linear relationship was established between LEB and the Work Engagement Subscales of vigor, dedication and absorption which demonstrates that there is a significant relationship between them.

Meanwhile, the Chi-square test was used to determine the relationship between LEB and selected Demographic Profile. At 5% level of significance, there is insufficient evidence to conclude that age, gender, years of service, and civil status of nurses have significant relationship with the work engagement subscales except level of education. The results revealed that the nurses’ level of education have a significant effect on the increase or decrease of their vigor or the amount of physical, cognitive, and emotional energy they give on their job. Conclusions and recommendations were sought on how the results of the study can be used to improve the NHS retention scheme based on analysis of the data collected.

Regarding work engagement, the nurses demonstrated moderate to strong levels across the subscales of vigor, dedication, and absorption, with an overall mean score of 4.42.

Statistical analysis using Pearson’s r-test established a significant, moderate to strong uphill linear relationship between perceived leader empowering behaviors and the work engagement subscales of vigor, dedication, and absorption. This indicates that as empowering behaviors from leaders increase, so does the work engagement of the staff nurses. Furthermore, a Chi-square test was used to examine the relationship between work engagement and the demographic profile of the nurses. The results showed that most demographic variables, such as age, gender, years of service, and civil status, did not have a significant relationship with work engagement subscales. However, the level of education was found to have a significant effect on the increase or decrease of vigor, which refers to the physical, cognitive, and emotional energy nurses invest in their jobs.

The study concludes that leader empowering behaviors are significantly related to the work engagement of staff nurses. The results suggest that when leaders provide autonomy, share information, and support skill development, nurses feel more engaged in their roles. The findings also highlight that educational background plays a role in how nurses experience vigor in their work.

The implications of this study suggest that the NHS can improve its retention schemes by focusing on the empowerment behaviors of nurse leaders. By fostering an environment of accountability, information sharing, and autonomy, organizations can boost work engagement, which may lead to higher job satisfaction and a stronger intent to stay within the organization. Improving these leadership practices could ultimately reduce the financial burden of recruitment and training while ensuring the delivery of safe, high-quality patient care through a more committed and experienced nursing workforce.

title: Quality of Prenatal Care and Maternal Fetal Attachment Among Primagravida Mothers in Occidental Mindoro, Philippines
abstract:
The prenatal period is a proper chance for evaluating maternal-fetal attachment. By determining maternal fetal attachment during pregnancy, in time intervention and education could be planned for improving these interactions and consequently improve the mother-child attachment before the childbirth. Considering the importance of maternal attachment to the developing baby and various factors that may affect this matter there is still lack of necessary information in this regard in our country. 

The study determined the relationship between quality of prenatal care and maternal-fetal attachment among primigravidamothers during late pregnancy period. 

The study conducted a survey using a 46-item Quality of Prenatal Care Questionnaire (QPCQ) and 24-item Maternal-Fetal Attachment Scale among 343 primigravid mothers in different barangay health stations and prenatal care clinics. Pearson correlation was used to determine the correlation between maternal-fetal attachment scores and quality of prenatal scores. Beta coefficient and its corresponding 95% confidence intervals were computed using linear regression. 

The overall quality of prenatal care and maternal-fetal attachment of the primigravid women in the study setting is high. The quality of prenatal care is correlated significantly withmaternal-fetal attachment. Itmeans that the maternal-fetal attachment will be high if the pregnant mother had a high quality of prenatal care. Moreover, the following age, social support and education level were significantly associated with maternal fetal attachment.

Gonzales, Jr. investigated the relationship between perceived quality of prenatal care and maternal-fetal attachment among 343 primigravida mothers in the SAMARICA district of Occidental Mindoro, Philippines. Using a descriptive cross-sectional correlational design, the study utilized the Quality of Prenatal Care Questionnaire (QPCQ) and the Maternal-Fetal Attachment Scale (MFAS) to assess six domains of care and five dimensions of attachment.

The findings revealed that both the overall quality of prenatal care and the level of maternal-fetal attachment were high. Within the care domains, information sharing, anticipatory guidance, and sufficient time received the highest mean scores, while approachability, availability, and support and respect received slightly lower scores. A significant correlation was found between the quality of prenatal care and maternal-fetal attachment, indicating that higher quality care is associated with higher attachment levels. Additionally, maternal age, social support, and educational attainment were significantly associated with maternal-fetal attachment.

The study concludes that the quality of the prenatal care experience is a significant predictor of the bond a mother forms with her fetus. The researcher suggests that healthcare providers should adopt a holistic approach prioritizing the psychological and emotional needs of first-time mothers. Improving interpersonal communication, consultation time, and respect can enhance care quality. It is recommended that government health programs incorporate interventions designed to support maternal-fetal attachment and maternal role attainment.

The thesis titled "Quality of Prenatal Care and Maternal Fetal Attachment Among Primigravida Mothers in Occidental Mindoro, Philippines," authored by Artemio M. Gonzales, Jr., investigates the relationship between the perceived quality of prenatal care and the level of maternal-fetal attachment among first-time pregnant women.

The research problem stems from the critical importance of the prenatal period in establishing the maternal-fetal bond, which influences the transition to motherhood and the psychological well-being of the mother. While the World Health Organization emphasizes the need for a positive pregnancy experience, the author notes a lack of specific information in the Philippine context regarding how the quality of healthcare services impacts the emotional and psychological connection between a mother and her unborn child. Specifically, the study addresses the gap in understanding how various domains of prenatal care—such as information sharing, support, and respect—correlate with the attachment levels of primigravida mothers.

The study was conducted in the SAMARICA district of Occidental Mindoro, Philippines, specifically within the municipalities of San Jose, Magsaysay, Rizal, and Calintaan. The researcher utilized a descriptive cross-sectional research design with a correlational approach. The study population consisted of 343 primigravida mothers in their third trimester who had at least two previous prenatal visits. A cluster sampling method was employed to select participants from various barangay health stations and rural health units. Data were collected through structured interviews using two primary instruments: the 46-item Quality of Prenatal Care Questionnaire (QPCQ) and the 24-item Maternal-Fetal Attachment Scale (MFAS). The QPCQ assessed six domains: information sharing, anticipatory guidance, sufficient time, approachability, availability, and support and respect. The MFAS measured dimensions including future parental role-taking, differentiation of self from the fetus, interaction with the fetus, attributing characteristics to the fetus, and giving of self. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation to determine relationships between variables, and linear regression to compute beta coefficients.

The findings revealed that the overall quality of prenatal care and the level of maternal-fetal attachment among the respondents were high. Specifically, the mean score for the quality of prenatal care was 4.00 ± 0.26. Within the quality of care domains, information sharing, anticipatory guidance, and sufficient time received higher mean scores (above 4.00), while approachability, availability, and support and respect received slightly lower mean scores (below 4.00). Regarding demographic characteristics, the majority of respondents were aged 20–24, high school or college graduates, lived in households with more than five members, and had a partner accompanying them during prenatal visits.

A significant correlation was found between the quality of prenatal care and maternal-fetal attachment, indicating that higher quality prenatal care is associated with higher levels of maternal-fetal attachment. Furthermore, the study identified that maternal age, social support, and educational attainment were significantly associated with maternal-fetal attachment.

The study concludes that the quality of the prenatal care experience is a significant predictor of the bond a mother forms with her fetus. High-quality care, characterized by effective information sharing and guidance, facilitates a stronger maternal-fetal attachment. Additionally, demographic factors such as age, education, and the presence of social support play crucial roles in shaping this attachment.

The implications of these findings suggest that healthcare providers, particularly nurses and midwives in community health settings, should adopt a holistic approach to prenatal care. Beyond physical health monitoring, there is a need to prioritize the psychological and emotional needs of primigravida mothers. Improving interpersonal communication, ensuring sufficient time for consultations, and fostering a respectful environment can enhance the quality of care and, consequently, strengthen the maternal-fetal bond. The researcher recommends that government health programs and maternal health services incorporate interventions designed to support maternal-fetal attachment and maternal role attainment to improve long-term maternal and infant health outcomes.

title: Vital Exhaustion and Psychosocial Health Among Offshore Personnel Working in the Philippines
abstract: The offshore environment is a high-risk and demanding workplace exposing crew members to various physical and psychological stressors. Health and safety programs are implemented to prevent accidents and promote well-being among personnel. This study aims to determine the association between vital exhaustion and psychosocial health among offshore workers in the Philippines. Quantitative non experimental descriptive correlational design was used. Standardized questionnaires namely: Maastricht Vital Exhaustion (MVEQ) and Copenhagen Psychosocial Questionnaires (COPSOQ III) were utilized to gather data from fifty-five (55) respondents. The majority of the participants were male, belong to late middle adult age group (41-60 years old), completed a bachelor’s degree, were assigned in the maintenance and marine departments and have been working for 11-35 years offshore. Offshore workers have low vital exhaustion (VE) levels (M= 5.25, SD= 6.66) and good psychosocial health (PH) scores. Highest recorded scores fall under Influence and Development (M= 76.16, SD= 16.61), Outcome Scales (M= 75.68, SD= 17.58) and Interpersonal relations and leadership (M= 68.08, SD= 11.35). Lower mean scores in Further Parameters (M= 47.27, SD= 24.73) and Demands at Work (M= 40.9, SD= 14.15) also translate to favorable PH. There was a significant relationship among four (4) psychosocial health scales (p-value at .05), Demands at Work (< .001), Interpersonal relations and leadership (.001), Further Parameters (.001) and Outcome Scales (< .001), and the level of VE of offshore workers. There was also a significant relationship between VE (p-value at .05) and the demographic profile of offshore workers in terms of job assignment (.020) and work type (.002) however there was no significant association between PH and all demographic variables considered in the study. Majority of the respondents also claimed that environmental conditions were well-designed (M= 78.18, SD= 26.81) and safety concerns (M= 82.72, SD= 26.3) were managed appropriately in the workplace.

The offshore environment is a high-risk, isolated workplace where personnel face stressors like extreme weather and long hours. This research investigated the association between vital exhaustion (VE)—a state of fatigue, hopelessness, and irritability—and psychosocial health (PH) among offshore workers in the Philippines. Using a quantitative non-experimental descriptive correlational design, data were collected from fifty-five respondents working on natural gas field platforms and shipping vessels off Palawan Island. The study utilized the Maastricht Vital Exhaustion Questionnaire and the Copenhagen Psychosocial Questionnaire, grounded in Myra Levine’s Conservation Model.

Findings revealed that most participants were males aged 41-60 with bachelor's degrees, working in maintenance or marine departments with 11 to 35 years of experience. Respondents exhibited low levels of vital exhaustion and generally good psychosocial health, particularly in areas of influence, development, outcome scales, and interpersonal relations. A significant relationship was found between VE and four psychosocial health scales: demands at work, interpersonal relations and leadership, further parameters, and outcome scales. Additionally, VE showed a significant relationship with job assignment and work type, though no significant association was found between PH and the demographic variables studied.

The study concludes that while current levels of VE and PH are favorable, a significant link exists suggesting that as exhaustion increases, psychosocial health may decline. These findings can assist safety managers in developing interventions to prevent mental health issues and cardiovascular disease.
